title: 嘉靖四年江西鄉試錄
text:
江西鄉試錄序
嘉靖乙酉秋八月玆維大比先
是江西廵按監察御史秦〔鉞〕〔颸〕
言曰玆役也臣子效忠之道莫
急矣庸敢不預迺以謀于鎮守
太監崔〔和〕廵撫右副都御史陳
〔洪〕〔謨〕提督南贛軍務右副都御
===
史聶〔賢〕清戎監察御史陶〔儼〕則
謀于左右布政使蔣〔瑶〕嚴〔紘〕及
其左右叅政王〔大〕〔用〕馮〔馴〕左叅
議陳〔塀〕陸〔溥〕則謀于按察使丁
〔沂〕及其副使顧〔應〕〔祥〕周〔廣〕范〔輅〕
林〔大〕〔輅〕查〔約〕謝〔廸〕僉事徐〔乾〕魯
〔綸〕汪〔應〕〔軫〕高〔賁〕〔亨〕張〔□〕〔□〕而後□
punctuated:
江西鄉試錄序

嘉靖乙酉秋八月，玆維大比。先是，江西廵按監察御史秦〔鉞〕〔颸〕言曰：「玆役也，臣子效忠之道莫急矣，庸敢不預？」迺以謀于鎮守太監崔〔和〕、廵撫右副都御史陳〔洪〕〔謨〕、提督南贛軍務右副都御史聶〔賢〕、清戎監察御史陶〔儼〕，則謀于左右布政使蔣〔瑶〕、嚴〔紘〕及其左右叅政王〔大〕〔用〕、馮〔馴〕、左叅議陳〔塀〕、陸〔溥〕，則謀于按察使丁〔沂〕及其副使顧〔應〕〔祥〕、周〔廣〕、范〔輅〕、林〔大〕〔輅〕、查〔約〕、謝〔廸〕、僉事徐〔乾〕、魯〔綸〕、汪〔應〕〔軫〕、高〔賁〕〔亨〕、張〔□〕〔□〕，而後□
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Jiangxi Provincial Examination

In autumn, the eighth month of the yiyou year of Jiajing [1525], the triennial examination was held. Before this, Qin Yuesi [?], the Regional Inspector of Jiangxi and Investigating Censor, said: “In this undertaking, nothing is more urgent than the duty of a subject to demonstrate loyalty. How could I dare not prepare beforehand?”

He therefore consulted Cui He, the Grand Defender and Grand Eunuch; Chen Hongmo, the Grand Coordinator and Right Vice Censor-in-Chief; Nie Xian, the Right Vice Censor-in-Chief supervising military affairs in Nan’an and Ganzhou; and Tao Yan, the Investigating Censor charged with inspecting military personnel. He then consulted Jiang Yao and Yan Hong, the Left and Right Provincial Administration Commissioners, together with Wang Dayong and Feng Xun, their Left and Right Vice Administration Commissioners, and Chen Ping and Lu Pu, Left Assistant Administration Commissioners. He then consulted Ding Yi, the Provincial Surveillance Commissioner, together with his Surveillance Vice Commissioners Gu Yingxiang, Zhou Guang, Fan Lu, Lin Dalu, Zha Yue, and Xie Di, and the Surveillance Assistant Commissioners Xu Qian, Lu Lun, Wang Yingzhen, Gao Benheng, and Zhang [two illegible characters]. Only afterward [illegible] …

title: 嘉靖四年江西鄉試錄
text:
事於是禮聘〔度〕及教授吳〔益夫〕
爲考試官教諭朱〔佩〕潘〔龍〕許〔相〕
黄〔源〕王〔昺〕陳〔希登〕馬〔驎〕訓導張
〔廉〕吳〔桂〕蔡〔珀〕爲同考試官一時
有事兹土者南京戶部署郎中
蔣〔孔煬〕兵部署郎中彭〔本用〕戶
部主事江〔元輔〕祖〔琚〕亦罔不與
===
聞之〔度〕等旣至則聞都臺藩臬
亦各遷拜不常矣〔賢〕遷而潘〔希〕
〔曾〕代〔瑶〕遷而〔紘〕代〔紘〕轉而袁〔櫝〕
代〔沂〕遷而張〔羽〕代〔廣〕遷而徐〔一〕
〔鳴〕代〔乾〕去而鍾〔雲瑞〕代執事者
兼有勞焉提調則屬布政使〔紘〕
叅議〔溥〕監試則屬副使〔應祥〕僉
punctuated:
事。於是禮聘〔度〕及教授吳〔益夫〕爲考試官，教諭朱〔佩〕、潘〔龍〕、許〔相〕、黄〔源〕、王〔昺〕、陳〔希登〕、馬〔驎〕、訓導張〔廉〕、吳〔桂〕、蔡〔珀〕爲同考試官。一時有事兹土者，南京戶部署郎中蔣〔孔煬〕、兵部署郎中彭〔本用〕、戶部主事江〔元輔〕、祖〔琚〕，亦罔不與聞之。
〔度〕等旣至，則聞都臺、藩臬亦各遷拜不常矣。〔賢〕遷而潘〔希〕〔曾〕代，〔瑶〕遷而〔紘〕代，〔紘〕轉而袁〔櫝〕代，〔沂〕遷而張〔羽〕代，〔廣〕遷而徐〔一〕〔鳴〕代，〔乾〕去而鍾〔雲瑞〕代，執事者兼有勞焉。提調則屬布政使〔紘〕、叅議〔溥〕，監試則屬副使〔應祥〕、僉
translation_en:
… affairs. Thereupon Du 〔度〕 and Professor Wu Yifu were formally invited to serve as Examiners. Instructors Zhu Pei, Pan Long, Xu Xiang, Huang Yuan, Wang Bing, Chen Xideng, and Ma Lin, together with Assistant Instructors Zhang Lian, Wu Gui, and Cai Po, were appointed Associate Examiners. Those then conducting official business in the region—Jiang Kongyang, Acting Bureau Director in the Nanjing Ministry of Revenue; Peng Benyong, Acting Bureau Director in the Ministry of War; and Jiang Yuanfu and Zu Ju, Secretaries in the Ministry of Revenue—were likewise all consulted about the matter.
After Du and the others arrived, they learned that appointments in the censorial headquarters and the Provincial Administration and Surveillance Commissions had also repeatedly changed through transfers and new appointments. Nie Xian was transferred and replaced by Pan Xizeng; Jiang Yao was transferred and replaced by Yan Hong; Yan Hong was reassigned and replaced by Yuan Du; Ding Yi was transferred and replaced by Zhang Yu; Zhou Guang was transferred and replaced by Xu Yiming; and Xu Qian departed and was replaced by Zhong Yunrui. The officials handling these matters thus bore additional burdens. The duties of Proctor were entrusted to Provincial Administration Commissioner Yan Hong and Assistant Administration Commissioner Lu Pu; supervision of the examination was entrusted to Surveillance Vice Commissioner Gu Yingxiang and an Assistant Surveillance Commissioner …

title: 嘉靖四年江西鄉試錄
text:
事〔儉〕防檢于外則靈署都指揮
僉事劉〔璽〕馮〔勲〕王〔寧〕其掌卷彌
封對讀諸執事自知府而下則
又各以其檄來遂以乙之日入
簾合前董學副使〔廣〕所選十三
郡之士如故事而試之三積二
十餘日凡閱三千卷而拔茲九
十五人者蓋
===
制額也於是鄉試錄成〔虔〕以職事當
序諸首惟
今制揭曉有燕歌鹿鳴以賓興之其
來遠矣請以鹿鳴之說為旅酬
告焉鹿鳴之詩曰我有嘉賓鼓
瑟吹笙吹笙鼓簧承筐是將人
punctuated:
事〔儉〕。防檢于外，則靈署都指揮僉事劉〔璽〕、馮〔勲〕、王〔寧〕。其掌卷、彌封、對讀諸執事，自知府而下，則又各以其檄來。遂以乙之日入簾，合前董學副使〔廣〕所選十三郡之士，如故事而試之三，積二十餘日，凡閱三千卷，而拔茲九十五人者，蓋制額也。
於是鄉試錄成，〔虔〕以職事當序諸首。惟今制，揭曉有燕，歌《鹿鳴》以賓興之，其來遠矣。請以《鹿鳴》之說為旅酬告焉。《鹿鳴》之詩曰：「我有嘉賓，鼓瑟吹笙。吹笙鼓簧，承筐是將。人
translation_en:
…Assistant Surveillance Commissioner Jian. Responsible for security and inspection outside were the Assistant Regional Military Commissioners Liu Xi, Feng Xun, and Wang Ning, serving in the ling office [?]. The other functionaries responsible for handling scripts, sealing identifying information, and checking readings, from prefects downward, each came in response to an official summons. Then, on the yi day [?], we entered the examiners’ enclosure and assembled the candidates from the thirteen prefectures previously selected by Guang, the Surveillance Vice Commissioner overseeing education. Following established practice, we examined them in three sessions. Over more than twenty days, we read three thousand scripts and selected these ninety-five men—the prescribed quota.
The Record of the Provincial Examination was thus completed, and I, Qian, was obliged by my official duties to place a preface at its beginning. Under the present regulations, a banquet is held after the results are announced, and “The Deer Call” (Lu ming) is sung to honor and advance the successful candidates as guests. This practice has a long history. Allow me to offer an explanation of “The Deer Call” as an address for the communal exchange of toasts. The poem “The Deer Call” says: “I have fine guests; we play the zithers and blow the mouth organs. We blow the mouth organs, sounding their reeds; baskets are held up in presentation. Those…

title: 嘉靖四年江西鄉試錄
text:
之好我示我周行以乞言也今
之錄其文以
獻加多矣曰我有嘉賓德音孔昭
示民不恌君子是則是傚以名
教也今之錄其名氏傳播無窮
加顯矣古鹿鳴之嘉賓類皆司
徒之養士司馬樂正之所論而
===
官之者也何其盛也後世鄉舉
里選之瀍廢而一切科目之途
闢獨賓興之禮往往有古之意
又何末也我
朝設科取士剗滌漢唐以來詞賦
之習而一於經義論策乎求之
所以掄文之弊也比其後也斆
punctuated: 之好我，示我周行」，以乞言也。今之錄其文以獻，加多矣。曰：「我有嘉賓，德音孔昭，示民不恌，君子是則是傚。」以名教也。今之錄其名氏，傳播無窮，加顯矣。古《鹿鳴》之嘉賓，類皆司徒之養士、司馬樂正之所論而官之者也，何其盛也！後世鄉舉里選之瀍廢，而一切科目之途闢，獨賓興之禮往往有古之意，又何末也！我朝設科取士，剗滌漢唐以來詞賦之習，而一於經義論策乎求之，所以掄文之弊也。比其後也，斆
translation_en:
… “Those who favor me show me the right way”: this was to solicit counsel. Today, recording their compositions for presentation to the throne provides still more. The ode says: “I have honored guests; their virtuous reputation shines brightly. They show the people how not to be frivolous; gentlemen take them as models and emulate them.” This serves moral instruction. Today, recording their names and disseminating them without end makes them still more illustrious.

The honored guests of the ancient ode “The Deer Call” (Lu ming) were generally scholars nurtured by the Minister of Education, assessed by the Minister of War and the Director of Music, and then appointed to office. How flourishing it was! In later ages, recommendation from the townships and selection from the villages fell into disuse [?], while the avenues of examination recruitment were opened. Only the ceremony of honoring and recommending worthy men still frequently preserved something of the ancient spirit—yet how diminished it had become!

Our dynasty established examinations to recruit scholars, sweeping away the practice of verse and rhapsody cultivated since the Han and Tang, and seeking candidates exclusively through interpretations of the classics, discourses, and policy essays. This was intended to address the abuses of selection by literary composition [?]. Later on, teaching …

title: 嘉靖四年江西鄉試錄
text:
學相禪主司士相遭而亦不免
焉蓋其勢也方今
皇上嗣極惇本復質于茲再舉百執
事祗承
德意視昔彌固江西固多賢之地也
必有所謂道德之士出而名世
凡茲與鹿鳴之席而不以古之
===
嘉賓自待者有其善者也令夫
琴瑟笙簧筐篚幣帛同言論
風旨同而古今人不同則可乎
古之人歌鹿鳴而興也受之而
不慚令之人歌鹿鳴而與也聞
之而足以懼凡茲冐古人之樂
而不以令人自懼者無是心者
punctuated: 學相禪，主司、士相遭，而亦不免焉，蓋其勢也。方今皇上嗣極，惇本復質，于茲再舉。百執事祗承德意，視昔彌固。江西固多賢之地也，必有所謂道德之士出而名世。凡茲與鹿鳴之席而不以古之嘉賓自待者，有其善者也。令夫琴瑟笙簧、筐篚幣帛同，言論風旨同，而古今人不同，則可乎？古之人歌鹿鳴而興也，受之而不慚；令之人歌鹿鳴而與也，聞之而足以懼。凡茲冐古人之樂而不以令人自懼者，無是心者
translation_en:
…learning passed on in succession [?], and examiners and candidates encountered one another, yet they too could not escape these abuses: such was the tendency of circumstances. Now His Majesty has succeeded to the throne, honored the foundations, and restored simplicity; this is the second holding of the examination under his reign. All officials reverently uphold his virtuous intentions, more firmly than before. Jiangxi has always been a land rich in worthy men. Surely men of moral principle and virtue will emerge to win renown in their age. Among all those attending this Deer Calling banquet, those who do not hold themselves to the standard of the honored guests of antiquity have their own goodness [?].

Now [?], if the zithers, mouth organs and reeds, the baskets and gifts of silk are the same, and the discourse and its tenor are the same, yet the people of antiquity and today differ, can this be acceptable? When the men of antiquity were recommended for office to the singing of Deer Calling, they received the honor without shame. When the men of today [?] participate in the singing of Deer Calling, hearing it should suffice to make them apprehensive. All those who presume to enjoy the music of the ancients yet do not feel apprehension as men of today [?] are people without this disposition…

title: 嘉靖四年江西鄉試錄
text:
也天之所以與我者古今一而
已周行德音胥此焉出而非學
亦何以反其本也故曰仕而優
則學學而優則仕也善學者合
仕與學而一之者也合道德名
實而一之者也今之學者二矣
或失則固或失則浮是故與其
===
浮也寧固其言也浮于實也其
名也浮于行也而今之所錄者
固言也名也於虖懼哉茲役也
簾以內考試同考試官得行之
也簾以外提調監試官各專之
也而御史〔鉞〕寔合內外而臨之
者也作興之者兩廣御史及清
punctuated: 也。天之所以與我者，古今一而已。周行德音，胥此焉出，而非學，亦何以反其本也？故曰：「仕而優則學，學而優則仕。」也。善學者，合仕與學而一之者也，合道德名實而一之者也。今之學者二矣，或失則固，或失則浮。是故與其浮也，寧固。其言也浮于實也，其名也浮于行也，而今之所錄者，固言也、名也。於虖，懼哉！茲役也，簾以內，考試、同考試官得行之也；簾以外，提調、監試官各專之也。而御史〔鉞〕寔合內外而臨之者也。作興之者，兩廣御史及清
translation_en:
…such are they. What Heaven has bestowed upon us is the same in ancient and modern times. The great way and virtuous repute both issue from this; without learning, how could one return to their source? Hence the saying: “When serving in office, if you have capacity to spare, study; when studying, if you have capacity to spare, serve in office.” Those who learn well unite service and study as one, and unite the Way, virtue, reputation, and substance as one. Learners today divide these into two. Some err through rigidity, others through superficiality. Thus, rather than be superficial, it is better to be rigid. Their words exceed their substance, and their reputations exceed their conduct; yet what we record here is, after all, words and reputations. Alas, how daunting!

In this undertaking, the Examiners and Associate Examiners conduct the work inside the curtain; outside it, the Proctors and Examination Inspectors each have their own responsibilities. Censor 〔Yue〕, however, brings together the work inside and outside and oversees it all. The impetus for this came from the censor for Liangguang and the censor for military reorganization…

title: 嘉靖四年江西鄉試錄
text:
戎御史之意也相成之者後先
諸藩臬之功也而御史寔集衆
思而用之者也始而選士董學
之明也終而拔尤諸考校之勤
也而〔度〕竊自附於公無私者也
直隸松江府儒學教授王〔度〕謹
序
punctuated:
戎御史之意也。相成之者，後先諸藩臬之功也，而御史寔集衆思而用之者也。始而選士，董學之明也；終而拔尤，諸考校之勤也。而〔度〕竊自附於公無私者也。
直隸松江府儒學教授王〔度〕謹序。
translation_en:
…the intention of the censor charged with inspecting military registers. That these efforts complemented one another was the achievement of successive provincial administration commissioners and surveillance commissioners; the censor himself brought together their various ideas and put them into practice. The initial selection of candidates owed to the discernment of the official supervising education; the final choice of the outstanding among them owed to the diligence of the examiners. I, Du, venture to count myself among those who served impartially, without private interests.
Respectfully composed as a preface by Wang Du, Instructor of the Confucian School of Songjiang Prefecture in the directly administered metropolitan region.

title: 嘉靖四年江西鄉試錄
text:
嘉靖四年江西鄉試

巡按江西監察御史秦鉞〔懋功浙江慈谿縣人　甲戌進士〕
提調官
江西等處承宣布政使司左布政使嚴紘〔仲周應天府江浦縣人　壬戌進士〕
江西等處承宣布政使司左參議陸溥〔原博浙江錢塘縣人　戊辰進士〕

江西等處提刑按察司副使顧應祥〔惟賢浙江長興縣人　乙丑進士〕
江西等處提刑按察司僉事張儉〔存禮浙江縉居縣人　甲戌進士〕
===

直隸松江府儒學教授王度〔律生浙江臨海縣籍寧海　縣人癸未進士〕
南京京衛武學教授吳益夫〔維裕福建閩縣人　丁卯貢士〕

山東東昌府臨清州丘縣儒學教諭朱侃〔子和直隸蕪湖縣人　丙子貢士〕
福建興化府莆田縣儒學教諭潘龍〔言卿廣東南海縣人　丙子貢士〕
福建建寧府建安縣儒學教諭許相〔廷輔廣東新會縣人　丙子貢士〕
湖廣安陸州京山縣儒學教諭黃源〔子淵福建南安縣人　癸酉貢士〕
直隸揚州府通州海門縣儒學教諭王禹〔文疇福建候官縣人　壬午貢士〕
punctuated:
嘉靖四年江西鄉試

監臨官：
巡按江西監察御史秦鉞〔懋功，浙江慈谿縣人，甲戌進士〕。

提調官：
江西等處承宣布政使司左布政使嚴紘〔仲周，應天府江浦縣人，壬戌進士〕。

江西等處提刑按察司副使顧應祥〔惟賢，浙江長興縣人，乙丑進士〕。

直隸松江府儒學教授王度〔律生，浙江臨海縣籍，寧海縣人，癸未進士〕。
南京京衛武學教授吳益夫〔維裕，福建閩縣人，丁卯貢士〕。

南昌府通判韓選〔士賢直隸桐城縣人丁卯貢士〕
九江府通判安節〔之亨湖廣武昌護衛人辛酉貢士〕
廣信府經歷司經歷何周〔汝南直隸卅徒縣人監生〕
撫州府照磨所檢校殷甫〔周甫直隸嘉定縣人監生〕
廣信府永豐縣知縣方禾〔嘉伯直隸泰州人辛酉貢士〕
撫州府樂安縣知縣吳鯉〔躍如直隸太湖縣人庚午貢士〕
廣信府永豐縣主簿張澄〔文靜浙江鄞縣人監生〕
會昌守禦千戶所吏目於僎〔天德浙江嘉善縣人知印〕
南昌府南浦驛驛丞梁喬〔遷之湖廣襄陽縣人承差〕
南昌府南昌縣武陽驛驛丞王良弼〔國佐廣東保昌縣人承差〕
吉安府廬陵縣螺川驛驛丞吳深〔世隆山東章丘縣人承差〕
建昌府南城縣盱江驛驛丞李糾〔天威河南鈞州人承差〕
punctuated: 南昌府通判韓選〔士賢，直隸桐城縣人，丁卯貢士〕。九江府通判安節〔之亨，湖廣武昌護衛人，辛酉貢士〕。廣信府經歷司經歷何周〔汝南，直隸卅徒縣人，監生〕。撫州府照磨所檢校殷甫〔周甫，直隸嘉定縣人，監生〕。廣信府永豐縣知縣方禾〔嘉伯，直隸泰州人，辛酉貢士〕。撫州府樂安縣知縣吳鯉〔躍如，直隸太湖縣人，庚午貢士〕。廣信府永豐縣主簿張澄〔文靜，浙江鄞縣人，監生〕。會昌守禦千戶所吏目於僎〔天德，浙江嘉善縣人，知印〕。南昌府南浦驛驛丞梁喬〔遷之，湖廣襄陽縣人，承差〕。南昌府南昌縣武陽驛驛丞王良弼〔國佐，廣東保昌縣人，承差〕。吉安府廬陵縣螺川驛驛丞吳深〔世隆，山東章丘縣人，承差〕。建昌府南城縣盱江驛驛丞李糾〔天威，河南鈞州人，承差〕。

title: 嘉靖四年江西鄉試錄
text:
第壹塲
四書
無欲速無見小利欲速則不達見小利則
大事不成
肫肫其仁淵淵其淵浩浩其天
滄浪之水清兮可以濯我纓滄浪之水濁
兮可以濯我足孔子曰小子聽之清斯
濯纓濁斯濯足矣自取之也
易
===
貞固足以幹事
天地感而萬物化生聖人感人心而天下
和平觀其所感而天地萬物之情可見
矣
是故法象莫大乎天地變通莫大乎四時
縣象著明莫大乎日月崇高莫大乎富
貴備物致用立成器以爲天下利莫大
乎聖人探賾索隱鉤深致遠以定天下
之吉凶成天下之亹亹者莫大乎蓍龜
punctuated:
第壹塲

四書

無欲速，無見小利。欲速則不達，見小利則大事不成。

肫肫其仁，淵淵其淵，浩浩其天。

滄浪之水清兮，可以濯我纓；滄浪之水濁兮，可以濯我足。孔子曰：「小子聽之！清斯濯纓，濁斯濯足矣，自取之也。」

易

貞固足以幹事。

天地感而萬物化生，聖人感人心而天下和平。觀其所感，而天地萬物之情可見矣。

是故法象莫大乎天地，變通莫大乎四時，縣象著明莫大乎日月，崇高莫大乎富貴，備物致用、立成器以爲天下利莫大乎聖人，探賾索隱、鉤深致遠，以定天下之吉凶、成天下之亹亹者莫大乎蓍龜。
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

Do not seek haste; do not look to small gains. Seeking haste prevents attainment; looking to small gains prevents great undertakings from being accomplished.

Utterly sincere is his benevolence; unfathomably deep is his depth; boundlessly vast is his heavenliness.

When the waters of the Canglang are clear, I can wash my cap strings in them; when the waters of the Canglang are muddy, I can wash my feet in them. Confucius said: “My young disciples, listen to this! When clear, they are used to wash cap strings; when muddy, they are used to wash feet. They bring this treatment upon themselves.”

Book of Changes

Correctness and firmness are sufficient to carry out undertakings.

Heaven and earth affect one another, and the myriad things are transformed and brought into being. The sage moves human hearts, and all under heaven is peaceful and harmonious. By observing what they affect, one can perceive the true dispositions of heaven, earth, and the myriad things.

Thus, among models and images, none are greater than heaven and earth; in change and adaptation, none are greater than the four seasons; among suspended images shining brightly, none are greater than the sun and moon; in eminence and exaltation, none are greater than wealth and noble rank. In preparing things for use and fashioning finished implements to benefit all under heaven, none are greater than the sages. In probing mysteries and seeking what is hidden, plumbing the depths and reaching afar, thereby determining good and ill fortune for all under heaven and bringing its unremitting endeavors to completion, none are greater than the milfoil stalks and tortoise shells.

title: 嘉靖四年江西鄉試錄
text:
有大者不可以盈故受之以謙有大而能
謙必豫故受之以豫
書
帝曰咨汝羲暨和朞三百有六旬有六日
以閏月定四時成歳允釐百工庶績咸
熈
與治同道罔不興
人之有能有為使羞其行而邦其昌凡厥
正人既富方穀
寛而有制從容以和
===
詩
關關雎鳩在河之洲窈窕淑女君子好逑
鴥彼飛隼其飛戾天亦集爰止方叔涖止
其車三千師干之試方叔率止鉦人伐
鼓陳師鞠旅顯允方叔伐鼓淵淵振旅
闐闐
受天之祜四方來賀
穆穆來假敬明其德敬慎威儀維民之則
punctuated:
有大者不可以盈，故受之以謙；有大而能謙，必豫，故受之以豫。

書
帝曰：「咨！汝羲暨和，朞三百有六旬有六日，以閏月定四時，成歳，允釐百工，庶績咸熈。」
與治同道，罔不興。
人之有能有為，使羞其行，而邦其昌。凡厥正人，既富方穀。
寛而有制，從容以和。

詩
關關雎鳩，在河之洲。窈窕淑女，君子好逑。
鴥彼飛隼，其飛戾天，亦集爰止。方叔涖止，其車三千。師干之試，方叔率止。鉦人伐鼓，陳師鞠旅。顯允方叔，伐鼓淵淵，振旅闐闐。
受天之祜，四方來賀。
穆穆來假，敬明其德。敬慎威儀，維民之則。
translation_en:
…Those who possess greatness must not become full of themselves; hence Great Possession is followed by Modesty. Those who possess greatness and can remain modest will surely find delight; hence Modesty is followed by Delight.

Book of Documents
The Emperor said: “Ah! You, Xi and He: the full year comprises three hundred and sixty-six days. Use intercalary months to fix the four seasons and complete the year. Truly put the hundred offices in order, and all undertakings will flourish.”
Those who follow the same way as good government invariably prosper.
When people have ability and accomplishment, enable them to advance their work, and your state will flourish. As for its upright men, once they are provided for, they will become good.
Be generous yet exercise restraint, composed and harmonious.

Book of Odes
“Guan, guan” cry the ospreys, on an islet in the river. The modest, virtuous maiden is a fine mate for the gentleman.
Swift is that flying falcon; its flight reaches the sky, and it also alights and rests here. Fang Shu arrives, with three thousand chariots. The host displays its shields; Fang Shu leads it. The gong men beat the drums; they array the troops and marshal the ranks. Illustrious and trustworthy is Fang Shu! The drums resound deeply; the troops return in thunderous array.
Receiving Heaven’s blessing, he is congratulated by those who come from the four quarters.
Solemnly he approaches, reverently making his virtue manifest. Reverent and careful in his bearing, he is a model for the people.

title: 嘉靖四年江西鄉試錄
text:
春秋
春王正月〔隱公元年〕夏齊侯衛侯胥命于蒲
〔桓公三年〕
楚人伐黄〔僖公十有一年〕楚人滅黄〔僖公十有二年〕
冬十月甲午叔孫得臣敗狄于鹹〔文公十有
一年〕
楚子使椒來聘〔文公九年〕十有一月公如楚
〔襄公二十八年〕夏五月公至自楚〔襄公二十九年〕
禮記
===
夫爲人子者三賜不及車馬
郊特牲而社稷大牢天子適諸侯諸侯膳
用犢諸侯適天子天子賜之禮大牢貴
誠之義也
宮爲君商爲臣角爲民徵爲事羽爲物
事君欲諫不欲陳詩云心乎愛矣瑕不謂
矣中心藏之何日忘之
第貳場
論
punctuated:
春秋

春，王正月。〔隱公元年〕夏，齊侯、衛侯胥命于蒲。〔桓公三年〕
楚人伐黄。〔僖公十有一年〕楚人滅黄。〔僖公十有二年〕
冬，十月甲午，叔孫得臣敗狄于鹹。〔文公十有一年〕
楚子使椒來聘。〔文公九年〕十有一月，公如楚。〔襄公二十八年〕夏，五月，公至自楚。〔襄公二十九年〕

禮記

夫爲人子者，三賜不及車馬。
郊特牲，而社稷大牢。天子適諸侯，諸侯膳用犢；諸侯適天子，天子賜之禮大牢，貴誠之義也。
宮爲君，商爲臣，角爲民，徵爲事，羽爲物。
事君欲諫，不欲陳。詩云：「心乎愛矣，瑕不謂矣？中心藏之，何日忘之？」

第貳場

論
translation_en:
Spring and Autumn Annals

In spring, the first month of the royal calendar. 〔First year of Duke Yin.〕 In summer, the Marquis of Qi and the Marquis of Wei exchanged pledges at Pu. 〔Third year of Duke Huan.〕
The men of Chu attacked Huang. 〔Eleventh year of Duke Xi.〕 The men of Chu destroyed Huang. 〔Twelfth year of Duke Xi.〕
In winter, on the jiawu day of the tenth month, Shusun Dechen defeated the Di at Xian. 〔Eleventh year of Duke Wen.〕
The Viscount of Chu sent Jiao on a diplomatic visit to our court. 〔Ninth year of Duke Wen.〕 In the eleventh month, the duke went to Chu. 〔Twenty-eighth year of Duke Xiang.〕 In summer, in the fifth month, the duke returned from Chu. 〔Twenty-ninth year of Duke Xiang.〕
Record of Rites

For one who is a son, even three successive grants of gifts should not extend to carriages and horses.
The suburban sacrifice uses a single animal, whereas the sacrifices to the gods of soil and grain use a full set of sacrificial animals—an ox, a sheep, and a pig. When the Son of Heaven visits a feudal lord, the lord serves him a calf; when a feudal lord visits the Son of Heaven, the Son of Heaven accords him the ceremonial gift of a full set of sacrificial animals. This embodies the principle of valuing sincerity.
The gong note represents the ruler; shang, the ministers; jue, the people; zhi, affairs; and yu, things.
In serving a ruler, one should seek to remonstrate with him, without exposing his faults. The Book of Odes says: “In my heart I love him; why should I not tell him? I treasure him within my heart; what day could I forget him?”
Second Session

Discourse

title: 嘉靖四年江西鄉試錄
text:
聖學無所爲而然
詔誥表〔内科一道〕
擬漢文帝弛利省費以振民詔〔後六年〕
擬唐以韓愈爲吏部侍郎誥〔長慶三年〕
擬宋以九經頒賜州縣學校及聚徒講誦
之所謝表〔咸平四年〕
判語〔五條〕
選用軍職
守掌在官財物
===
收藏禁書及私習天文
窩弓殺傷人
家人求索
第叁場
策五道
問炎漢以來代凡幾君靡有不尊孔氏矣
若過魯之祀先聖之褒親自爲贊特其
尤隆者耳然皆隨其一時秉彝之好而
非終身致治之實皆奉耆若哉
punctuated:
聖學無所爲而然。

詔誥表〔内科一道〕
擬漢文帝弛利省費以振民詔〔後六年〕。
擬唐以韓愈爲吏部侍郎誥〔長慶三年〕。
擬宋以九經頒賜州縣學校及聚徒講誦之所謝表〔咸平四年〕。

判語〔五條〕
選用軍職。
守掌在官財物。
收藏禁書及私習天文。
窩弓殺傷人。
家人求索。

第叁場
策五道。
問：炎漢以來，代凡幾君，靡有不尊孔氏矣。若過魯之祀、先聖之褒、親自爲贊，特其尤隆者耳。然皆隨其一時秉彝之好，而非終身致治之實，皆奉耆若哉？
translation_en:
Sage learning is so of itself, without an ulterior purpose.

Edict, proclamation, and memorial 〔one topic from among these [?]〕
Compose an edict in the voice of Emperor Wen of Han relaxing revenue exactions and reducing expenditure to relieve the people. 〔Sixth year of the Later Era〕
Compose a Tang proclamation appointing Han Yu Vice Minister of Personnel. 〔Third year of Changqing〕
Compose a Song memorial of thanks for the distribution of the Nine Classics to prefectural and county schools and to places where students gather for lectures and recitation. 〔Fourth year of Xianping〕

Legal judgments 〔five items〕
Selection and appointment of military officers.
Custody and management of property in official keeping.
Collecting and keeping prohibited books and privately studying astronomy.
Killing or injuring people with concealed spring bows.
Demands and exactions by household members.

Third Session
Five policy questions.
Question: Since the Han dynasty, how many rulers have there been through successive dynasties? None failed to honor Confucius. Sacrificing when passing through Lu, bestowing honors upon the Former Sage, and personally composing eulogies were merely the most conspicuous instances of such reverence. Yet all these followed a momentary inclination arising from their innate moral nature, rather than constituting the substance of a lifetime devoted to achieving good government. Did they all thus honor the aged [?] …

title: 嘉靖四年江西鄉試錄
text:
朝之極其崇重而服行之者也蓋嘗伏讀我
太宗文皇帝御製孔廟之碑而仰窺
祖宗右文之治矣
聖德之厚及其子孫
宸翰之光被諸林闕自肇祀以來所未覩也
文皇之言曰尚推孔子之道一
皇考之所以表章者於乎盛矣然則
文皇之所學者固
聖祖之所謂學乎
===
聖祖之所學者又吾孔子之所謂學乎得其學
則所表章者非虛文得其表章則其致
治者不徒矣或謂南都之木主其革之
而未盡乎京師之塑像其因之而未革
乎此則
聖人之用意有非恒情之所易窺否則漢唐宋
諸君亦嘗修其祀矣即儀文之詳畧不
同而治化必不如是之相懸也其亦有
可得而論乎諸生還
punctuated: 朝之極其崇重而服行之者也。蓋嘗伏讀我太宗文皇帝御製孔廟之碑，而仰窺祖宗右文之治矣。聖德之厚及其子孫，宸翰之光被諸林闕，自肇祀以來所未覩也。文皇之言曰：「尚推孔子之道，一皇考之所以表章者。」於乎盛矣！然則文皇之所學者，固聖祖之所謂學乎？聖祖之所學者，又吾孔子之所謂學乎？得其學，則所表章者非虛文；得其表章，則其致治者不徒矣。或謂南都之木主，其革之而未盡乎？京師之塑像，其因之而未革乎？此則聖人之用意，有非恒情之所易窺。否則漢唐宋諸君亦嘗修其祀矣，即儀文之詳畧不同，而治化必不如是之相懸也。其亦有可得而論乎？諸生還
translation_en:
…the dynasty has accorded him the utmost reverence and esteem, and put his teachings into practice. I have reverently read the imperially composed stele inscription for the Temple of Confucius by our Emperor Taizong Wen, and thereby glimpsed with admiration the ancestral emperors’ government that honored civil learning. The abundance of his sagely virtue extended to Confucius’s descendants, and the radiance of his imperial writing illuminated the wooded temple precincts—something never witnessed since sacrifices to Confucius first began. Emperor Wen said: “May we further promote the Way of Confucius, wholly following [?] what my deceased imperial father honored and made manifest.” Ah, how magnificent!

Was what Emperor Wen studied, then, indeed what the Sagely Progenitor called learning? And was what the Sagely Progenitor studied also what our Confucius called learning? If they grasped that learning, what they honored and made manifest was no empty formality; if they grasped the meaning of thus honoring and making it manifest, their efforts to achieve good government were not in vain.

Some say: as for the wooden spirit tablet in the Southern Capital, was the reform incomplete? As for the sculpted image in the capital, was it retained without reform? Here the sage’s intentions include things that ordinary understanding cannot readily fathom. Otherwise, the rulers of the Han, Tang, and Song also attended to the sacrifices to Confucius; even if their ceremonial forms differed in elaborateness, their achievements in government and moral transformation surely would not have been so far apart. Might there be something here that can be discussed? You candidates, return [?] …

title: 嘉靖四年江西鄉試錄
text:
聖謨明孔道必有見於其大尚敬陳之
問古之儒者幼而志於學壯而達於政蓋
廟堂紀法之議即學校傳習之業學與
政非二端也然孔門四科以政事文學
列而爲二豈以人不能兼長歟將二者
果不相係也伊傅周召以相業名政之
著也其學亦有可言者與孔孟程朱以
儒術顯學之宗也其政亦有可言者與
他如歷代諸賢列于儒林者若而人授
===
之以政亦能達其所學之用否與列于
循吏者若而人究其所學又能基其立
政之體否與然擅擁立之功者君子議
其不學無術而稱大忠于天下者漢史
列傳猶未之觀政似不須於學也宰相
封侯者君子謂其曲學阿世而斟量立
螯者乃自謂不能籌策於廟堂學又似
無補於政也其間又有優於治民者終
身不談政事富於問學者終身不談文
punctuated:
聖謨，明孔道，必有見於其大，尚敬陳之。

問：古之儒者，幼而志於學，壯而達於政。蓋廟堂紀法之議，即學校傳習之業，學與政非二端也。然孔門四科，以政事、文學列而爲二，豈以人不能兼長歟？將二者果不相係也？伊傅周召以相業名，政之著也，其學亦有可言者與？孔孟程朱以儒術顯，學之宗也，其政亦有可言者與？他如歷代諸賢，列于儒林者若而人，授之以政，亦能達其所學之用否與？列于循吏者若而人，究其所學，又能基其立政之體否與？然擅擁立之功者，君子議其不學無術；而稱大忠于天下者，漢史列傳猶未之觀，政似不須於學也。宰相封侯者，君子謂其曲學阿世；而斟量立螯者，乃自謂不能籌策於廟堂，學又似無補於政也。其間又有優於治民者，終身不談政事；富於問學者，終身不談文
translation_en:
…the sagely counsels and elucidate the Way of Confucius. You must have insights into their larger significance; respectfully set them forth.

Question: The Confucian scholars of antiquity devoted themselves to learning in youth and became accomplished in government in maturity. Deliberations on regulations and laws at court were precisely the work transmitted and studied in the schools: learning and government were not two separate pursuits. Yet among the four disciplines of Confucius’s school, government and literary learning were listed separately. Was this because people could not excel in both, or were the two truly unrelated? Yi Yin, Fu Yue, the Duke of Zhou, and the Duke of Shao were renowned for their achievements as ministers—conspicuous accomplishments in government. Is there also something to be said about their learning? Confucius, Mengzi, the Cheng masters, and Zhu Xi were distinguished for their Confucian teachings and were leading authorities in learning. Is there also something to be said about their government? Likewise, among the worthies of successive dynasties, could those included among the Confucian scholars, if entrusted with government, fully put their learning to use? And if we investigate the learning of those included among the exemplary officials, could it provide a foundation for the essential principles of their government?

Yet the man who achieved distinction by enthroning a ruler was criticized by gentlemen as unlearned and lacking intellectual method; and of the man acclaimed throughout the realm for his great loyalty, the biographies in the History of the Han had yet to witness his like [?]. Government thus seems not to require learning. The man who became chief minister and was enfeoffed as a marquis was said by gentlemen to have distorted learning to curry favor with his age; while the man described as ‘weighing and establishing claws’ [?] himself declared that he could not devise policies at court. Learning thus seems to offer no help to government either. Among them were also men excellent at governing the people who never discussed government throughout their lives, and men rich in learning who never discussed literary…

title: 嘉靖四年江西鄉試錄
text:
章又各有其說否也夫學以致用政不
虛行至當之說正今日之願聞也有慊
不吐是負所學諸士子其毋讓曰未能
問自古帝王之治天下莫不以治曆明時
爲首務羲和欽天之法其詳不可得而
聞矣漢作三統曆始立積年日法爲推
步之準後世因之歷唐及宋作者無慮
數十家然行之未久輒復更易其故何
歟堯典以閏月定四時而後世又有所
===
謂歲差之說不知昉於何人豈置閏之
外復有所謂差歟我
朝大統曆法悉用勝國授時曆之制不用積
年日法以歲實加氣應求冬至以中積
加閏應求經朔行之二百餘年無有改
者諸家之曆皆有元顧不能久授時曆
不立元乃能久而無弊何歟夫天運無
形而難知所可見者日月之交而已書
詩春秋所載日食俱在朔漢魏以後日
punctuated:
章，又各有其說否也？夫學以致用，政不虛行，至當之說，正今日之願聞也。有慊不吐，是負所學。諸士子其毋讓曰未能。

問：自古帝王之治天下，莫不以治曆明時爲首務。羲和欽天之法，其詳不可得而聞矣。漢作三統曆，始立積年日法爲推步之準，後世因之。歷唐及宋，作者無慮數十家，然行之未久，輒復更易，其故何歟？《堯典》以閏月定四時，而後世又有所謂歲差之說，不知昉於何人？豈置閏之外，復有所謂差歟？我朝大統曆法，悉用勝國授時曆之制，不用積年日法，以歲實加氣應求冬至，以中積加閏應求經朔，行之二百餘年，無有改者。諸家之曆皆有元，顧不能久；授時曆不立元，乃能久而無弊，何歟？夫天運無形而難知，所可見者日月之交而已。《書》《詩》《春秋》所載日食俱在朔，漢魏以後日
translation_en:
…literary composition: is there also an explanation for each of these cases? Learning is intended for practical application, and government cannot proceed on empty foundations. An explanation that gets to the heart of the matter is precisely what we wish to hear today. To harbor reservations and leave them unspoken is to betray what you have learned. You candidates should not decline by saying that you are incapable.

Question: From antiquity, emperors and kings governing the realm have invariably made regulating the calendar and clarifying the seasons their foremost task. The details of Xi and He’s methods for reverently observing Heaven can no longer be learned. When the Han devised the Triple Concordance Calendar (Santong li), they first established accumulated years and a day divisor as the standards for astronomical computation, and later generations followed them. Through the Tang and into the Song, there were altogether several dozen makers of calendars. Yet these calendars were repeatedly changed before they had been in use for long. Why was this? The Canon of Yao uses intercalary months to fix the four seasons, but later generations also developed what is called the theory of precession. Who originated it? Beyond the insertion of intercalary months, is there also this so-called discrepancy?

Our dynasty’s Great Unification Calendar (Datong li) adopts in full the system of the Season-Granting Calendar (Shoushi li) of the preceding dynasty. It does not use accumulated years and a day divisor. It adds the actual length of the year to the solar-term epoch offset to find the winter solstice, and adds the accumulated mean interval to the intercalation epoch offset to find the mean new moon. It has been in use for more than two hundred years without alteration. The calendars of the various schools all have a calendrical epoch, yet cannot endure; the Season-Granting Calendar establishes no such epoch, yet can endure without defects. Why is this? The movement of Heaven is without visible form and difficult to comprehend; what can be observed is merely the conjunction of the sun and moon. The solar eclipses recorded in the Book of Documents, the Book of Odes, and the Spring and Autumn Annals all occur on the first day of the lunar month. After the Han and Wei, solar …

title: 嘉靖四年江西鄉試錄
text:
食或在晦何歟近年以來步交食者率
多先後不同而不能一一密合或謂授
時曆法久而不能無差建議欲增損之
者不知果真有所見歟古今論曆者或
曰有一定之法或曰無一定之法不過
隨時考驗以合於天而已若果有一定
之法則皆可以常數求而脩德格天之
說爲不足信若果無一定之法則不可
以常數求而考測推步之術爲不足憑
===
矣是皆載諸史冊班班可攷諸士子學
無究心於此者乎願著于篇毋隱
問周禮聖人經世之書周公所以致太平
之跡上而天地日月下而封域山川著
而禮樂刑政微而禽獸草木纖悉具備
其精神心術盡於此矣孔子曰周監于
二代郁郁乎文哉其以是歟後世雖未
能悉遵古制要之官聯服御車旗禮儀
之節率有取焉秦人滅學斯禮厄矣漢
punctuated:
食或在晦，何歟？近年以來，步交食者率多先後不同，而不能一一密合。或謂授時曆法久而不能無差，建議欲增損之者，不知果真有所見歟？古今論曆者，或曰有一定之法，或曰無一定之法，不過隨時考驗以合於天而已。若果有一定之法，則皆可以常數求，而脩德格天之說爲不足信；若果無一定之法，則不可以常數求，而考測推步之術爲不足憑矣。是皆載諸史冊，班班可攷。諸士子學，無究心於此者乎？願著于篇，毋隱。
問：周禮，聖人經世之書，周公所以致太平之跡。上而天地日月，下而封域山川，著而禮樂刑政，微而禽獸草木，纖悉具備，其精神心術盡於此矣。孔子曰：「周監于二代，郁郁乎文哉！」其以是歟？後世雖未能悉遵古制，要之官聯服御車旗禮儀之節，率有取焉。秦人滅學，斯禮厄矣。漢
translation_en:
…eclipses sometimes occur on the last day of the lunar month. Why is this? In recent years, those calculating eclipses have generally differed in their predictions, some placing them earlier and others later, and have been unable to achieve an exact match in every case. Some say that the methods of the Season-Granting Calendar (Shoushi li), after long use, cannot remain free of discrepancies, and propose adjustments. Do these proposals really rest on sound insight? Those who have discussed calendrical calculation, past and present, have sometimes said that it has fixed methods, and sometimes that it has no fixed methods, requiring only observation and verification as circumstances change, so as to accord with Heaven. If it truly has fixed methods, then everything can be calculated using constant numerical values, and the claim that cultivating virtue can move Heaven is unworthy of belief. If it truly has no fixed methods, then constant numerical values cannot be used to calculate it, and the techniques of observation, measurement, and astronomical computation are unworthy of reliance. All these matters are recorded in the histories and can be clearly verified. Among you candidates, has no one devoted serious study to this? I ask you to set forth your views in writing, withholding nothing.
Question: The Rites of Zhou is a book through which the sage ordered the world, a record of how the Duke of Zhou brought about Great Peace. Above, it encompasses Heaven and Earth, the sun and moon; below, territorial boundaries, mountains and rivers; in manifest affairs, rites and music, punishments and government; in minute matters, birds and beasts, plants and trees. Everything is included in the finest detail: his spirit and the workings of his mind are fully embodied here. Confucius said: “Zhou looked to the two preceding dynasties. How splendid was its culture!” Was this what he meant? Although later ages could not follow all the ancient institutions, their arrangements for coordination among offices, dress and equipment, carriages and banners, and ritual observances were generally drawn from this book. When the men of Qin destroyed learning, these rites suffered calamity. In the Han…

title: 嘉靖四年江西鄉試錄
text:
武帝時有得其本以獻者何以不免秦
世瀆亂之誚漢成帝時有識其書以用
者何以反致六國陰謀之訾鄭康成漢
儒之領袖也一加註疏而五失具存其
詳有可聞歟由漢而來有用十之一二
者有用十之五六者有用十之七八者
奚其治之不古若歟賢如唐太宗知其
爲真聖人之書故貞觀之治多所摸效
宜若難矣何以漸不克終歟世達經殘
周公不可作矣使後之君子有歆羨西
周之化者則於是書也將何所取用何
以崇信歟願盡言以觀用世之學
===
問天人相與之際每驗于災異然而氣數
相值在盛世有所不免至於人事有缺
雖聖人亦以爲懼我
皇上即位以來以乂安海内爲心以恭己化民
爲德人事亦云脩矣邇者水旱相仍火
災再見以致遣賑貸之臣下罪己之
punctuated:
武帝時有得其本以獻者，何以不免秦世瀆亂之誚？漢成帝時有識其書以用者，何以反致六國陰謀之訾？鄭康成，漢儒之領袖也，一加註疏，而五失具存，其詳有可聞歟？由漢而來，有用十之一二者，有用十之五六者，有用十之七八者，奚其治之不古若歟？賢如唐太宗，知其爲真聖人之書，故貞觀之治多所摸效，宜若難矣，何以漸不克終歟？世達經殘，周公不可作矣。使後之君子有歆羨西周之化者，則於是書也，將何所取用，何以崇信歟？願盡言，以觀用世之學。

問：天人相與之際，每驗于災異。然而氣數相值，在盛世有所不免；至於人事有缺，雖聖人亦以爲懼。我皇上即位以來，以乂安海内爲心，以恭己化民爲德，人事亦云脩矣。邇者水旱相仍，火災再見，以致遣賑貸之臣，下罪己之
translation_en:
…During Emperor Wu’s reign, someone obtained a copy and presented it. Why, then, did it not escape the charge of having been corrupted and disordered in Qin times? During Emperor Cheng of Han’s reign, someone recognized the book’s significance and put it to use. Why did this instead provoke the accusation that it embodied the covert schemes of the Six States? Zheng Kangcheng was a leader among Han Confucian scholars; yet once he had supplied annotations and explanations, all five errors remained. May we hear the details? Since the Han, some have applied one or two tenths of it, others five or six tenths, and others seven or eight tenths. Why did their governance fail to equal that of antiquity? A ruler as worthy as Emperor Taizong of Tang recognized it as truly a sage’s book, and the governance of the Zhenguan era therefore followed its example in many respects. It would seem to have been difficult [?]; why, then, did he gradually fail to carry it through to the end? The ages have passed [?], the classic is damaged, and the Duke of Zhou cannot rise again. If gentlemen of later ages admire and yearn for the transforming influence of the Western Zhou, what should they select from this book for practical application, and on what grounds should they revere and trust it? Set forth your views fully, so that we may assess your learning for service in the world.

Question: The interaction between Heaven and humanity is repeatedly evidenced in disasters and anomalies. Yet when configurations of vital energy and allotted cycles coincide, even flourishing ages cannot entirely avoid them. When there are shortcomings in human affairs, even sages regard them with fear. Since ascending the throne, our Emperor has set his heart on bringing order and peace to all within the seas, and has made reverent self-discipline and the transformation of the people his guiding virtues. Human affairs may thus be said to have been put in order. Recently, however, floods and droughts have followed one another, and fires have occurred twice, leading him to dispatch officials to distribute relief and loans, and to issue a self-reproaching …

title: 嘉靖四年江西鄉試錄
text:
詔何以有是哉即其憂勤惕勵不遑寧處其視
古人之弭變也何如變異疊興民不爲
患其視古人之立政也何如世儒論災
異者紛然不一以致人君之脩省漫無
所從有衍公羊之派以著陰陽論者或
有譏其傅會然則春秋紀山川之變異
以爲人爲之感召非歟有廣穀梁之說
以著五行傳者或有譏其牽强然則洪
範以五行之災祥爲五事之休咎非歟
===
文章名世後學所宗一則以受命不于
其天至於請復尊號表則條陳其瑞應
之美何自背其說歟一則以不畏天變
爲非至讀蜀書則以麟鳳龜龍爲常事
何自蹈其轍歟要之災異之作非無由
而至天心仁愛必有道可回然而五經
所載有一定之理諸儒所論有一定之
見可得指而言歟諸士子積學待用將
以堯舜其君其於災異之說辯之明矣
punctuated: 詔，何以有是哉？即其憂勤惕勵，不遑寧處，其視古人之弭變也何如？變異疊興，民不爲患，其視古人之立政也何如？世儒論災異者紛然不一，以致人君之脩省漫無所從。有衍公羊之派以著陰陽論者，或有譏其傅會；然則《春秋》紀山川之變異，以爲人爲之感召，非歟？有廣穀梁之說以著五行傳者，或有譏其牽强；然則《洪範》以五行之災祥爲五事之休咎，非歟？文章名世，後學所宗，一則以受命不于其天，至於《請復尊號表》，則條陳其瑞應之美，何自背其說歟？一則以不畏天變爲非，至《讀蜀書》，則以麟鳳龜龍爲常事，何自蹈其轍歟？要之，災異之作，非無由而至；天心仁愛，必有道可回。然而五經所載，有一定之理；諸儒所論，有一定之見。可得指而言歟？諸士子積學待用，將以堯舜其君，其於災異之說，辯之明矣。
translation_en:
…edict. Why have such things occurred? In his anxious diligence and vigilant self-discipline, allowing himself no time for repose, how does he compare with the ancients in averting calamities? Anomalous events have arisen repeatedly, yet the people have not suffered from them: how does he compare with the ancients in establishing good government? Scholars offer a bewildering variety of accounts of disasters and anomalies, leaving the ruler with no clear guidance for self-cultivation and introspection. Some have developed the Gongyang tradition and written discussions of yin and yang; others have criticized their strained associations. Yet is it wrong, then, to understand the anomalies of mountains and rivers recorded in the Spring and Autumn Annals as responses elicited by human conduct? Some have expanded upon the teachings of Guliang and written commentaries on the Five Phases; others have criticized their forced interpretations. Yet is it wrong, then, that the Great Plan treats the disasters and auspicious signs of the Five Phases as manifestations of favorable and unfavorable outcomes associated with the Five Activities?

There are writers renowned in their age whose works later students take as authoritative. One held that receiving the mandate did not depend upon Heaven [?], yet in his Memorial Requesting the Restoration of the Honorific Title he enumerated the excellence of auspicious portents. Why did he contradict his own argument? Another condemned the failure to fear celestial anomalies, yet in Reading the History of Shu he treated qilin, phoenixes, tortoises, and dragons as ordinary occurrences. Why did he himself fall into the same error? In essence, disasters and anomalies do not arise without cause; Heaven's heart is benevolent and loving, and there must be a way to turn it back toward favor. Nevertheless, what the Five Classics record has determinate principles, and what the various scholars discuss has determinate interpretations. Can these be identified and explained? You candidates have accumulated learning and await employment, intending to make your ruler a Yao or a Shun; surely you have clearly distinguished among the explanations of disasters and anomalies.

title: 嘉靖四年江西鄉試錄
text:
願聞其詳以爲
聖天子獻
punctuated: 願聞其詳，以爲聖天子獻。
translation_en: …I wish to hear a detailed account, to present to the sagely Son of Heaven.

title: 嘉靖四年江西鄉試錄

中式舉人九十五名

中式舉人九十五名。

第一名魏良政，新建縣學生，詩。
第二名江治，進賢縣附學生，書。
第三名歐陽塾，泰和縣附學生，易。
第四名阮范，安福縣附學生，春秋。
第五名畢竟夔，貴溪縣附學生，禮記。
第六名胡文宗，廬陵縣學生，詩。
第七名陳德文，泰和縣增廣生，易。
第八名周宗正，上饒縣學生，書。

第十名萬爚，南昌府學增廣生，詩。

第十五名賀謹徐，永新縣學增廣生，易。
第十六名張臬，進賢縣增廣生，詩。
translation_en:
Ninety-five successful provincial graduates (juren).

First: Wei Liangzheng, a government student at the Xinjian County school. His examination classic was the Book of Odes.
Second: Jiang Zhi, an attached student at the Jinxian County school. His examination classic was the Book of Documents.
Third: Ouyang Shu, an attached student at the Taihe County school. His examination classic was the Book of Changes.
Fourth: Ruan Fan, an attached student at the Anfu County school. His examination classic was the Spring and Autumn Annals.
Fifth: Bi Jingkui, an attached student at the Guixi County school. His examination classic was the Book of Rites.
Sixth: Hu Wenzong, a government student at the Luling County school. His examination classic was the Book of Odes.
Seventh: Chen Dewen, an added student at the Taihe County school. His examination classic was the Book of Changes.
Eighth: Zhou Zongzheng, a government student at the Shangrao County school. His examination classic was the Book of Documents.
Ninth: Liu Zizhong, an attached student at the Anfu County school. His examination classic was the Spring and Autumn Annals.
Tenth: Wan Yue, an added student at the Nanchang Prefectural school. His examination classic was the Book of Odes.
Eleventh: Yang Zuo, a government student at the Taihe County school. His examination classic was the Book of Changes.
Twelfth: Zhou Lin, a government student at the Jianchang Prefectural school. His examination classic was the Book of Odes.
Thirteenth: Han Yuanheng, an added student at the Guangxin Prefectural school. His examination classic was the Book of Documents.
Fourteenth: Long Shanzhi, a government student at the Nanchang County school. His examination classic was the Book of Odes.

title: 嘉靖四年江西鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
無欲速無見小利欲速則不達見小利則
大事不成
陳德文
同考試官教諭馬　批〔題本簡易明白作者詞多重複此篇數言即了其義授之以政必能達者〕
同考試官教諭黃　批〔聖人告子夏之言正為政者所當戒此作得之〕
===
同考試官教諭潘　批〔隱括政體得夫子言外之意〕
考試官教授吳　批〔辭不繁而意自足錄之〕
考試官教授王　批〔遲速小大之間王伯之所由分也夫子雖未明言而意已寓予能發之可以占為政矣〕
聖人告賢者為政當戒夫近小而必申言其弊
焉蓋為政當以遠大為期也苟務近小則各有
其弊矣可不以是為戒哉子夏問政聖人告之
意謂為政之道遲速之間而通塞攸係大小之
判而成不成所關予之宰莒父也可不審其初
punctuated:
第壹場

四書

「無欲速，無見小利。欲速則不達，見小利則大事不成。」

陳德文

同考試官教諭馬批〔題本簡易明白，作者詞多重複。此篇數言即了其義，授之以政，必能達者。〕

同考試官教諭黃批〔聖人告子夏之言，正為政者所當戒，此作得之。〕

同考試官教諭潘批〔隱括政體，得夫子言外之意。〕

考試官教授吳批〔辭不繁而意自足，錄之。〕

考試官教授王批〔遲速小大之間，王伯之所由分也。夫子雖未明言，而意已寓，予能發之，可以占為政矣。〕

聖人告賢者為政，當戒夫近小，而必申言其弊焉。蓋為政當以遠大為期也，苟務近小，則各有其弊矣，可不以是為戒哉？子夏問政，聖人告之，意謂為政之道，遲速之間而通塞攸係，大小之判而成不成所關。予之宰莒父也，可不審其初

First Session

Four Books

“Do not seek quick results; do not look to small gains. Seeking quick results prevents attainment; looking to small gains prevents great undertakings from being accomplished.”

Chen Dewen

Associate Examiner Ma, Instructor, comments: 〔The topic is inherently simple and clear, yet writers often repeat themselves. This essay conveys its meaning completely in a few words. Entrusted with government, its author would surely prove capable of accomplishing his aims.〕

Associate Examiner Huang, Instructor, comments: 〔The sage’s words to Zixia express precisely what those who govern must guard against. This composition grasps this.〕

Associate Examiner Pan, Instructor, comments: 〔It encapsulates the essentials of government and grasps what the Master meant beyond his explicit words.〕

Examiner Wu, Professor, comments: 〔The wording is concise, yet the meaning is complete. Accept it.〕

Examiner Wang, Professor, comments: 〔The distinction between the kingly and hegemonic ways arises from the choice between slow and swift, small and great. Although the Master did not state this explicitly, the meaning is already implicit. I can bring it out [?]; from this one may judge the author’s capacity to govern.〕

The sage instructed a worthy man that, in governing, he should guard against pursuing the immediate and the small, and necessarily elaborated upon their harmful consequences. For government should aim at what is far-reaching and great. If one pursues the immediate and the small, each has its attendant harm. Can one fail to take warning from this? Zixia asked about government, and the sage instructed him. His meaning was that, in the way of governing, progress or obstruction hinges on the choice between slow and swift, while accomplishment or failure depends upon the distinction between great and small. As I serve as administrator of Jufu [?], can I fail to examine matters carefully at their outset …

title: 嘉靖四年江西鄉試錄
text:
而致其決乎是故順事恕施政之序也銳於進
者未免乘之以躁心則計功於建立之始而責
效於旦夕之期矣爾爲政也必須之以從容持
之以悠久無以欲速累其心可焉訏謨遠猷政
之體也狃於利者未免局之以狹量則法制畫
於粗定而治化止于小康矣爾爲政也必宏遠
其規模廣大其事業無以小利動其心可焉何
也蓋欲速而能達無不可也夫惟欲速則推行
無漸或限於時勢之難通急遽無倫將阻于施
===
爲之弗達推之有不準也動之有不化也蓋操
之無漸而行之愈礙矣其何以欲速爲哉見小
利而無害于大猶之可也夫惟見小利則志願
易盈化不至于廣被怠荒易作澤不可以遠施
舉目而遺其綱也事末而忘其本也蓋所得者
小而所失者大矣其何以見小利爲哉苟能以
是爲戒則不速而自速舉大以該小矣否則莒
父且不可爲而況天下乎大抵天下之道二公
私而已矣蓋公則通而溥私則塞而隘此固治
punctuated:
而致其決乎？是故，順事恕施，政之序也。銳於進者，未免乘之以躁心，則計功於建立之始，而責效於旦夕之期矣。爾爲政也，必須之以從容，持之以悠久，無以欲速累其心，可焉。訏謨遠猷，政之體也。狃於利者，未免局之以狹量，則法制畫於粗定，而治化止于小康矣。爾爲政也，必宏遠其規模，廣大其事業，無以小利動其心，可焉。何也？蓋欲速而能達，無不可也。夫惟欲速，則推行無漸，或限於時勢之難通；急遽無倫，將阻于施爲之弗達。推之有不準也，動之有不化也。蓋操之無漸，而行之愈礙矣，其何以欲速爲哉？見小利而無害于大，猶之可也。夫惟見小利，則志願易盈，化不至于廣被；怠荒易作，澤不可以遠施。舉目而遺其綱也，事末而忘其本也。蓋所得者小，而所失者大矣，其何以見小利爲哉？苟能以是爲戒，則不速而自速，舉大以該小矣。否則，莒父且不可爲，而況天下乎？
大抵天下之道二，公私而已矣。蓋公則通而溥，私則塞而隘，此固治
translation_en:
…and reach a firm decision about it? Thus, proceeding in accordance with circumstances and acting with consideration for others constitute the proper sequence of government. Those eager to advance inevitably allow impatience to take hold: they reckon achievements when their undertakings have only just begun and demand results within a day. In governing, you must allow matters to develop unhurriedly and sustain your efforts over the long term. Do not let the desire for speed burden your mind; then you will do well. Grand plans and far-reaching designs constitute the essential substance of government. Those habituated to seeking profit inevitably become confined by narrow-mindedness: their laws and institutions go no further than a rough establishment, and their governance and transforming influence stop at modest well-being. In governing, you must make your plans broad and far-reaching and your undertakings extensive. Do not let small gains stir your mind; then you will do well. Why is this? If one could desire speed and still attain one's ends, there would be nothing wrong with it. But precisely because one desires speed, implementation lacks gradual stages and may be constrained by circumstances that are difficult to overcome. Haste has no orderly sequence, and action will be obstructed, failing to attain its ends. What one puts into practice may fail to conform to proper standards, and those one moves to action may fail to be transformed. Because one's handling of affairs lacks gradual stages, carrying them out becomes ever more obstructed. What use, then, is the desire for speed? To attend to small gains without harming larger concerns would still be acceptable. But precisely because one attends to small gains, one's aspirations are easily satisfied, and one's transforming influence fails to spread widely. Negligence readily arises, and one's beneficence cannot extend far. This is to lift the meshes of a net while neglecting its main cord, to attend to the branches while forgetting the root. What one gains is small, while what one loses is great. What use, then, is attending to small gains? If you can take these things as warnings, you will achieve speed naturally without hurrying, and encompass the small by taking up the great. Otherwise, you will be unable even to govern Jufu 莒父, much less all under Heaven!
Broadly speaking, there are two ways in the world: public-mindedness and self-interest, nothing more. Public-mindedness leads to openness and breadth; self-interest leads to obstruction and narrowness. This is indeed, in governing…

title: 嘉靖四年江西鄉試錄
text:
道上下之所以分亦天下國家之所由以治亂
者也夫子譏管仲之器小而曾西亦鄙其卑陋
而不爲者正以其急功利而無公天下之志耳
夫子告子夏之言雖爲一邑之政而王伯之辨
實肪於此聖人之言而上下小大之皆通者其
此類歟
肫肫其仁淵淵其淵浩浩其天
魏良政
同考試官教諭許　批〔見理明瑩措詞峻潔　湯中乃〕
有逆作乎
===
同考試官教諭朱　批〔讀此有難題易作之意〕
考試官教授吳　批〔作中庸義立意純潔措詞莊　重宜錄以式〕
考試官教授王　批〔揭書出題非以困士作者往　往與經綸立本知化三句同至不可辨剝此無他取其精〕
切而已
至誠功用之各極其盛所以爲天道也蓋德極
其誠則功用極其盛宜〔然〕非聖人天道之極
punctuated:
道上下之所以分，亦天下國家之所由以治亂者也。夫子譏管仲之器小，而曾西亦鄙其卑陋而不爲者，正以其急功利而無公天下之志耳。夫子告子夏之言，雖爲一邑之政，而王伯之辨實肪於此。聖人之言而上下小大之皆通者，其此類歟？

肫肫其仁，淵淵其淵，浩浩其天。
魏良政

同考試官教諭許，批〔見理明瑩，措詞峻潔。湯中乃〕有逆作乎？
同考試官教諭朱，批〔讀此有難題易作之意。〕
考試官教授吳，批〔作中庸義，立意純潔，措詞莊重，宜錄以式。〕
考試官教授王，批〔揭書出題，非以困士。作者往往與經綸、立本、知化三句同，至不可辨。剝此無他，取其精〕切而已。

至誠功用之各極其盛，所以爲天道也。蓋德極其誠，則功用極其盛，宜〔然〕。非聖人天道之極
translation_en:
…the distinction between higher and lower ways of governing, and also that upon which order and disorder in the realm and its states depend. The Master criticized Guan Zhong for his limited capacity, while Zeng Xi likewise disdained his baseness and would not emulate him, precisely because he pursued quick achievements and profit and lacked the aspiration to serve the realm impartially. Although the Master's words to Zixia concerned the government of a single town, the distinction between true kingship and hegemony is indeed grounded here [?]. Are these not an example of the sage's words applying alike to higher and lower, great and small?

“Most earnest is his benevolence; unfathomable is his depth; vast is his Heaven.”
By Wei Liangzheng.

Associate Examiner Xu, Instructor, comments: 〔“His understanding of principle is clear and luminous; his wording is forceful and polished. Tang Zhong then [?]〕—could there be a composition proceeding in reverse [?]?”
Associate Examiner Zhu, Instructor, comments: 〔“Reading this gives the impression that a difficult topic is easy to write on.”〕
Examiner Wu, Professor, comments: 〔“In expounding the meaning of the Doctrine of the Mean, his conception is pure and his wording dignified. It should be recorded as a model.”〕
Examiner Wang, Professor, comments: 〔“Selecting a passage from the book as a topic is not intended to confound the candidates. Writers often treat this topic just like the three clauses concerning ordering human relations, establishing the foundation, and understanding transformation, until the treatments cannot be distinguished. In selecting this [?], there is no other consideration: we value its precision〕and aptness alone.”

That the workings of utmost sincerity each attain their fullest flourishing is what makes them the Way of Heaven. For when virtue reaches the utmost sincerity, its workings naturally attain their fullest flourishing. Were it not for the sage's supreme attainment of the Way of Heaven…

title: 嘉靖四年江西鄉試錄
text:
致惡足以語此哉吾想子思子立言之意謂夫
至誠之功用既皆出於自然矣而有不極其盛
哉人知至誠之經綸也而不知經綸即仁也所
以貫乎五品之人倫也因其天性而恩無不篤
本諸人情而愛無不周其合也心之無私也其
分也理之各當也覆天下而澤後世油然而感
人心之同而皆其仁也何肫肫乎人知至誠之
立本也而不知立本即淵也所以涵乎所性之
全體也天理流行莫非其深微之德人欲淨盡
===
悉皆其湛一之真放之準者有其本也資之深
者逢其原也妙衆理而神萬物寂然而通天下
之故而皆其淵也何淵淵乎人知至誠之知化
也而不知知化即天也所以超於聞見之不及
也命之不已者運之於虛明之中體之不遺者
受之於廣大之地成位乎中而不見其不足昭
假于下而不謂之不倖太極全而陰陽合於穆
而為不顯之機而無非天也何浩浩乎是則經
綸立本知化而妙其功矣其仁其淵其天而極
punctuated: 致，惡足以語此哉！吾想子思子立言之意，謂夫至誠之功用既皆出於自然矣，而有不極其盛哉？人知至誠之經綸也，而不知經綸即仁也。所以貫乎五品之人倫也，因其天性而恩無不篤，本諸人情而愛無不周。其合也，心之無私也；其分也，理之各當也。覆天下而澤後世，油然而感人心之同，而皆其仁也，何肫肫乎！人知至誠之立本也，而不知立本即淵也。所以涵乎所性之全體也，天理流行，莫非其深微之德；人欲淨盡，悉皆其湛一之真。放之準者，有其本也；資之深者，逢其原也。妙衆理而神萬物，寂然而通天下之故，而皆其淵也，何淵淵乎！人知至誠之知化也，而不知知化即天也。所以超於聞見之不及也，命之不已者，運之於虛明之中；體之不遺者，受之於廣大之地。成位乎中而不見其不足，昭假于下而不謂之不倖。太極全而陰陽合，於穆而為不顯之機，而無非天也，何浩浩乎！是則經綸、立本、知化而妙其功矣，其仁、其淵、其天而極
translation_en:
…culmination—how could one otherwise speak of this? I imagine that Master Zisi’s intention in setting forth these words was this: since the workings of utmost sincerity all arise spontaneously, could any fail to attain their fullest flourishing?

People know that utmost sincerity orders and regulates, but do not know that this ordering and regulating is itself benevolence. It thereby permeates the five human relationships. Following their natural endowments, it leaves no kindness less than heartfelt; grounded in human feelings, it leaves no one beyond the reach of its love. In bringing them together, it manifests the mind’s impartiality; in distinguishing them, it accords each principle its proper place. It shelters all under Heaven and bestows blessings upon later generations, spontaneously stirring what human hearts share in common. All this is its benevolence. How earnest and sincere it is!

People know that utmost sincerity establishes the foundation, but do not know that establishing the foundation is itself profundity. It thereby embraces the entirety of one’s endowed nature. Wherever heavenly principle flows, there is nothing that is not its profound and subtle virtue; when selfish human desires are entirely purified away, everything is its limpid, undivided authenticity. That it remains the standard wherever extended is because it has its foundation; that one draws deeply upon it is because one encounters its source. It wondrously encompasses all principles and works spiritually through the myriad things. Though still, it comprehends the causes of all affairs under Heaven. All this is its profundity. How deep and unfathomable it is!

People know that utmost sincerity understands transformation, but do not know that understanding transformation is itself Heaven. It thereby transcends what hearing and sight cannot reach. Heaven’s unceasing mandate operates within its emptiness and clarity; what it embodies without omission is received within its breadth and greatness. It takes its proper position in the midst of Heaven and Earth, without showing any inadequacy; it shines forth and reaches below, and is not said to be without good fortune [?]. The Supreme Ultimate is whole, and yin and yang unite. Profound and reverent, it constitutes the subtle impulse of what remains unseen. None of this is other than Heaven. How vast it is!

Thus, in ordering and regulating, establishing the foundation, and understanding transformation, its efficacy is wondrous; in its benevolence, its profundity, and its Heaven-like character, it reaches the utmost…

title: 嘉靖四年江西鄉試錄
text:
其贊矣非天下之至誠其孰能有之而非天下
之至聖其孰知之哉抑論上言至聖之德分其
屬而言也所以爲小德之川流也此言至誠之
道合其本而言也所以爲大德之敦化也其實
一也所以皆天道也由是觀之君子之學析之
不可以不精而合之不可以不大析之精則爲
其大者益力合之大則爲其精者益盡其要在
於誠之而已
滄浪之水清兮可以濯我纓滄浪之水濁
兮可以濯我足孔子曰小子聽之淸斯
濯纓濁斯濯足矣自取之也
===
周麟
同考試官訓導吳　批　〔古有滄浪之歌孺子偶述而歌之耳非歌於滄浪之上也作者尋源遡流恐失本旨此〕
〔篇斟酌輕重詞達意暢講段數語令人灑然〕
同考試官訓導張　批　講有取處甚明快可錄
考試官教授吳　批　〔題本枯淡而意在言外此作詞能達意且有悟於聽者不覺色潤入刻之〕
punctuated:
其贊矣。非天下之至誠，其孰能有之？而非天下之至聖，其孰知之哉？抑論上言至聖之德，分其屬而言也，所以爲小德之川流也；此言至誠之道，合其本而言也，所以爲大德之敦化也。其實一也，所以皆天道也。由是觀之，君子之學，析之不可以不精，而合之不可以不大。析之精，則爲其大者益力；合之大，則爲其精者益盡。其要在於誠之而已。
滄浪之水清兮，可以濯我纓；滄浪之水濁兮，可以濯我足。孔子曰：「小子聽之！淸斯濯纓，濁斯濯足矣，自取之也。」
周麟
同考試官訓導吳　批：〔古有滄浪之歌，孺子偶述而歌之耳，非歌於滄浪之上也。作者尋源遡流，恐失本旨。此〕〔篇斟酌輕重，詞達意暢，講段數語，令人灑然。〕
同考試官訓導張　批：講有取處，甚明快，可錄。
考試官教授吳　批：〔題本枯淡，而意在言外。此作詞能達意，且有悟於聽者，不覺色潤，入刻之。〕
translation_en:
…and the praise of him reaches its utmost. Who but one of the utmost sincerity in all the world could possess these qualities? And who but the utmost sage in all the world could recognize them? To consider the matter further: the preceding passage speaks of the virtue of the utmost sage by distinguishing its various aspects; hence it describes the lesser virtues flowing like streams. This passage speaks of the Way of utmost sincerity by uniting its fundamental principles; hence it describes the greater virtue bringing about abundant transformation. In reality, they are one, and thus both are the Way of Heaven. Viewed in this light, the gentleman’s learning must be precise in its analysis and comprehensive in its synthesis. The more precise the analysis, the greater the effort devoted to comprehensiveness; the more comprehensive the synthesis, the more fully precision is attained. The essential point lies simply in making oneself sincere.
“When the waters of the Canglang are clear, I can wash my cap-strings in them; when the waters of the Canglang are muddy, I can wash my feet in them.” Confucius said: “Listen to this, my young disciples! When clear, they serve to wash cap-strings; when muddy, they serve to wash feet. They bring this treatment upon themselves.”
Zhou Lin
Comment by Associate Examiner Wu, an Assistant Instructor: 〔The Song of the Canglang existed in antiquity; the boy merely happened to repeat it in song. He was not singing on the banks of the Canglang. Writers who seek its source and trace its course risk missing the original meaning. This〕〔essay weighs the relative importance of its points carefully; its wording conveys the meaning, and its ideas flow freely. The few phrases in the explanatory section leave the reader refreshed.〕
Comment by Associate Examiner Zhang, an Assistant Instructor: The exposition has commendable points. It is very clear and brisk, and merits inclusion.
Comment by Examiner Wu, an Instructor: 〔The topic itself is dry and plain, but its meaning lies beyond the words. The wording of this essay conveys that meaning and also brings insight to those who hear it; imperceptibly, it acquires color and richness. Include it in the woodblock edition.〕

title: 嘉靖四年江西鄉試錄
text:
考試官教授王　批〔發明孟子戒當時之意令人〕
警省
大賢述孺子詠物以適其情聖人聞言而發其
理其警當時之意深矣蓋事變未有無故而至
者也即聖人有取於孺子之歌則不仁之禍夫
豈由於人哉昔孟子論不仁之不可與言至此
蓋謂禍福無自來之理在人有感召之幾獨不
觀孺子之歌與孔子之言乎彼孺子之歌曰滄
浪之水有清者焉本源未撓而靜深澄徹則可
===
就之而濯我之纓滌舊染而爲新渾然物我之
一體也滄浪之水有濁者焉蒙泉已汩而沸潰
溷淆則可以之而濯我之足去積汙而自潔悠
然內外之兩忘也孺子因物感興於順適之餘
聖人聲入心通於言意之表乃呼門人而謂之
曰至理不遺於小物恒情多忽於邇言孺子之
歌小子其聽之哉夫惟水之清而不可以輕用
也斯以之而濯纓夫惟水之濁而不可以遂棄
也斯以之而濯足以水之清而自得其濯之貴
punctuated:
考試官教授王批〔發明孟子戒當時之意，令人〕警省。

大賢述孺子詠物以適其情，聖人聞言而發其理，其警當時之意深矣。蓋事變未有無故而至者也，即聖人有取於孺子之歌，則不仁之禍，夫豈由於人哉？昔孟子論不仁之不可與言，至此蓋謂禍福無自來之理，在人有感召之幾。獨不觀孺子之歌與孔子之言乎？彼孺子之歌曰：「滄浪之水有清者焉，本源未撓而靜深澄徹，則可就之而濯我之纓，滌舊染而爲新，渾然物我之一體也。滄浪之水有濁者焉，蒙泉已汩而沸潰溷淆，則可以之而濯我之足，去積汙而自潔，悠然內外之兩忘也。」孺子因物感興於順適之餘，聖人聲入心通於言意之表，乃呼門人而謂之曰：「至理不遺於小物，恒情多忽於邇言。孺子之歌，小子其聽之哉！夫惟水之清而不可以輕用也，斯以之而濯纓；夫惟水之濁而不可以遂棄也，斯以之而濯足。以水之清而自得其濯之貴，
translation_en:
Examiner Wang, Professor, comments: 〔“Elucidates Mencius’s intention to admonish his contemporaries, prompting readers〕 to take warning and reflect.”

The great worthy recounted how a boy sang of things to give expression to his feelings, and how the sage, hearing his words, brought out their underlying principle. Profound indeed was his intention to admonish his contemporaries. For no change in circumstances ever comes about without a cause. Given that even the sage found something worth adopting in the boy’s song, how could the calamities attending inhumaneness be attributed to other people? When Mencius, discussing why one cannot reason with the inhumane, reached this point, his meaning was that neither misfortune nor good fortune comes of itself: the impulse that calls it forth lies in the person. Have we not considered the boy’s song and Confucius’s words?

The boy’s song says: “When the waters of Canglang are clear, their source undisturbed, still, deep, and limpid, I can approach them and wash my cap strings, cleansing away old stains and making them new. Things and self blend into a single whole. When the waters of Canglang are muddy, the issuing spring already disturbed, surging, spilling, and turbid, I can use them to wash my feet, removing accumulated dirt and cleansing myself. At ease, I forget both what is within and what is without.”

The boy drew inspiration from what he encountered, in a mood of ease and contentment. As the sounds reached the sage, his mind grasped what lay beyond the words and their expressed meaning. He therefore called his disciples and said: “The highest principle is not absent from small things, yet ordinary people often overlook familiar sayings. Young men, listen to the boy’s song! Because the water is clear and should not be used carelessly, one uses it to wash cap strings; because the water is muddy yet should not simply be discarded, one uses it to wash feet. Through its clarity, the water itself obtains the more honorable use in washing …

title: 嘉靖四年江西鄉試錄
text:
初無心於纓也亦無心於水也物理之相値者
有推之而不得者矣使有時而濁焉安知不以
之而濯足乎以水之濁而自得乎濯之賤初何
心於水也亦何心於足也氣類之相應若有避
之而不能者矣使有時而清焉安知不以之而
濯纓乎夫此一滄浪也唯其有清濁之殊是以
有致用之異人非不仁禍亦何由而至哉大抵
禍固以不仁而致也有能去不仁而求仁亦可
以轉其禍而爲福太甲之興也以桐秦穆之將
===
也以殽檇李勝吳會稽强越其明驗也戰國之
君私欲蔽固皆不能去禍以求福其終於敗亡
也固宜孔孟自取之言其亦重有感也夫
易
貞固足以幹事
歐陽塾
同考試官教諭馬　批〔他卷講貞固幹事處語多重複是篇說理詳明措詞簡當錄之以式多士〕
同考試官教諭黃　批〔幹事處體認明白是可以語〕
punctuated:
初無心於纓也，亦無心於水也。物理之相値者，有推之而不得者矣。使有時而濁焉，安知不以之而濯足乎？以水之濁而自得乎濯之賤，初何心於水也，亦何心於足也？氣類之相應，若有避之而不能者矣。使有時而清焉，安知不以之而濯纓乎？夫此一滄浪也，唯其有清濁之殊，是以有致用之異。人非不仁，禍亦何由而至哉？大抵禍固以不仁而致也，有能去不仁而求仁，亦可以轉其禍而爲福。太甲之興也以桐，秦穆之將也以殽，檇李勝吳，會稽强越，其明驗也。戰國之君，私欲蔽固，皆不能去禍以求福，其終於敗亡也固宜。孔孟自取之言，其亦重有感也夫！

易
貞固足以幹事。
歐陽塾

同考試官教諭馬，批〔他卷講貞固幹事處，語多重複。是篇說理詳明，措詞簡當，錄之以式多士。〕

同考試官教諭黃，批〔幹事處體認明白，是可以語〕
translation_en:
…There was initially no deliberate concern for the cap strings, nor for the water. When the inherent principles of things coincide, their conjunction cannot always be rejected. If the water should at some time become muddy, how can we know that it would not be used to wash feet? When muddy water finds its fitting use in the humble task of washing feet, what deliberate concern was there initially for the water, or for the feet? The mutual response of things of kindred vital energies seems impossible to evade. If the water should at some time become clear, how can we know that it would not be used to wash cap strings? This is the very same Canglang River: only because its water differs in clarity and muddiness does its use differ. If a person were not inhumane, by what means could calamity come upon him? Generally, calamity is indeed brought about by inhumanity. Yet anyone able to abandon inhumanity and seek humaneness can also turn calamity into good fortune. Tai Jia’s restoration arose from his stay at Tong; Duke Mu of Qin’s advancement [?] arose from Xiao. Zuili brought victory to Wu, and Kuaiji strengthened Yue: these are clear proofs. The rulers of the Warring States were blinded and entrenched in their selfish desires, unable to cast off calamity and seek good fortune. It was indeed fitting that they ultimately met defeat and destruction. Surely the words of Confucius and Mencius about bringing things upon oneself were also prompted by profound feeling!

Book of Changes
“Correctness and firmness suffice to manage affairs.”
Ouyang Shu

Associate Examiner Ma, Instructor, comments: “In discussing correctness and firmness and the management of affairs, the other papers are often repetitive. This essay explains the principles fully and clearly, and its wording is concise and apt. It is included to serve as a model for the many candidates.”

Associate Examiner Huang, Instructor, comments: “Its understanding of the passage on managing affairs is clear. With this person one can discuss …”

title: 嘉靖四年江西鄉試錄
text:
易矣
同考試官教諭潘　批〔易義類能言之求其深淨精〕
〔微者無踰此篇〕
考試官教授吳　批〔非精于易者不能故錄〕
考試官教授王　批〔得文言之旨〕
文言論君子全夫智之德則事無不立矣甚矣
智一天下之動也君子知正而固守之則智之
德全矣事豈不依之而立哉文言申乾彖傳之
意及此謂夫天之四德有所謂貞也于人則爲
===
智焉君子何以能全之邪誠以正本於天命之
微知之而能守者寡矣君子則心體虛明于惕
厲之餘於凡正理之渾然者而固守之不移發
于人道之著守之而能固者鮮矣君子則義理
昭融于進修之後於凡正理之燦然者而服膺
之弗失介豫之石不以久暫而或殊所謂利居
貞者有巳秉晋之昭不以順逆而或異所謂大
居正者是巳夫君子之貞固如此吾知中無定
見者事多眩惑也今則以正爲之依據而泛應
punctuated:
易矣。
同考試官教諭潘，批〔易義類能言之，求其深淨精〕〔微者，無踰此篇〕。
考試官教授吳，批〔非精于易者不能，故錄〕。
考試官教授王，批〔得文言之旨〕。
文言論君子全夫智之德，則事無不立矣。甚矣，智一天下之動也！君子知正而固守之，則智之德全矣，事豈不依之而立哉？文言申乾彖傳之意，及此謂夫天之四德有所謂貞也，于人則爲智焉。君子何以能全之邪？誠以正本於天命之微，知之而能守者寡矣。君子則心體虛明于惕厲之餘，於凡正理之渾然者，而固守之不移；發于人道之著，守之而能固者鮮矣。君子則義理昭融于進修之後，於凡正理之燦然者，而服膺之弗失。介豫之石，不以久暫而或殊，所謂利居貞者有巳；秉晋之昭，不以順逆而或異，所謂大居正者是巳。夫君子之貞固如此，吾知中無定見者，事多眩惑也。今則以正爲之依據，而泛應
translation_en:
…the Book of Changes.

Associate Examiner Pan, Instructor, comments: 〔Most can discuss the meaning of the Changes, but for depth, clarity, refinement〕〔and subtlety, none surpasses this essay.〕

Examiner Wu, Professor, comments: 〔Only someone thoroughly versed in the Changes could accomplish this; hence its inclusion.〕

Examiner Wang, Professor, comments: 〔It grasps the purport of the Commentary on the Words of the Text.〕

The Commentary on the Words of the Text explains that when the gentleman perfects the virtue of wisdom, there is no undertaking he cannot establish. How profound is wisdom’s power to unify all activity under Heaven! When the gentleman knows what is right and holds firmly to it, the virtue of wisdom is complete. How could undertakings fail to find their support in this and become established? The Commentary on the Words of the Text develops the meaning of the Commentary on the Judgment for Qian. At this point it says that among Heaven’s four virtues is what is called steadfast correctness; in human beings, this becomes wisdom. How can the gentleman perfect it? Truly, rightness has its root in the subtle workings of Heaven’s mandate, and few who know it can hold to it. Through vigilance and caution, the gentleman’s mind becomes empty and luminous; he holds unwaveringly to right principle in its undivided entirety. Rightness manifests itself in the evident workings of the human Way, yet few who hold to it can remain firm. Through advancing in learning and cultivating himself, the gentleman comes to comprehend moral principles with luminous clarity; he takes all the brilliant manifestations of right principle to heart and never loses them. Firm as the rock in Yu [Enthusiasm], he does not vary with the length or brevity of the time: this is what is meant by ‘it is beneficial to remain steadfastly correct’ [?]. Holding to the brightness of Jin [Advance], he does not change with favorable or adverse circumstances: this is what is meant by ‘what is great is to abide in correctness.’ Such is the gentleman’s steadfast correctness and firmness. I know that those who lack settled discernment within are often bewildered in their undertakings. Now, however, he takes rightness as his basis and responds to every circumstance…

title: 嘉靖四年江西鄉試錄
text:
有曲當之妙素無定守者事多叢脞也今則以
正爲之憑籍而施爲無凝滯之虞事有是非也
正以立之而卓乎其有本猶長短之依乎度也
事有常變也正以植之而秩乎其有序猶輕重
之依乎權也是豈不足以爲事之幹也哉是何
也天下無正外之理亦無理外之事一正立而
萬事隨之君子體乾之功如是則天德之貞不
在天而在君子矣抑乾之德大矣故易于乾必
以天道聖人明之而此則言君子何也蓋非天
道無以盡乾非聖人無以配乾非君子則亦無
以體乾也君子體乾之德猶夫乾焉則一聖人
一天而已矣周子曰賢希聖聖希天其此之謂
歟然非至健則亦莫之能也已故曰君子以自
彊不息
有大者不可以盈故受之以謙有大而能
謙必豫故受之以豫
===
===
同考試官教諭馬　批
賀謹徐
序卦題明緒多端且甚對而
punctuated:
有曲當之妙。素無定守者，事多叢脞也；今則以正爲之憑籍，而施爲無凝滯之虞。事有是非也，正以立之，而卓乎其有本，猶長短之依乎度也；事有常變也，正以植之，而秩乎其有序，猶輕重之依乎權也。是豈不足以爲事之幹也哉？是何也？天下無正外之理，亦無理外之事。一正立，而萬事隨之。君子體乾之功如是，則天德之貞不在天，而在君子矣。抑乾之德大矣，故易于乾必以天道聖人明之，而此則言君子，何也？蓋非天道無以盡乾，非聖人無以配乾，非君子則亦無以體乾也。君子體乾之德，猶夫乾焉，則一聖人、一天而已矣。周子曰：「賢希聖，聖希天。」其此之謂歟？然非至健，則亦莫之能也已。故曰：「君子以自彊不息。」

有大者不可以盈，故受之以謙；有大而能謙，必豫，故受之以豫。

同考試官教諭馬　批
賀謹徐
序卦題，明緒多端，且甚對而
translation_en:
…there is the subtle excellence of responding fittingly to every particular. Those who ordinarily lack a steadfast commitment are often disordered in their affairs; now, however, taking correctness as their support, they need not fear obstruction or stagnation in their actions. Affairs involve right and wrong: establish them through correctness, and they stand firmly grounded, just as lengths depend upon a measure. Affairs involve both regular circumstances and changes: root them in correctness, and they fall into orderly arrangement, just as weights depend upon a balance. Is this not sufficient to make correctness the supporting trunk of affairs? Why is this so? Under Heaven there is no principle outside correctness, nor any affair outside principle. Once correctness is established, the myriad affairs follow it. If the gentleman’s achievement in embodying Qian is such, then the steadfast correctness of Heaven’s virtue resides not in Heaven but in the gentleman.

Yet the virtue of Qian is great. Thus, in treating Qian, the Book of Changes invariably elucidates it through the Way of Heaven and the sage. Why, then, does this passage speak of the gentleman? Without the Way of Heaven, Qian cannot be fully expressed; without the sage, nothing can match Qian; and without the gentleman, Qian cannot be embodied. When the gentleman embodies Qian’s virtue and becomes like Qian itself, he is simply a sage, a Heaven. Master Zhou said, “The worthy aspires to sagehood; the sage aspires to Heaven.” Is this not what he meant? Yet without utmost vigor, no one can accomplish this. Hence it is said, “The gentleman thereby strengthens himself without ceasing.”

“One who possesses greatness must not become full of himself; therefore it is followed by Qian [Modesty]. Possessing greatness yet being capable of modesty necessarily brings ease; therefore it is followed by Yu [Ease].”

Comment by Associate Examiner Ma, Instructor.
He Jinxu 賀謹徐 [?].
For a topic drawn from the Sequence of the Hexagrams, the lines of exposition are manifold [?], and it is very well matched [?], yet…

title: 嘉靖四年江西鄉試錄
text:
文不僅作者甚難考者亦難矣若不為所穿鑿之
同考試官教諭黃　批〔此篇攷據之通分析明白他日以此致用必有大過人者尚勉旃〕
同考試官教諭潘　批〔此題甚有關世道子之文足以發之亦有補於鳴世者〕
考試官教授吳　批〔語不浮而意實相承善作序卦文字者〕
考試官教授王　批〔講不可盈數語讀之令人惕然〕
===
存君道之大戒致治道之益隆卦之所以序也
甚矣君道莫患於自盈也戒以從謙而天下之
治有不益隆者哉夫子傳序卦發明大有謙豫
相承之義若曰恒人之見踈每悔禍於無及聖
人之慮遠必防患於未然何則王帛萬國撫大
統而無虞儲積九年徵太平於有象天下時乎
其大有也有大可樂也亦可憂也人君處此鮮
不因之以自盈者夫君盈而天下之治索矣蓋
好大喜功盈而誇也窮奢極欲盈而侈也流連
punctuated:
文不僅，作者甚難，考者亦難矣。若不為所穿鑿之……
同考試官教諭黃批〔此篇攷據之通，分析明白，他日以此致用，必有大過人者，尚勉旃。〕
同考試官教諭潘批〔此題甚有關世道，子之文足以發之，亦有補於鳴世者。〕
考試官教授吳批〔語不浮而意實相承，善作序卦文字者。〕
考試官教授王批〔講不可盈數語，讀之令人惕然。〕
存君道之大戒，致治道之益隆，卦之所以序也。
甚矣，君道莫患於自盈也！戒以從謙，而天下之治有不益隆者哉？夫子傳《序卦》，發明大有、謙、豫相承之義，若曰：恒人之見踈，每悔禍於無及；聖人之慮遠，必防患於未然。何則？王帛萬國，撫大統而無虞；儲積九年，徵太平於有象。天下時乎其大有也。有大可樂也，亦可憂也。人君處此，鮮不因之以自盈者。夫君盈，而天下之治索矣。蓋好大喜功，盈而誇也；窮奢極欲，盈而侈也；流連……
translation_en:
…The composition is not merely [?]—it is very difficult for its author, and difficult for its examiner as well. If it is not subjected to strained interpretations [?]…
Associate Examiner and Instructor Huang comments: 〔This essay shows thorough command of its textual authorities and clear analysis. If you put this learning to practical use in the future, you will surely have qualities far surpassing others. Continue to exert yourself!〕
Associate Examiner and Instructor Pan comments: 〔This topic has a considerable bearing on the moral order of the world. Your essay adequately elucidates it and also contributes to giving that order a voice in the world.〕
Examiner and Professor Wu comments: 〔The language is not superficial, and the ideas genuinely follow one another. This is someone skilled at composing essays on the Sequence of the Hexagrams.〕
Examiner and Professor Wang comments: 〔The few phrases explaining why one must not become self-satisfied make the reader apprehensive and alert.〕
To preserve the great warning governing the ruler’s way, and to bring the way of governance to ever greater flourishing: this is why the hexagrams are arranged in this sequence.
How grave it is! In the ruler’s way, nothing is more dangerous than self-satisfaction. If he takes warning and follows humility, how could order throughout the realm fail to flourish further? In his commentary, the Sequence of the Hexagrams, the Master elucidates the meaning of Great Possession, Modesty, and Enthusiasm succeeding one another. It is as though he said: ordinary people’s perception is deficient, and they often regret disaster when it is too late; the sage’s foresight reaches far, and he invariably guards against trouble before it arises. Why is this? Ruling the myriad states [?], he presides over the great imperial succession without anxiety; with provisions accumulated for nine years, he finds tangible evidence of great peace. The realm is then in its season of Great Possession. Great possessions are a cause for joy, but also a cause for concern. Few rulers in such circumstances do not consequently become self-satisfied. Yet when the ruler becomes self-satisfied, order throughout the realm declines. For delighting in grand undertakings and craving achievements is self-satisfaction expressed as boastfulness; exhausting the possibilities of luxury and indulging desire to the utmost is self-satisfaction expressed as extravagance; lingering on…

title: 嘉靖四年江西鄉試錄
text:
荒亡怠且危也恃厥有而喪厥有矣如之何其
可哉此大有之後所以必受之以謙也謙者有
而不居之謂也盛滿之戒不於斯而見乎民生
已遂如傷之視方深王道大行不顯之敬愈篤
有大而能謙如此也此君之美也亦民之福也
人君持此未必望之以由豫者然君謙而天下
之和應矣蓋刑清民服豫之昭也作樂崇德豫
之暢也雍熙太和盛以極也感於上而應於下
矣有不可必之理哉此謙卦之後所以必受之
===
以豫也豫者人心和樂以應其上也謙德之終
不於斯而徵乎吁人君不以天下之樂私其身
而天下之民將亦不使吾君終於戚矣相須之
殷有如此哉大抵人君一心關天下之理亂而
敬肆之間存否係之不可不謹也故一少康也
始敗而終成一明宗也先治而後亂何也一臨
難而知懼一既濟而心懈故也周公無逸之作
貽萬世君天下之心法乎成王克終保文武於
不衰者公之力也公固深於易者也
punctuated:
荒亡，怠且危也，恃厥有而喪厥有矣，如之何其可哉？此大有之後所以必受之以謙也。謙者，有而不居之謂也。盛滿之戒，不於斯而見乎？民生已遂，如傷之視方深；王道大行，不顯之敬愈篤。有大而能謙如此也，此君之美也，亦民之福也。人君持此，未必望之以由豫者，然君謙而天下之和應矣。蓋刑清民服，豫之昭也；作樂崇德，豫之暢也；雍熙太和，盛以極也。感於上而應於下矣，有不可必之理哉？此謙卦之後所以必受之以豫也。豫者，人心和樂以應其上也。謙德之終，不於斯而徵乎？吁！人君不以天下之樂私其身，而天下之民將亦不使吾君終於戚矣。相須之殷，有如此哉！
大抵人君一心，關天下之理亂，而敬肆之間，存否係之，不可不謹也。故一少康也，始敗而終成；一明宗也，先治而後亂。何也？一臨難而知懼，一既濟而心懈故也。周公無逸之作，貽萬世君天下之心法乎？成王克終保文武於不衰者，公之力也。公固深於易者也。
translation_en:
…abandonment and dissipation bring negligence and danger. Relying on what he possesses, he loses what he possesses: how could this be acceptable? This is why Great Possession must be followed by Modesty. Modesty means possessing without claiming credit. Is the warning against fullness and excess not apparent here? Though the people's livelihood is already secure, his concern for them, as though they were injured, only deepens; though the kingly Way prevails widely, his reverence even in what is unseen grows still more earnest. Such is possessing greatness while remaining modest. This is the ruler's excellence and also the people's good fortune. A ruler who maintains this disposition may not necessarily expect contentment to result from it; yet when the ruler is modest, harmony throughout the realm responds. Punishments are just and the people submit: this is the manifestation of Contentment. Music is instituted to exalt virtue: this is the full expression of Contentment. Concord, prosperity, and supreme harmony reach the height of flourishing. An influence exerted above elicits a response below: could there be any reason why this should not assuredly follow? This is why the hexagram Modesty must be followed by Contentment. Contentment means that the people's hearts respond to their superior with harmony and joy. Is the ultimate effect of modest virtue not demonstrated here? Ah! If the ruler does not reserve the enjoyment of the realm for himself alone, the people of the realm will likewise not let their ruler end in sorrow. How profound is their mutual dependence!
In general, the ruler's single heart determines whether the realm is ordered or disordered; its preservation or loss depends on the distinction between reverence and heedlessness. He must therefore be vigilant. Thus Shaokang began in defeat but ended in success, whereas Mingzong's reign began in order but ended in disorder. Why? Because the one knew fear when confronting adversity, while the other grew lax at heart once success had been achieved. Was not the Duke of Zhou's composition of Against Idleness a bequest to rulers of the realm for ten thousand generations—a method for governing the heart? That King Cheng was able to preserve the legacy of Kings Wen and Wu to the end without decline was due to the duke's efforts. The duke was indeed profoundly versed in the Book of Changes.

title: 嘉靖四年江西鄉試錄

書
咨汝羲暨和朞三百有六旬有六日以閏
月定四時成歲允釐百工庶績咸熙
江治
同考試官訓導吳　批　〔合天日與月相會之間以置〕
〔閏而後朞自朞歲自歲朔自明有許多道理在場中士子〕
〔類不得其要領故言皆錯雜無章而理反晦此作獨得之〕

同考試官訓導張　批　〔曆數難齊亦難言此作說氣〕
〔朔處明白要是不輕於言者〕
===
考試官教授吳　批　〔文義切當無一浮語足爲程〕
〔式〕
考試官教授王　批　〔檃括傳語成文自然精到〕
聖君總命曆官責以治曆之成功而期以治官
之成效也甚矣天人之相因也術不違天則政
不失時矣孰謂曆成而治有不成哉想昔帝堯
之意以謂治曆者爲治之先務而置閏者造曆
之全功惟汝羲及和也曷既厥心乎哉何則日
punctuated:
書

「咨！汝羲暨和，朞三百有六旬有六日，以閏月定四時，成歲，允釐百工，庶績咸熙。」

江治
