Comment by Examiner Wang, Instructor: 〔The discussion of the interaction between Heaven and humanity is penetrating, precise, and sound.〕 Moreover, a spirit of loyalty [?] overflows beyond the words. Such a level would certainly be difficult to attain without a profound understanding of the principles of government. With scholars like this, something can be accomplished.
Heaven’s intention to issue warnings is manifested in anomalies; the ruler’s actual means of averting anomalies lies in virtue. The coming of calamities and anomalies is indeed a means of perfecting the ruler’s virtue. When he cultivates virtue to dispel anomalies, human affairs are properly ordered and Heaven’s Way proceeds harmoniously. Benevolent and loving intent resides within adversity; the subtlety of this wordless communication can only be answered with the heart. Thus, auspicious signs arriving in abundance may increase my faults, while calamities and anomalies arising repeatedly may serve to augment my capacities where they are deficient [?]. How could one excuse oneself by appealing to fixed patterns and forget the need for fear and apprehension? You gentlemen have issued a policy question concerning calamities and anomalies because it bears directly upon the urgent business of the present day. Reverently perceiving our Emperor’s anxious diligence, you wish to contribute to his sagely virtue.
I have heard that Heaven and humanity share one principle, and that stimulus and response operate through one mechanism. Within the realm of undifferentiated stillness, they communicate with each other. Once the theory of comparison and association [?] became prevalent, the principle uniting Heaven and humanity was contravened; once the teachings of Gan and Shi appeared, the mechanism of stimulus and response was misrepresented.

title: 嘉靖四年江西鄉試錄
text:
殊不知匹夫匹婦猶能召日星之變致雨
雪之災矧人君爲天地民物之主繫四海
休戚之命哉人事之得失陰陽之順逆此
感彼應捷於影響未可以迂遠異勢遽忘
其奉若之道也世儒論災異者家異其傳
人異其說致天道之不明啓人君之不信
乃自謂其術足以探上玄其功足以開后
世其貽害豈淺哉春秋紀災異以爲人事
之感召特以示畏天戒而已公羊作傳已
===
非聖人之意董仲舒又衍其說以著陰陽
論至火災之對專以刑罰不中爲言其失
愈甚真德秀譏其傳會宜矣所可取者天
人三策其庶幾格君之學乎洪範以五行
之變歸之五事之應槩言其理而已穀梁
有傳已非君子所取劉向又廣其說以著
五行傳至以五行五事各分類應蘇老泉
譏其牽强宜矣所可取者條陳封事其庶
幾天道之驗乎當是時夏侯勝京房之輩
punctuated:
殊不知，匹夫匹婦猶能召日星之變，致雨雪之災，矧人君爲天地民物之主，繫四海休戚之命哉！人事之得失，陰陽之順逆，此感彼應，捷於影響，未可以迂遠異勢，遽忘其奉若之道也。世儒論災異者，家異其傳，人異其說，致天道之不明，啓人君之不信，乃自謂其術足以探上玄，其功足以開后世，其貽害豈淺哉！
春秋紀災異，以爲人事之感召，特以示畏天戒而已。公羊作傳，已非聖人之意；董仲舒又衍其說，以著陰陽論，至火災之對，專以刑罰不中爲言，其失愈甚。真德秀譏其傳會，宜矣。所可取者，天人三策，其庶幾格君之學乎？洪範以五行之變歸之五事之應，槩言其理而已。穀梁有傳，已非君子所取；劉向又廣其說，以著五行傳，至以五行五事各分類應，蘇老泉譏其牽强，宜矣。所可取者，條陳封事，其庶幾天道之驗乎？當是時，夏侯勝、京房之輩
translation_en:
They entirely fail to understand that even an ordinary man or woman can call forth anomalies in the sun and stars and bring about disastrous rain and snow. How much more so the ruler, who presides over the people and all things between Heaven and Earth, and on whom depends the weal or woe of all within the Four Seas! Success and failure in human affairs, and the harmonious or contrary workings of yin and yang: a stimulus here evokes a response there more swiftly than a shadow or an echo. One must not hastily forget the way of reverently complying with Heaven on the grounds that these things are remote from one another and operate under different conditions. Among scholars who discuss calamities and anomalies, each school has its own tradition and each person his own explanation. They obscure the Way of Heaven and lead rulers to disbelieve it, yet claim that their methods suffice to fathom Heaven’s mysteries and their achievements to enlighten later ages. Can the harm they leave behind be slight?
The Spring and Autumn Annals records calamities and anomalies as things called forth by human affairs, solely to show that Heaven’s warnings must be held in awe. Gongyang’s commentary already departed from the sage’s intent. Dong Zhongshu further elaborated its explanations to compose his Discourse on Yin and Yang; in his response concerning a disastrous fire, he spoke exclusively of inappropriate punishments, going still further astray. Zhen Dexiu was right to criticize his contrived connections. What deserves approval is his Three Policy Essays on Heaven and Man: do these not approach the learning that serves to rectify the ruler? The Great Plan attributes changes in the Five Phases to their responses to the Five Activities, merely stating the general principle. Guliang’s commentary was already something the gentleman would not accept. Liu Xiang further expanded its explanations to compose his Commentary on the Five Phases, going so far as to classify the Five Phases and Five Activities separately and assign corresponding responses to each. Su Laoquan was right to criticize his strained interpretations. What deserves approval is his itemized exposition in sealed memorials: does this not come close to demonstrating the workings of the Way of Heaven? At that time, men such as Xiahou Sheng and Jing Fang…

title: 嘉靖四年江西鄉試錄
text:
既跡此而騰其說谷永李尋之徒復假此
以濟其姦則又二子之所弗取也至如柳
宗元言受命不于其天至上尊號表復條
陳其瑞應蓋先人事而后天道亦非盡棄
其瑞應也可盡以是非柳耶歐陽脩以不
畏天變爲欺君至讀蜀書以麟鳳龜龍爲
常事蓋王建紀載之謬偶述而誦之耳可
遽以是病歐耶夫諸儒之論說不一則人
君之脩省靡宗至其脩省弗應遂謂天之
===
與人衆不相關而作善之念微矣嘗考論
災祥之理莫過於商書辨脩省之道莫過
于王嘉書曰天道福善禍淫持此以論而
后春秋洪範之理明矣舉以應天以實下
以文執此以往而后董仲舒劉向之說破
矣我
皇上即位以來水旱疊奏於郡國火災再見於
宮闕蓋天心仁愛俾
聖德之成同符五帝蘇功三王而益之雖然人
punctuated:
既跡此而騰其說，谷永、李尋之徒復假此以濟其姦，則又二子之所弗取也。至如柳宗元言受命不于其天，至《上尊號表》復條陳其瑞應，蓋先人事而后天道，亦非盡棄其瑞應也，可盡以是非柳耶？歐陽脩以不畏天變爲欺君，至讀《蜀書》，以麟鳳龜龍爲常事，蓋王建紀載之謬，偶述而誦之耳，可遽以是病歐耶？夫諸儒之論說不一，則人君之脩省靡宗；至其脩省弗應，遂謂天之與人衆不相關，而作善之念微矣。
嘗考論災祥之理，莫過於《商書》；辨脩省之道，莫過于王嘉。《書》曰：「天道福善禍淫。」持此以論，而后《春秋》《洪範》之理明矣。舉以應天以實，下以文，執此以往，而后董仲舒、劉向之說破矣。
我皇上即位以來，水旱疊奏於郡國，火災再見於宮闕，蓋天心仁愛，俾聖德之成同符五帝，蘇功三王而益之。雖然，人
translation_en:
…had already followed this approach and broadcast their theories, while men such as Gu Yong and Li Xun further exploited it to advance their treachery. This, however, was something those two masters themselves would have rejected. As for Liu Zongyuan, he said that receiving the mandate did not depend upon Heaven; yet in his Memorial Presenting an Honorific Title, he again enumerated auspicious responses. He evidently placed human affairs first and Heaven’s Way second, without entirely rejecting auspicious responses. Can this alone justify condemning Liu outright? Ouyang Xiu regarded failure to fear heavenly anomalies as deceiving the ruler; yet, on reading the History of Shu, he treated qilin, phoenixes, tortoises, and dragons as commonplace. These were evidently errors in the records concerning Wang Jian, which he merely happened to recount and recite. Can one hastily fault Ouyang on this basis? When Confucian scholars disagree in their explanations, the ruler has no settled guide for self-cultivation and self-examination. When these efforts elicit no response, he consequently concludes that Heaven and humankind have no connection, and his intention to do good weakens.
I have examined these matters: for discussing the principles of calamities and auspicious signs, nothing surpasses the Documents of Shang; for explaining the way of self-cultivation and self-examination, no one surpasses Wang Jia. The Book of Documents says: “Heaven’s Way blesses the good and brings disaster upon the profligate.” Only by taking this as the basis of discussion can the principles of the Spring and Autumn Annals and the Great Plan become clear. Respond to Heaven with substance, with literary form placed below it [?]. Only by proceeding on this basis can the theories of Dong Zhongshu and Liu Xiang be refuted.
Since our emperor ascended the throne, reports of floods and droughts have repeatedly come from the prefectures and domains, and fires have twice appeared in the imperial palace. Heaven’s intention is surely benevolent and loving: it would bring his sagely virtue to fulfillment in conformity with the Five Emperors, revive the achievements of the Three Kings [?], and surpass them. Nevertheless, human …

title: 嘉靖四年江西鄉試錄
text:
和之世也恭聞
皇上克謹天戒以享天心納群工之言防未萌
之慾
御經筵以求其故
命便殿以思其失省躬之道不可盡述而上
帝昭臨之矣罷無益之工禁無功之賞廣
儲蓄以固其本去無藝以紓其歛立政之
美不可枚舉而下民永賴之矣憂勤之意
豈特遣賑貸之臣下罪己之
===
詔而已哉考之於古商周之時高宗宣王嘗遇
災異矣一則克正厥事一則側身脩行而
雊雉旱魃之變終不足以爲國之妖雖其
中興之美不待警戒而後諭然勵其志而
成其功者謂非災異可乎西漢之時文景
嘗多災異矣一則恭儉自持一則遵業不
改而水旱雨雪之變終不足以爲民之患
雖其安養之久不待于樽節之崇然禁其
慾而防其侈謂非災異可乎即是以觀則
punctuated: 和之世也。恭聞皇上克謹天戒，以享天心，納群工之言，防未萌之慾，御經筵以求其故，命便殿以思其失。省躬之道，不可盡述，而上帝昭臨之矣。罷無益之工，禁無功之賞，廣儲蓄以固其本，去無藝以紓其歛。立政之美，不可枚舉，而下民永賴之矣。憂勤之意，豈特遣賑貸之臣、下罪己之詔而已哉？考之於古，商周之時，高宗、宣王嘗遇災異矣。一則克正厥事，一則側身脩行，而雊雉、旱魃之變，終不足以爲國之妖。雖其中興之美，不待警戒而後諭，然勵其志而成其功者，謂非災異可乎？西漢之時，文、景嘗多災異矣。一則恭儉自持，一則遵業不改，而水旱雨雪之變，終不足以爲民之患。雖其安養之久，不待于樽節之崇，然禁其慾而防其侈，謂非災異可乎？即是以觀，則
translation_en:
…an age of harmony among the people. We have respectfully heard that Your Majesty conscientiously heeds Heaven’s warnings to win Heaven’s favor, accepts the counsel of all officials, and guards against desires before they arise. You attend the Classics Colloquium to seek the causes of these calamities and summon audiences in a side hall [?] to reflect upon your failings. Your practices of self-examination cannot be fully recounted, and the Lord on High watches over them clearly. You discontinue unprofitable works and prohibit rewards unsupported by merit, enlarge reserves to strengthen the foundations, and eliminate unbounded expenditure to ease the burden of levies. The merits of your government cannot be enumerated, and the common people will benefit from them forever. Could your anxious diligence consist merely in dispatching officials to distribute relief and loans and issuing edicts reproaching yourself?
Looking back to antiquity, in the Shang and Zhou dynasties, Gaozong and King Xuan both encountered calamities and anomalies. The former set his affairs right; the latter humbled himself and cultivated his conduct. Thus the anomalies of the crowing pheasant and the drought demon ultimately could not become baleful portents for their states. Although the excellence of their dynastic restorations did not have to await warnings before being understood, can we deny that calamities and anomalies spurred their resolve and brought their achievements to fruition?
During the Western Han, Emperors Wen and Jing frequently encountered calamities and anomalies. The former maintained a respectful and frugal bearing; the latter followed the undertaking he had inherited without altering it. Thus extraordinary floods, droughts, rain, and snow ultimately could not become afflictions for the people. Although the long duration of their peaceful nurturing of the people did not depend upon the exaltation of frugality, can we deny that calamities and anomalies restrained their desires and guarded against their extravagance? Viewed in this light, then…

title: 嘉靖四年江西鄉試錄
text:
我
皇上省躬以弭變固將比美於商周之中興
端本以立政陋文宗於不足爲矣是故
聖學之正有以黙契乎春秋災異之紀脗合
洪範事應之陳而諸儒之說又何足以惑
之哉然災異之作固人君之所當省而大
平無事尤君子之所深慮蓋功業之成多
得於屯遭困抑之際而怠荒之起易乘於
豐亨豫大之餘詩稱文王曰不聞亦式不
===
諫亦入夫不聞不諫且然況既聞既諫者
乎文王且然而況於法文王者乎古之人
君憂勤惕勵無時可寧是不待災異之著
而躬省之道已嚴此天理之所以常存而
治化之所以獨盛也以是存心致萬化之
本出咸和之政積而行之則天地以位萬
物以育薰蒸感格災害不生而享國長久
之道要不可以他求者草野之言未知符
朝堂之論否也惟執事進之
punctuated: 我皇上省躬以弭變，固將比美於商周之中興；端本以立政，陋文宗於不足爲矣。是故聖學之正，有以黙契乎春秋災異之紀，脗合洪範事應之陳，而諸儒之說又何足以惑之哉？然災異之作，固人君之所當省，而大平無事，尤君子之所深慮。蓋功業之成，多得於屯遭困抑之際；而怠荒之起，易乘於豐亨豫大之餘。《詩》稱文王曰：「不聞亦式，不諫亦入。」夫不聞不諫且然，況既聞既諫者乎？文王且然，而況於法文王者乎？古之人君，憂勤惕勵，無時可寧，是不待災異之著，而躬省之道已嚴。此天理之所以常存，而治化之所以獨盛也。以是存心，致萬化之本，出咸和之政，積而行之，則天地以位，萬物以育，薰蒸感格，災害不生，而享國長久之道，要不可以他求者。草野之言，未知符朝堂之論否也，惟執事進之。
translation_en:
…our August Emperor, examining himself to avert abnormal phenomena, will assuredly rival the restorations of the Shang and Zhou in their excellence. By rectifying the root to establish good government, he will regard Wenzong [?] as an inadequate model. Thus the correctness of his sagely learning accords implicitly with the records of calamities and anomalies in the Spring and Autumn Annals and tallies with the exposition of actions and their corresponding responses in the Great Plan. How, then, could the explanations of the various scholars suffice to mislead him?

Yet although the occurrence of calamities and anomalies certainly calls for a ruler’s self-examination, peaceful times free of troubles are especially a matter of profound concern to the gentleman. Accomplishments are often achieved amid adversity and constraint [?], while negligence and indolence readily arise in the wake of abundance, prosperity, ease, and greatness. The Book of Odes says of King Wen: “Even without being told, he followed the rule; even without remonstrance, he accepted counsel.” If this was so when he had neither been told nor remonstrated with, how much more should it be so after hearing instruction and remonstrance? If even King Wen acted thus, how much more should those who take King Wen as their model?

The rulers of antiquity were anxious and diligent, watchful and resolute, allowing themselves no moment of repose. Without waiting for calamities and anomalies to become manifest, they already practiced rigorous self-examination. This is why heavenly principle constantly endured and their transforming governance flourished so exceptionally. With this disposition maintained in the heart, one brings to fulfillment the root of all transformation and issues policies that bring harmony to all. Through sustained practice, Heaven and Earth will take their proper places and the myriad things will be nourished. This pervasive influence will move and reach all things; calamities will not arise. The way to enjoy a long-lasting reign must, in essence, be sought nowhere else.

These are the words of one in the countryside. I do not know whether they accord with deliberations at court. I ask only that you, the officials in charge, submit them.

title: 嘉靖四年江西鄉試錄
text:
江西鄉試錄後序
嘉靖乙酉江西鄉試事竣錄具
成維時人事整暇天氣清朗諸
執事相視欣然如有得也監臨
御史秦〔鉞〕惕然若之乃言曰
夫固知若得士是賀也不知吾
之有懼於得也恒言科目非所
===
待士而朱子在南康軍時其書
堂講義未嘗戒人科舉特存乎
人耳夫謂科目不足盡士可謂
科目盡不得士不可亦存乎人
耳方士之未得也惟士之有臧
否焉矣既得也厥得失在予漢
興賢良一詔有閩郡不應一人
punctuated:
江西鄉試錄後序

嘉靖乙酉，江西鄉試事竣，錄具成。維時人事整暇，天氣清朗，諸執事相視欣然，如有得也。監臨御史秦〔鉞〕惕然若之，乃言曰：「夫固知若得士是賀也，不知吾之有懼於得也。恒言科目非所待士，而朱子在南康軍時，其書堂講義未嘗戒人科舉，特存乎人耳。夫謂科目不足盡士，可；謂科目盡不得士，不可。亦存乎人耳。方士之未得也，惟士之有臧否焉矣；既得也，厥得失在予。漢興賢良一詔，有閩郡不應一人。
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Jiangxi Provincial Examination

In the yiyou year of the Jiajing reign (1525), the Jiangxi Provincial Examination concluded, and its record was completed. At that time, affairs were in order and there was leisure; the weather was clear and bright. The officials conducting the examination looked at one another with pleasure, as though they had gained something. The Supervising Official, Censor Qin〔Yue〕, appeared apprehensive at this [?] and said:

“I certainly know that you are celebrating the acquisition of worthy men; you do not know that this very acquisition gives me cause for fear. It is commonly said that the examination system is no way to treat scholars. Yet when Master Zhu was in Nankang Military Prefecture, his lectures at the academy never warned people against the civil-service examinations. It depends solely on the people involved. To say that the examination system cannot encompass all worthy men is permissible; to say that it obtains no worthy men at all is not. This too depends on the people involved. Before scholars have been selected, it is only their own merits and faults that are at issue. Once they have been selected, responsibility for success or failure rests with me. When the Han issued an edict calling for the recommendation of the worthy and good, there was the case of Min Commandery, which did not put forward a single person in response. …

title: 嘉靖四年江西鄉試錄
text:
若夫地之不產非有司過也產
矣而不知不明知而不舉不忠
不知而舉誣入且自誣非吾輩
今日責哉大江之西故號多賢
率儒先過化之區士之鍾匡廬
而毓彭蠡者景行親切豈不有
超出倫類而特由此進者乎今
===
所知固諸士之文矣而予未敢
遽謂得也適莽蒼者志乎黼黻
之觀管籥之聽去十旬貿貿然
反固也乃若挾千金資之通都
闤闠奇貨百物唯其所取歸而
發笥則燕石也而可乎故人唯
不得之懼吾斯得之懼也于時
punctuated: 若夫地之不產，非有司過也。產矣而不知，不明；知而不舉，不忠；不知而舉，誣入且自誣。非吾輩今日責哉？大江之西，故號多賢，率儒先過化之區。士之鍾匡廬而毓彭蠡者，景行親切，豈不有超出倫類而特由此進者乎？今所知固諸士之文矣，而予未敢遽謂得也。適莽蒼者，志乎黼黻之觀、管籥之聽，去十旬，貿貿然反，固也。乃若挾千金資之通都闤闠，奇貨百物，唯其所取，歸而發笥，則燕石也，而可乎？故人唯不得之懼，吾斯得之懼也。于時
translation_en:
As for a locality that produces no worthy men, that is no fault of the responsible officials. But if it produces them and officials fail to recognize them, this is lack of discernment; if they recognize them but fail to recommend them, this is disloyalty; if they recommend men without knowing them, they misrepresent others [?] and deceive themselves as well. Is this not our responsibility today? The region west of the great Yangzi has long been renowned for its many worthy men; much of it has received the transforming influence of earlier Confucian masters. Among scholars who embody the concentrated spirit of Kuanglu and are nurtured by Pengli, with the lofty conduct of their predecessors so close at hand, surely there are some who surpass their fellows and advance through this very path? At present, what we know is indeed these scholars’ writing, yet I dare not hastily declare that we have found worthy men.

Someone who goes into the wilderness hoping to behold embroidered ceremonial robes and hear pipes and flutes may spend a hundred days away and return bewildered: that is only to be expected. But suppose someone takes a thousand gold pieces to the markets of a great metropolis, where rare goods and a hundred kinds of merchandise are his for the choosing, and then returns home and opens his chest, only to find ordinary stones from Yan: could that be acceptable? Thus, while others fear only failing to obtain worthy men, I fear the very fact that I have obtained them. At this moment…

title: 嘉靖四年江西鄉試錄
text:
益夫與諸同事咸作而曰方益
夫等應聘而來也由金陵逾彭
石以泝鄱陽達于章見水焉排
空觸石騰蛟奔龍或風雨恬霽
則波煙相媚咫尺倏忽千態萬
狀蓋天下至文也見山焉五老
九奇摩穹出雲香爐瀑布崒然
===
相望皆屹立長江之上根盤不
知其幾許又天下一奇觀也若
襟江帶湖之雄西山南浦之秀
又不暇論矣乃今又見文焉有
道政事者有述禮樂者有及性
與天道者其稱堯舜周孔如取
左右又若親見濂溪晦翁象山
punctuated: 益夫與諸同事咸作而曰：「方益夫等應聘而來也，由金陵逾彭石，以泝鄱陽，達于章。見水焉，排空觸石，騰蛟奔龍；或風雨恬霽，則波煙相媚，咫尺倏忽，千態萬狀，蓋天下至文也。見山焉，五老九奇，摩穹出雲，香爐瀑布，崒然相望，皆屹立長江之上，根盤不知其幾許，又天下一奇觀也。若襟江帶湖之雄，西山南浦之秀，又不暇論矣。乃今又見文焉，有道政事者，有述禮樂者，有及性與天道者。其稱堯舜周孔，如取左右；又若親見濂溪、晦翁、象山
translation_en:
…Yifu and his colleagues all rose and said: “When we accepted the invitation and came here, we traveled from Jinling past Pengshi, upstream through Poyang, and reached Zhang. We saw waters surging skyward and striking rocks, like leaping dragons and dragons racing onward. When wind and rain subsided and the skies cleared, waves and mist lent each other charm; within a tiny space and a fleeting instant, they assumed a thousand forms and ten thousand shapes. Surely these were the finest patterns under Heaven. We saw mountains: Wulao and Jiuqi, brushing the heavens and rising above the clouds; Xianglu and the waterfall, facing one another in towering grandeur. All stood high above the Yangzi River, their roots extending no one knows how far—another extraordinary spectacle under Heaven. As for the grandeur of the river worn as a lapel and the lake as a girdle, and the beauty of Xishan and Nanpu, we have no leisure even to discuss them.

“Now we have also seen literary compositions. Some discuss affairs of government; some expound rites and music; some touch upon human nature and the Way of Heaven. Their references to Yao, Shun, the Duke of Zhou, and Confucius come as readily as reaching for something close at hand. It is also as though they had personally seen Lianxi, Huiweng, and Xiangshan…

title: 嘉靖四年江西鄉試錄
text:
諸君子於白鹿鵞湖之上而揖
之者也是故其辭淵然在矣鏘
然鳴矣幽然光矣沛然流矣其
氣如決九仞之淵注之海如乘
凰駕虬直至乎天斯乃下耆夫
辭以昭德氣以徵志是謂稱其
山川豪傑之興無待文王矧兹
===
流波之遠也安知不有清風高
節如柴桑翁文章行業如歐陽
子不屈虜廷如洪忠宣精忠大
節如文山疊山忠義敢言如澹
菴盧溪者出而名世乎茍得一
人焉光兹後矣况若而人邪是
益夫與諸執事皆可無愳也已
punctuated: 諸君子於白鹿鵞湖之上而揖之者也。是故其辭淵然在矣，鏘然鳴矣，幽然光矣，沛然流矣。其氣如決九仞之淵，注之海；如乘凰駕虬，直至乎天。斯乃下耆夫。辭以昭德，氣以徵志，是謂稱其山川。豪傑之興，無待文王，矧兹流波之遠也！安知不有清風高節如柴桑翁，文章行業如歐陽子，不屈虜廷如洪忠宣，精忠大節如文山、疊山，忠義敢言如澹菴、盧溪者，出而名世乎？茍得一人焉，光兹後矣，况若而人邪？是益夫與諸執事皆可無愳也已
translation_en:
…these gentlemen at Bailu and Ehu, and bowing to them in greeting. Thus their words possess profound depth, ring out sonorously, shine with a quiet light, and flow abundantly. Their vital force is like breaching a pool nine ren deep and pouring its waters into the sea; like riding a phoenix and driving a horned dragon straight up to Heaven. This indeed is … [?; the text 斯乃下耆夫 is unclear]. Their words manifest their virtue, and their vital force attests their aspirations: this is what it means to be worthy of their mountains and rivers. Outstanding men arise without awaiting a King Wen; how much more so here, where the currents of his influence reach so far!

How can we know that there will not emerge men who win renown in their age, with pure character and lofty integrity like the Old Master of Chaisang; literary accomplishment and virtuous conduct like Master Ouyang; refusal to submit at a barbarian court like Hong Zhongxuan; wholehearted loyalty and great integrity like Wenshan and Dieshan; or loyalty, righteousness, and courage to speak out like Dan’an and Luxi? If even one such man is found, he will bring glory to this land in generations to come. How much more so with so many such men! Thus I, Yifu, and all the officials involved may be free of apprehension …

title: 嘉靖四年江西鄉試錄
text:
矣時御史以〔益夫〕言然遂書于
末簡
南京京衛武學教授吴〔益夫〕謹
序
punctuated:
矣。時御史以〔益夫〕言然，遂書于末簡。
南京京衛武學教授吴〔益夫〕謹序。
translation_en:
… At the time, the censor deemed Yifu’s words correct, so they were written on the final leaf.
Preface respectfully composed by Wu Yifu, Instructor in the Military School of the Capital Guards at Nanjing.

title: 嘉靖四年江西鄉試錄
text:
國初南都之塑像乃元人之俗而我
聖祖毅然去之其功偉矣彼大成之稱獨非元
之所加者與此愚之未解一也今京師之
太學亦元人之舊而我
文皇因之不改其義深矣彼
聖祖之華獨非義之至當者歟此愚之未解二
也嘗觀吾孔子之作春秋也內夏外夷不
遺餘力而韃靼亂華又古今所無之變其
一時君臣誣罔矯僞之禮愚恐聖人在天
===
之靈必所不屑也孰事所謂
聖人之用意有非恒情之所易窺邈則以爲
祖宗一時慎重之意當如此爾乃今百有五十
餘年于茲矣
聖天子在上賢公卿在下苟有以
聞豈無主張斯議以爲吾道之一快乎此非愚
之狂也固薦紳之議也惟進而折衷之謹
對
第二問
punctuated:
國初，南都之塑像乃元人之俗，而我聖祖毅然去之，其功偉矣。彼大成之稱，獨非元之所加者與？此愚之未解一也。今京師之太學亦元人之舊，而我文皇因之不改，其義深矣。彼聖祖之華，獨非義之至當者歟？此愚之未解二也。嘗觀吾孔子之作《春秋》也，內夏外夷，不遺餘力。而韃靼亂華，又古今所無之變。其一時君臣誣罔矯僞之禮，愚恐聖人在天之靈必所不屑也。孰事所謂「聖人之用意，有非恒情之所易窺」？邈則以爲祖宗一時慎重之意，當如此爾。乃今百有五十餘年于茲矣。聖天子在上，賢公卿在下，苟有以聞，豈無主張斯議，以爲吾道之一快乎？此非愚之狂也，固薦紳之議也。惟進而折衷之。謹對。

第二問
translation_en:
At the beginning of our dynasty, the use of sculpted images in the southern capital was a custom inherited from the Yuan. Our sacred founder resolutely abolished it: great indeed was his achievement. Yet was not the designation “Great Perfection” also conferred by the Yuan? This is the first point that I, in my ignorance, do not understand. The Imperial University in the present capital likewise survives from the Yuan, and our Emperor Wen retained it unchanged: profound indeed was his reasoning. Yet was not the sacred founder’s “splendor” [?] entirely consonant with what was right? This is the second point that I do not understand.

I have observed that when our Confucius composed the Spring and Autumn Annals, he spared no effort in treating the Chinese as insiders and the barbarians as outsiders. The Tatars’ disruption of China, moreover, was an upheaval without parallel in ancient or modern times. I fear that the sage’s spirit in Heaven would surely disdain the fraudulent and spurious rites devised by the ruler and ministers of that time. What, then, of the saying [?], “The sage’s intentions are not always readily fathomed by ordinary minds”? I consider [?] that the ancestral emperors’ intention at the time was simply to proceed with such caution. But more than a hundred and fifty years have now elapsed.

With a sagely Son of Heaven above and worthy dukes and ministers below, if this matter were brought to his attention, would there not be someone to champion this proposal and thereby bring great satisfaction to those who follow our Way? This is no reckless fancy of mine; it is indeed a proposal discussed among the scholar-officials. I ask only that you advance it and reach a considered judgment upon it. Respectfully submitted in reply.

Second Question

title: 嘉靖四年江西鄉試錄
text:
江治
同考試官訓導吳　批　〔以體用偏全發明政學且能詳舉古人而評隲之必知學而可達於政者也〕
同考試官訓導張　批　〔策上以政學欲觀所養故不以隱僻之說相困子能探本窮源旅經斷史灼有定見學已至此何有於政耶〕
考試官教授吳　批　〔問目所及士子類能言之至於援引該博文勢舂容無踰子者〕
考試官教授王　批　〔議論精當故實不遺可以驗博古之學矣〕
===
對天下未嘗有無體之用也唯其偏全之
分已矣亦未嘗有無用之體也惟其難易
之時已矣是故觀天下之用者存乎體體
有偏全而用之小大隨之世豈有無體之
用哉論天下之體者存乎時時有難易而
體之通塞繫之世豈有無用之體哉觀此
則知吾儒内外合一之學體用相須之妙
而執事政學不同之問亦可得而復矣夫
punctuated:
江治

同考試官訓導吳批〔以體用偏全發明政學，且能詳舉古人而評隲之，必知學而可達於政者也。〕

同考試官訓導張批〔策上以政學，欲觀所養，故不以隱僻之說相困。子能探本窮源，旅經斷史，灼有定見。學已至此，何有於政耶？〕

考試官教授吳批〔問目所及，士子類能言之。至於援引該博，文勢舂容，無踰子者。〕

考試官教授王批〔議論精當，故實不遺，可以驗博古之學矣。〕

對：天下未嘗有無體之用也，唯其偏全之分已矣；亦未嘗有無用之體也，惟其難易之時已矣。是故觀天下之用者存乎體，體有偏全，而用之小大隨之，世豈有無體之用哉？論天下之體者存乎時，時有難易，而體之通塞繫之，世豈有無用之體哉？觀此，則知吾儒内外合一之學、體用相須之妙，而執事政學不同之問，亦可得而復矣。夫
translation_en:
Jiang Zhi 江治

Comment by Associate Examiner Wu, Instructor: 〔By considering substance and function, and partiality and completeness, you elucidate governance and learning. Moreover, you cite men of antiquity in detail and appraise them. You must be someone who understands learning and can thereby attain competence in governance.〕

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor: 〔The policy question presents governance and learning [?] to discover what you have cultivated; hence it does not trouble you with obscure and abstruse doctrines. You can investigate fundamentals and pursue origins, marshal the Classics [?] and judge historical accounts, displaying clearly established views. With your learning already at this level, what difficulty could governance present?〕

Comment by Examiner Wu, Professor: 〔Candidates can generally discuss the matters covered by the question. But in the breadth of your citations and the ease and amplitude of your prose, none surpasses you.〕

Comment by Examiner Wang, Professor: 〔Your arguments are precise and sound, and you leave out no historical precedents. This attests to your broad learning in antiquity.〕

Reply: In all the world there has never been function without substance; there is only the distinction between partial and complete substance. Nor has there ever been substance without function; there are only times of difficulty and ease. Thus, to examine function in the world, one must attend to substance. Substance may be partial or complete, and the scope of its function follows accordingly. How could there be function without substance in the world? To discuss substance in the world, one must attend to the times. Times may be difficult or easy, and whether substance finds expression or is obstructed depends upon them. How could there be substance without function in the world? From this we can understand our Confucian learning, which unites the internal and external, and the subtle way in which substance and function require one another. Your question concerning the difference between governance and learning can thereby also be answered. Now, …

title: 嘉靖四年江西鄉試錄
text:
盈天地之間者惟萬物萬物者萬事□□
由生也然事有理故天下之道理與事□
已矣天以其無所於寄特命儒者出而□
之故儒者之道學與政而已矣學也者所
以明其理而為政之體政也者所以出其
事而為學之用故大學之明德新民乃儒
者功用之全而中庸之成己成物不害為
一舉事者誠以吾儒之道其體段本如是
其全而功用本如是其大故也故欽明文
===
思安安者巍乎其有成功而五典百揆之
徽叙則自明物察倫中來也有危微授受
之旨廼有萬世永賴之功而明刑弼教則
固邁種德者基之也西土未興而羑里之
易已繫蟠溪未離而牧野之陣以成儒者
之道在君而為君在臣而為臣在鄉相則
大業之富有在布衣則盛德之日新而道
無加損焉也故曰居仁由義大人之事備
矣又曰達不離道焉是故此政即此學矣
punctuated: 盈天地之間者，惟萬物。萬物者，萬事□□由生也。然事有理，故天下之道，理與事□已矣。天以其無所於寄，特命儒者出而□之。故儒者之道，學與政而已矣。學也者，所以明其理而為政之體；政也者，所以出其事而為學之用。故《大學》之明德新民，乃儒者功用之全；而《中庸》之成己成物，不害為一舉事者，誠以吾儒之道，其體段本如是其全，而功用本如是其大故也。故欽明文思安安者，巍乎其有成功；而五典百揆之徽叙，則自明物察倫中來也。有危微授受之旨，廼有萬世永賴之功；而明刑弼教，則固邁種德者基之也。西土未興，而羑里之《易》已繫；蟠溪未離，而牧野之陣以成。儒者之道，在君而為君，在臣而為臣；在鄉相，則大業之富有；在布衣，則盛德之日新，而道無加損焉也。故曰：「居仁由義，大人之事備矣。」又曰：「達不離道焉。」是故此政即此學矣。
translation_en:
…What fills the space between Heaven and Earth is simply the myriad things. The myriad things are that from which all affairs arise [two illegible characters obscure the wording]. Yet affairs have their principles; thus the Way throughout the world consists simply of principles and affairs [one character illegible]. Heaven, having nowhere to entrust them, specially commands Confucian scholars to come forth and [?] them. Thus the Way of Confucian scholars consists simply of learning and governance. Learning clarifies principles and constitutes the substance of governance; governance puts affairs into practice and constitutes the application of learning. Hence illuminating virtue and renewing the people, as taught in the Great Learning, encompass the full accomplishment of Confucian scholars. Perfecting oneself and perfecting things, as taught in the Doctrine of the Mean, may therefore be regarded as a single undertaking. This is indeed because the substance of our Confucian Way is inherently so complete, and its efficacy inherently so great.

Thus he who was reverent, discerning, accomplished, thoughtful, and naturally at ease achieved towering success; and the harmonious ordering of the five teachings and the hundred affairs arose from understanding things and discerning human relationships. The teaching concerning the precarious human mind and the subtle moral mind was transmitted and received, and thereby came achievements upon which ten thousand generations would forever depend. Making punishments clear to support instruction was assuredly founded upon vigorous cultivation of virtue. Before the western lands had risen to power, the explanations of the Changes had already been appended at Youli; before the departure from Panxi, the battle formation for Muye had already taken shape.

The Way of Confucian scholars enables a ruler to act as a ruler and a minister to act as a minister. Among high ministers [?], it manifests itself in the abundant scope of great undertakings; among commoners, in the daily renewal of flourishing virtue. Yet the Way itself undergoes neither increase nor diminution. Hence it is said: “Dwell in benevolence and follow righteousness, and the work of a great man is complete.” It is also said: “When successful, he does not depart from the Way.” Thus this governance is precisely this learning.

title: 嘉靖四年江西鄉試錄
text:
外用而求之者非也此學即此政矣外體
而事焉者末也舉其全焉則爲左右厥辟
爲舟楫鹽梅爲洛邑之營太平之迹原其
所自何莫非一德咸有也志以道寧也易
爻之旨敬義之訓也是何也有是全體則
有是大用其不然必其偏焉者也如執事
所舉若而人是也當其難焉則不過爲六
經爲七篇爲易傳爲諸集傳而已至於三
月而墮都郈莱一言而君臣知罪治蒲而
===
化行理建而學興不足爲小試云耳此豈
道學之過哉特寔爲之聖哲馳騖而不足
者也其不然者必當其易如執事所舉若
而人矣昔者冉求非不悅夫子之道子路
亦升孔氏之堂結纓一事先儒謂其有行
一不義殺一不辜而得天下不爲之心記
者以其長於政事偶列之矣子游絃歌武
城子夏出宰莒父想聞聖教必有可觀記
者以其長於文學特表之耳雖然二子謂
punctuated:
外用而求之者，非也。此學即此政矣，外體而事焉者，末也。舉其全焉，則爲左右厥辟，爲舟楫鹽梅，爲洛邑之營、太平之迹。原其所自，何莫非一德咸有也，志以道寧也，《易》爻之旨、敬義之訓也？是何也？有是全體，則有是大用。其不然，必其偏焉者也，如執事所舉若而人是也。當其難焉，則不過爲六經，爲七篇，爲《易傳》，爲諸集傳而已。至於三月而墮都郈莱，一言而君臣知罪，治蒲而化行，理建而學興，不足爲小試云耳。此豈道學之過哉？特寔爲之聖哲馳騖而不足者也。其不然者，必當其易，如執事所舉若而人矣。
昔者冉求非不悅夫子之道，子路亦升孔氏之堂。結纓一事，先儒謂其有行一不義、殺一不辜而得天下不爲之心。記者以其長於政事，偶列之矣。子游絃歌武城，子夏出宰莒父，想聞聖教，必有可觀。記者以其長於文學，特表之耳。雖然，二子謂
translation_en:
…Those who seek it apart from its practical application are mistaken. This learning is itself this governance; to pursue governance apart from its underlying substance is to attend only to the secondary. Taken in its entirety, it means assisting one’s sovereign, serving as his boat and oars, his salt and plums, planning Luoyi, and bringing about the achievements of great peace. Tracing these things to their source, do they not all derive from possessing unified virtue, from settling one’s purpose through the Way, from the meaning of the line statements of the Book of Changes, and from the teachings on reverence and righteousness? Why is this so? Where there is this complete substance, there is this great practical efficacy. Where this is not so, the attainment must be partial—as with the people you, sir, have cited. When circumstances are difficult for them, they do no more than produce the Six Classics, the Seven Books of Mencius, the Commentary on the Book of Changes, and the various collected commentaries. As for razing Du, Hou, and Lai [?] within three months, making ruler and ministers recognize their wrongdoing with a single utterance, governing Pu so that moral transformation spread, and administering Jian so that learning flourished, these scarcely amount to a small trial of their abilities. How could this be a fault of learning the Way? Rather, putting it into actual practice is something toward which even sages and wise men strive without finding their efforts sufficient [?]. Those for whom it is otherwise must have encountered easy circumstances, like those people you, sir, have cited.
In former times, Ran Qiu was not without delight in the Master’s Way, and Zilu, too, had ascended the hall of Confucius. Concerning his act of tying his cap strings before death, earlier Confucian scholars said that he possessed the resolve to refuse to commit a single unrighteous act or kill a single innocent person, even if thereby he could gain the world. Because he excelled in governmental affairs, the recorder simply placed him in that category. Ziyou accompanied singing with strings at Wucheng, and Zixia went out to serve as magistrate of Jufu. Having presumably received the sage’s teachings, they must have had achievements worth seeing. Because they excelled in textual learning, the recorder merely singled them out under that heading. Nevertheless, to say of these two men…

title: 嘉靖四年江西鄉試錄
text:
之有體有用則可求其有綏來動和之化
王齊反手之覩則無矣此愚所謂偏全之
分也雖然未也後世列於儒林者代不之
人求其可授以政而達諸用者吾得四人
焉賈誼仲舒韓愈王通其儔也下此則揚
雄劉歆之徒無足論矣列於循吏者何代
無之求其或本諸學而有其體者吾得二
人焉文翁卓茂其匹也外此則黃覇功名
且損治郡矣他何論哉若是者謂其體用
===
有偏則可謂其判然相無吾不敢也至若
公孫曲學阿世而取相封矦霍光不學無
術而擁昭立宣萊公雖不免張詠之譏而
澶淵之役功不可泯是弘之竊取本無足
觀而張霍之暗合固隨試而輒效者也推
而極之則春秋之世有器小而致齊之盛
惠小而强鄭之衰者漢唐之時有謙讓未
遑而幾致刑措慚德不免而身致太平者
非皆所謂暗合而竊取者乎三代以上道
punctuated: 之有體有用則可，求其有綏來動和之化、王齊反手之覩，則無矣。此愚所謂偏全之分也。雖然，未也。後世列於儒林者，代不之人，求其可授以政而達諸用者，吾得四人焉：賈誼、仲舒、韓愈、王通，其儔也。下此則揚雄、劉歆之徒，無足論矣。列於循吏者，何代無之？求其或本諸學而有其體者，吾得二人焉：文翁、卓茂，其匹也。外此則黃覇功名且損治郡矣，他何論哉？若是者，謂其體用有偏則可，謂其判然相無，吾不敢也。至若公孫曲學阿世而取相封矦，霍光不學無術而擁昭立宣，萊公雖不免張詠之譏，而澶淵之役功不可泯。是弘之竊取本無足觀，而張霍之暗合，固隨試而輒效者也。推而極之，則春秋之世，有器小而致齊之盛、惠小而强鄭之衰者；漢唐之時，有謙讓未遑而幾致刑措、慚德不免而身致太平者，非皆所謂暗合而竊取者乎？三代以上，道
translation_en:
…it is permissible to say that they possessed both substance and practical application. Yet one cannot find in them the transforming influence by which, when a sage brings peace, people come to him, and when he acts, they respond in harmony; nor the prospect of ruling Qi as a true king as easily as turning over one’s hand. This is what I, in my humble opinion, call the distinction between partial and complete attainment.

Yet this does not exhaust the matter. Among those ranked in later ages as Confucian scholars, every age had such men [?]. Seeking those who could be entrusted with government and put their learning into practice, I find four: Jia Yi, Zhongshu [Dong Zhongshu], Han Yu, and Wang Tong belong to this company. Below them, men such as Yang Xiong and Liu Xin scarcely merit discussion. As for those ranked as exemplary officials, what age lacked them? Seeking those whose work was perhaps rooted in learning and who possessed its underlying substance, I find two: Wen Weng and Zhuo Mao belong to this class. Beyond these, even Huang Ba’s achievements and reputation fell short of what he had accomplished in governing a commandery. What need is there to discuss the others? Of such men, one may say that their substance and practical application were unevenly developed; I would not venture to say that the two were wholly separate, each altogether lacking the other.

Consider Gongsun [Hong], who distorted learning to flatter his age and thereby obtained the chancellorship and enfeoffment as a marquis; or Huo Guang, who lacked learning and cultivated method, yet supported Emperor Zhao and enthroned Emperor Xuan. Although the Duke of Lai [Kou Zhun] could not escape Zhang Yong’s criticism, his achievement in the campaign at Chanyuan cannot be effaced. Thus Hong’s appropriated success was fundamentally unworthy of regard, whereas the unknowing conformity [to the Way] of Zhang and Huo [?] did indeed prove effective whenever put to the test.

Extending this reasoning to its furthest reach, in the Spring and Autumn period there were men whose capacity was small, yet who brought Qi to greatness, and men whose benevolence was limited, yet who strengthened Zheng in its decline. In the Han and Tang periods there were men who had no leisure for modest deference, yet nearly brought punishments into disuse, and men whose conduct was not free from shame, yet who personally brought about great peace. Were these not all instances of what is called unknowing conformity and appropriated attainment? During the Three Dynasties and earlier, the Way…

title: 嘉靖四年江西鄉試錄
text:
出於一〔此未之前關也三代以下道出於〕
二文章政事始有岐而二之者矣雖然孰
事所問固知有體無用者矣亦知所謂無
體之用乎周瑜赤壁之勝謝玄淝水之捷
是已執事固知有用無體者矣未知無用
之體也誦詩三百不能專對四方斟量丘
壑不能籌策廟廊是已甚至老之虛釋之
無楊爲我而害義墨兼愛而害仁又無體
之體矣安可望其用邪申韓之刑名管晏
===
之功利儀秦之口舌鞅斯之慘刻又無用
之用矣更復論其體邪是其所以得罪名
教如此者良由不知吾儒之道也吾儒之
道蘊之爲德行如良貫未售中有深藏之
富發之爲事業如探囊出物隨手而得拼
傅剛召孔孟程朱不可尚矣若孔明一見
隆中輒許先主以鼎立之形如持左券交
手相付范文正公自做秀才便以天下爲
已任而象山亦曰宇宙內事儒者分內事
punctuated: 出於一〔此未之前關也。三代以下道出於〕二，文章政事始有岐而二之者矣。雖然，孰事所問，固知有體無用者矣，亦知所謂無體之用乎？周瑜赤壁之勝、謝玄淝水之捷，是已。執事固知有用無體者矣，未知無用之體也。誦詩三百，不能專對四方；斟量丘壑，不能籌策廟廊，是已。甚至老之虛、釋之無，楊爲我而害義，墨兼愛而害仁，又無體之體矣，安可望其用邪？申韓之刑名、管晏之功利、儀秦之口舌、鞅斯之慘刻，又無用之用矣，更復論其體邪？是其所以得罪名教如此者，良由不知吾儒之道也。吾儒之道，蘊之爲德行，如良貫未售，中有深藏之富；發之爲事業，如探囊出物，隨手而得。拼傅剛召、孔孟程朱，不可尚矣。若孔明一見隆中，輒許先主以鼎立之形，如持左券，交手相付。范文正公自做秀才，便以天下爲已任，而象山亦曰：「宇宙內事，儒者分內事
translation_en:
…issued from a single source. 〔This connects with the preceding passage [?]. After the Three Dynasties, the Way issued from〕 two sources, and literary composition and government affairs began to diverge into separate pursuits. Nevertheless, your question [?] certainly shows awareness of substance without application; but do you also know what is meant by application without substance? Zhou Yu’s victory at Chibi and Xie Xuan’s triumph at the Fei River are examples. You certainly know of application without substance, but you have yet to understand substance without application. Reciting the three hundred poems of the Book of Odes yet being unable to respond independently on diplomatic missions abroad; weighing hills and valleys yet being unable to devise plans at court—these are examples.

Going still further, Laozi’s emptiness and Buddhism’s nothingness, Yang Zhu’s doctrine of acting for oneself, which harms righteousness, and Mozi’s universal love, which harms benevolence, are substance devoid of substance. How could one expect them to have application? The doctrines of punishments and names of Shen Buhai and Han Fei, the pursuit of achievement and advantage by Guan Zhong and Yan Ying, the persuasive rhetoric of Zhang Yi and Su Qin, and the cruel severity of Shang Yang and Li Si are application devoid of application. What further discussion could there be of their substance? The reason they thus offend the moral teaching is precisely that they do not understand the Way of us Confucians.

Stored within, our Confucian Way becomes virtuous conduct, like a skilled merchant who has not yet sold his goods [?], possessing a wealth of deeply stored resources. Expressed outwardly, it becomes practical accomplishments, like taking something from a bag: whatever one reaches for comes readily to hand. The figures named as “Pin, Fu, Gang, and Shao” [?], together with Confucius, Mencius, Cheng, and Zhu, cannot be surpassed. Consider Kongming: at his first meeting with the Former Lord at Longzhong, he immediately promised him a position in a tripartite balance of power, as though he held the creditor’s half of a contract and were handing it directly to him. Lord Fan Wenzheng, from his days as a student, took responsibility for all under Heaven as his own charge. Xiangshan likewise said: “Affairs within the universe are affairs within the Confucian scholar’s allotted responsibilities…”

title: 嘉靖四年江西鄉試錄
text:
也則其學術淵源政事大畧皆可想見若
張忠定公再守西蜀易危為安而終身不
談政事歐陽文忠嶇迹呂黎瀘歷天下而
終身不談文章非皆有見乎此而不欲以
偏長自居者邪鵬之搏也培風負天莫之
天閼焉鷃鵪數仞而下亦飛之至此小大
之辨也樗櫟凡材窮居明體當於偏全之
間久矣况逢良匠當不瓠落無容將無所
謂當其難者何辜身親見之
===
第三問
魏良政
同考試官教諭許　批　數為六藝之一士君子所當
究心者今此學不講視籌筭若將浼焉至欽天之道雖主
官疇人習之故知數而不知理此策考據經史能極理數
以順天求合為主而自得之妙興受
同考試官教諭朱　批　曆數之學妙參天人非史氏
莫能喻是策滔滔千數百言以尚未竟所縕歸世其業者
宜之誠忍於終篇發之得士如子曆學其復明矣乎
punctuated:
也。則其學術淵源、政事大畧，皆可想見。若張忠定公再守西蜀，易危為安，而終身不談政事；歐陽文忠嶇迹呂黎瀘歷天下，而終身不談文章，非皆有見乎此，而不欲以偏長自居者邪？鵬之搏也，培風負天，莫之天閼焉；鷃鵪數仞而下，亦飛之至。此小大之辨也。樗櫟凡材，窮居明體，當於偏全之間久矣。况逢良匠，當不瓠落無容。將無所謂「當其難者何辜」，身親見之？

第三問
魏良政

同考試官教諭許　批：數為六藝之一，士君子所當究心者。今此學不講，視籌筭若將浼焉。至欽天之道，雖主官疇人習之，故知數而不知理。此策考據經史，能極理數，以順天求合為主，而自得之妙興受。

同考試官教諭朱　批：曆數之學，妙參天人，非史氏莫能喻。是策滔滔千數百言，以尚未竟所縕。歸世其業者宜之，誠忍於終篇發之。得士如子，曆學其復明矣乎？
translation_en:
… Thus one can readily imagine the sources of their learning and the broad outlines of their statecraft. Lord Zhang Zhongding twice governed western Shu, turning danger into security, yet throughout his life did not discuss government affairs. Ouyang Wenzhong travelled throughout the realm [the wording concerning his movements is garbled: ?], yet throughout his life did not discuss literary composition. Was this not because both understood this principle and were unwilling to define themselves by a single accomplishment? When the great peng bird beats its wings, it rides the deep wind with the sky at its back, and nothing obstructs it [?]. The little birds rise a few fathoms and descend: this, too, is the utmost extent of their flight. Such is the distinction between the small and the great. I am ordinary timber, like the useless ailanthus and oak; living in obscurity and seeking to understand the underlying substance, I have long stood between partial and comprehensive attainment. Now that I have encountered a skilled craftsman, surely I shall not remain unwieldy and without a place. Might I personally witness what is meant by the saying, “What fault have those who bear the hardship committed?”

Third Policy Question
Wei Liangzheng

Comment by Associate Examiner Xu, Instructor: Mathematics is one of the Six Arts, something to which scholars and gentlemen ought to devote careful attention. Today this learning is neglected, and people regard calculating rods and arithmetic as though they would be defiled by them. As for the way of reverently observing Heaven, although the responsible officials and hereditary astronomical specialists practise it, they know the numbers but not the principles. This policy essay examines evidence from the Classics and histories and can probe both principles and numbers to their utmost. Its central concern is to accord with Heaven and seek correspondence with it; the subtlety of its independently attained insights [the concluding words are garbled: ?].

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhu, Instructor: The study of calendrical computation subtly brings Heaven and humanity into relation; none but the official astronomers can comprehend it. This essay flows on for well over a thousand words, yet still has not exhausted what its author has within him. It is fitting to attribute this to those who practise the discipline hereditarily [?]; indeed, he holds back until the end of the essay to disclose it [?]. Having obtained a scholar such as you, may we expect calendrical learning to become clear once again?

title: 嘉靖四年江西鄉試錄
text:
恐未易及也可敬可敬
考試官教授吳　批　考據精詳識見高遠欽若之
任有望於子矣
考試官教授王　批　此卷五策俱優而曆學一篇
尤爲精切錄此以例其餘也
造曆者有一定之法乎其無一定之法乎
日月之運行星辰之次舍凡可以推步而
知之者亘古今而不變者也而曰無一定
之法吾不信也日月之有盈縮朓朒之不
===
齊爲星辰之有遲留疾伏之不同焉而錯
綜往來出入于二道之間雖竭天下之智
巧而不能盡者也而曰有一定之法吾不
信也於不可一定之中而参之隨時考驗
之術是乃所以爲一定之法也則於曆也
其庶幾乎杜預有曰治曆者當順天以求
合非爲合以驗天知乎此則可與言曆矣
請因明問而敬陳之曆數之說其來遠矣
書曰欽若昊天曆象日月星辰敬授人時
punctuated:
恐未易及也，可敬，可敬！

考試官教授吳　批：考據精詳，識見高遠，欽若之任，有望於子矣。

考試官教授王　批：此卷五策俱優，而曆學一篇尤爲精切，錄此以例其餘也。

造曆者有一定之法乎？其無一定之法乎？日月之運行，星辰之次舍，凡可以推步而知之者，亘古今而不變者也。而曰無一定之法，吾不信也。日月之有盈縮，朓朒之不齊，爲星辰之有遲留疾伏之不同焉，而錯綜往來，出入于二道之間，雖竭天下之智巧而不能盡者也。而曰有一定之法，吾不信也。於不可一定之中，而参之隨時考驗之術，是乃所以爲一定之法也。則於曆也，其庶幾乎！杜預有曰：「治曆者當順天以求合，非爲合以驗天。」知乎此，則可與言曆矣。請因明問而敬陳之。曆數之說，其來遠矣。《書》曰：「欽若昊天，曆象日月星辰，敬授人時。」
translation_en:
…I fear it will not be easy to equal. Admirable, admirable!

Examiner Wu, Professor, comments: “Your examination of the sources is meticulous and thorough, and your understanding lofty and far-reaching. We may look to you to undertake the responsibility of reverently following Heaven.”

Examiner Wang, Professor, comments: “All five policy essays in this script are excellent, but the essay on calendrical learning is especially precise and pertinent. We record this one as representative of the others.”

Do those who construct calendars have a fixed method? Or do they have no fixed method? The movements of the sun and moon and the stations occupied by the stars—all that can be known through astronomical calculation—remain unchanged throughout antiquity and the present. Thus, if someone says there is no fixed method, I do not believe it. Yet the sun and moon advance and fall behind; the moon’s appearance may be early or late, with unequal variations; and [?] the stars differ in their slow movement, lingering, rapid movement, and concealment. Their movements intertwine as they come and go, passing into and out of the space between the two paths. Even all the ingenuity in the world cannot exhaust these variations. Thus, if someone says there is a fixed method, I do not believe it. Amid what cannot be fixed, one must apply techniques of observation and verification suited to the time: this is precisely how a fixed method is established. Would this not bring us close to a sound calendar? Du Yu said: “Those who regulate the calendar should follow Heaven to seek agreement, rather than manufacture agreement and use it to test Heaven.” With someone who understands this, one may discuss calendrical learning.

Allow me respectfully to set forth my views in response to your illuminating question. The study of calendrical calculation has a long history. The Book of Documents says: “Reverently follow august Heaven; calculate and observe the sun, moon, and stars, and respectfully communicate the seasons to the people.”

title: 嘉靖四年江西鄉試錄
text:
曰在璿璣玉衡以齊七政曰協用五紀協
者順之謂也在者察之謂也協者合之謂
也即順天以求合之意也易曰澤中有火
革君子以治歷明時革者改也即隨時以
更改之意也由是言之則二帝三王之所
以治曆者其法雖不盡傳其意可得而知
矣自漢劉歆作三統曆以一十四萬四千
五百一十有一爲積年以黃鍾八十一爲
日法行之一百八十餘年而後天七十八
===
刻其法不行迨及魏晉以迄唐宋作者無
慮數十家皆有積年日法而行之愈不能
久有百年而改者矣有三四十年而改者
矣有一二年而即改者矣是何也天有不
齊之運而曆拘一定之法不知順天以求
合故也元許衡郭守敬之造授時曆也一
以考測爲主取二至遠近日晷酌其中而
用之以至元辛巳歲前冬至日時分秒爲
氣應以冬至距朔之日爲閏應而歷代所
punctuated:
曰：「在璿璣玉衡，以齊七政。」曰：「協用五紀。」協者，順之謂也；在者，察之謂也；協者，合之謂也。即順天以求合之意也。《易》曰：「澤中有火，革；君子以治歷明時。」革者，改也，即隨時以更改之意也。由是言之，則二帝三王之所以治曆者，其法雖不盡傳，其意可得而知矣。
自漢劉歆作三統曆，以一十四萬四千五百一十有一爲積年，以黃鍾八十一爲日法，行之一百八十餘年，而後天七十八刻，其法不行。迨及魏晉，以迄唐宋，作者無慮數十家，皆有積年、日法，而行之愈不能久。有百年而改者矣，有三四十年而改者矣，有一二年而即改者矣。是何也？天有不齊之運，而曆拘一定之法，不知順天以求合故也。
元許衡、郭守敬之造授時曆也，一以考測爲主，取二至遠近日晷，酌其中而用之。以至元辛巳歲前冬至日時分秒爲氣應，以冬至距朔之日爲閏應，而歷代所
translation_en:
…It says: “He examined the rotating sphere and jade cross-tube, to bring the seven celestial regulators into accord.” It also says: “Harmonize the use of the five reckonings of time.” Xie 協 means to follow [?]; zai 在 means to examine; xie 協 means to bring into accord. This is precisely the idea of following Heaven to seek agreement with it. The Book of Changes says: “Within the lake there is fire: the hexagram Ge, Change. The gentleman thereby regulates the calendar and makes the seasons clear.” Ge means to alter: this is precisely the idea of making changes as circumstances require. From this we can see that, although the methods by which the Two Emperors and Three Kings regulated the calendar have not been transmitted in full, their intent can still be understood.
Beginning with Liu Xin of the Han, who devised the Three Concordances Calendar, 144,511 was used as the accumulated number of years from the calendrical epoch, and eighty-one, the number associated with the Huangzhong pitch-pipe, as the day divisor. After this calendar had been used for more than 180 years, it lagged behind Heaven by seventy-eight ke, or hundredths of a day, and its method was no longer workable. From the Wei and Jin down through the Tang and Song, there were altogether several dozen makers of calendars. All used accumulated years and day divisors, yet their calendars remained usable for increasingly short periods. Some were revised after a hundred years, others after thirty or forty years, and still others after only one or two years. Why was this? Because the motions of Heaven are irregular, whereas calendars are confined to fixed methods: their makers did not understand how to follow Heaven to seek agreement with it.
When Xu Heng and Guo Shoujing of the Yuan devised the Season-Granting Calendar, they based it entirely on observation and measurement. They took gnomon-shadow measurements at times nearer to and farther from the two solstices, determined the midpoint, and used it. They took the day, hour, minute, and second of the winter solstice preceding the xinsi year of the Zhiyuan reign period as the reference value for the solar terms, and the interval in days between the winter solstice and the new moon as the reference value for intercalation. As for what successive dynasties had…

title: 嘉靖四年江西鄉試錄
text:
謂積年之法俱廢矣以日爲百分分爲百
秒而歷代所謂日法俱廢矣今以其法推
之以歲實加氣應即來歲之冬至也以歲
實加閏應滿朔實去之即來歲之閏餘也
上考往古則每百年長一下驗將來則每
百年消一何其密而備也簡而明也所謂
順天以求合而不爲合以驗天者也夫曆
法之所以易於差忒者以宿度之未真而
宿度之未真以天運之不齊耳何也周天
===
三百六十有五四分之一言其常數也殊
不知天運常有餘而歲運常不足其差甚
微人初不覺晉虞喜以爲五十年退一度
何承天以爲太過倍之而又不及劉焯折
取二家中數爲七十五年折之近似矣然
天有自然之運而以已意斷之可乎故郭
守敬始測景驗氣減周歲爲三百六十五
日二十四分二十五秒加周天爲三百六
十五度二十五分七十五秒强弱相減差
punctuated: 謂積年之法俱廢矣。以日爲百分，分爲百秒，而歷代所謂日法俱廢矣。今以其法推之，以歲實加氣應，即來歲之冬至也；以歲實加閏應，滿朔實去之，即來歲之閏餘也。上考往古，則每百年長一；下驗將來，則每百年消一。何其密而備也，簡而明也！所謂順天以求合，而不爲合以驗天者也。夫曆法之所以易於差忒者，以宿度之未真；而宿度之未真，以天運之不齊耳。何也？周天三百六十有五四分之一，言其常數也。殊不知天運常有餘，而歲運常不足。其差甚微，人初不覺。晉虞喜以爲五十年退一度，何承天以爲太過，倍之而又不及。劉焯折取二家中數，爲七十五年，折之近似矣。然天有自然之運，而以已意斷之，可乎？故郭守敬始測景驗氣，減周歲爲三百六十五日二十四分二十五秒，加周天爲三百六十五度二十五分七十五秒，强弱相減，差
translation_en:
…the methods of accumulated years, as they were called in successive dynasties, were all abandoned. By dividing a day into one hundred parts and each part into one hundred seconds, the so-called day divisors of successive dynasties were likewise all abandoned. Calculating now by this method, adding the length of the year to the solar-term epoch offset gives the winter solstice of the following year; adding the length of the year to the intercalation epoch offset and subtracting complete lunar months gives the intercalary remainder of the following year. In calculating backward into antiquity, one adds one unit for every hundred years; in checking forward into the future, one subtracts one unit for every hundred years. How precise and comprehensive, how simple and clear! This is what is meant by following Heaven to seek agreement, rather than contriving agreement as a test of Heaven.
Calendrical methods readily become inaccurate because the angular measures of the lunar lodges are not exact; and those measures are not exact because celestial motion is not uniform. Why is this? To say that the circuit of Heaven comprises three hundred sixty-five and one-quarter degrees is to state its standard value. This overlooks the fact that the celestial circuit is always slightly in excess, while the annual circuit is always slightly short. The difference is so minute that people initially fail to notice it. Yu Xi of the Jin dynasty held that the retreat was one degree in fifty years. He Chengtian considered this excessive and doubled the interval, but this in turn fell short. Liu Zhuo took the mean of the two estimates, making it seventy-five years; this compromise was close. Yet Heaven has its own natural motion: can one determine it by personal conjecture?
Thus Guo Shoujing began measuring gnomon shadows and verifying the solar terms. He reduced the annual circuit to 365 days, 24 parts, and 25 seconds, and increased the celestial circuit to 365 degrees, 25 parts, and 75 seconds. Subtracting the lesser from the greater gives a difference of…

title: 嘉靖四年江西鄉試錄
text:
一分五十秒積六十六年有奇而退一
定爲歲差夫古未有閏也至堯而後置閏
閏法立則四時之氣候齊矣古未有歲差
也至虞喜諸人而後有歲差歲差立則七
政之經度明矣二者相用而不可偏廢者
也天運之可驗者莫顯於日月之交食而
交食之不爽又係乎朔望之有定耳何也
日行一度月行十三度有奇言其平行也
二十九日有奇而會言其經朔也殊不知
===
日者陽之精也行南陸則盈行北陸則縮
月陰之精也近日則行疾遠日則行遲古
者止用經朔故月一大一小日食或在朔
二月食或在望之前後漢魏以後日食多
在晦其謬蓋坐此也張衡以月行遲疾分
爲九道何承天以日行盈縮推定小餘唐
李淳風作甲子元曆始立定朔之法淳風
又以晦月頻見乃以朔日小餘在日法四
分之三已上者虛進一日謂之進朔進之
punctuated: 一分五十秒，積六十六年有奇而退一，定爲歲差。夫古未有閏也，至堯而後置閏；閏法立，則四時之氣候齊矣。古未有歲差也，至虞喜諸人而後有歲差；歲差立，則七政之經度明矣。二者相用而不可偏廢者也。天運之可驗者，莫顯於日月之交食，而交食之不爽，又係乎朔望之有定耳。何也？日行一度，月行十三度有奇，言其平行也；二十九日有奇而會，言其經朔也。殊不知，日者陽之精也，行南陸則盈，行北陸則縮；月，陰之精也，近日則行疾，遠日則行遲。古者止用經朔，故月一大一小，日食或在朔二，月食或在望之前後。漢魏以後，日食多在晦，其謬蓋坐此也。張衡以月行遲疾分爲九道，何承天以日行盈縮推定小餘。唐李淳風作《甲子元曆》，始立定朔之法。淳風又以晦月頻見，乃以朔日小餘在日法四分之三已上者，虛進一日，謂之進朔。進之
translation_en: …one minute and fifty seconds, accumulating over sixty-six years and a fraction to a regression of one [degree?]; this was established as the annual precession. In antiquity there were initially no intercalary months; only with Yao were they instituted. Once the method of intercalation was established, the seasonal climatic periods were brought into alignment. In antiquity there was initially no allowance for annual precession; only with Yu Xi and others was it introduced. Once annual precession was established, the celestial longitudes of the seven luminaries—the sun, moon, and five planets—became clear. These two methods work together, and neither can be neglected. Among the observable manifestations of celestial motion, none is more evident than solar and lunar eclipses; accurate prediction of eclipses, in turn, depends on precisely determining new and full moons. Why is this? To say that the sun travels one degree and the moon thirteen degrees and a fraction refers to their mean motions. To say that they meet after twenty-nine days and a fraction refers to the mean new moon. What this fails to recognize is that the sun is the essence of yang: it moves faster along its southern course and slower along its northern course. The moon is the essence of yin: it moves swiftly when near the sun and slowly when far from it. In antiquity only the mean new moon was used, so months alternated between long and short, and solar eclipses sometimes fell on the second day of the month [?], while lunar eclipses sometimes fell before or after the full-moon date. From the Han and Wei onward, solar eclipses often fell on the last day of the month; these errors arose from this very practice. Zhang Heng divided the moon’s motion into nine paths according to its variations in speed. He Chengtian used variations in the sun’s motion to calculate the fractional remainder of a day. Li Chunfeng of the Tang compiled the Jiazi Epoch Calendar and first established the method of determining the true new moon. Because the moon was frequently visible on the last day of the month, Chunfeng further stipulated that, when the fractional remainder for the new-moon day was at least three-quarters of the day divisor, the calendar date should be advanced by one day. This was called ‘advancing the new moon.’ Advancing it…

title: 嘉靖四年江西鄉試錄
text:
誠是矣然日纏有自然之度而以己意附
之可乎故虞劆嘗曰朔在會同苟纏次既
合何疑於頻大日月相離何拘於間小一
行亦曰天事誠密雖四大三小庸何傷郭
守敬祖用其說一以辰集時刻所在之日
爲定朔夫定朔立則交會之時日不紊矣
交會準則天運之先後可驗矣二者相因
而不可失一者也我
朝大統曆法悉用授時曆之制洪武中漏刻
===
博士元統節取其法以洪武十七年甲子
爲曆元其實因之而未嘗改也迄今百五
十餘年行之而無弊近年以來因交食之
際有先天後天之不同而不能一一密合
議者遂謂其法已久不能無差而欲增損
之者愚以爲得其人則可不得其人恐未
可輕議也蓋嘗讀元史李謙曆議而玩其
測驗之法自近日以至遠日自近地以至
遠地東極高麗西極滇地南踰朱崖北盡
punctuated:
誠是矣，然日纏有自然之度，而以己意附之，可乎？故虞劆嘗曰：「朔在會同，苟纏次既合，何疑於頻大？日月相離，何拘於間小？」一行亦曰：「天事誠密，雖四大三小，庸何傷？」郭守敬祖用其說，一以辰集時刻所在之日爲定朔。夫定朔立，則交會之時日不紊矣；交會準，則天運之先後可驗矣。二者相因，而不可失一者也。
我朝大統曆法悉用授時曆之制。洪武中，漏刻博士元統節取其法，以洪武十七年甲子爲曆元，其實因之而未嘗改也。迄今百五十餘年，行之而無弊。近年以來，因交食之際有先天後天之不同，而不能一一密合，議者遂謂其法已久，不能無差，而欲增損之者。愚以爲得其人則可，不得其人，恐未可輕議也。蓋嘗讀元史李謙曆議，而玩其測驗之法，自近日以至遠日，自近地以至遠地，東極高麗，西極滇地，南踰朱崖，北盡
translation_en:
…is indeed correct. Yet the sun’s movement has its natural measure: is it permissible to impose one’s own notions upon it? Thus Yu Lian 虞劆 [?] once said: “The beginning of the month lies in conjunction. If the celestial positions have coincided, why be troubled by successive long months? If the sun and moon remain apart, why insist on alternating short months?” Yixing likewise said: “If the calculation of celestial phenomena is truly exact, what harm is there even in four successive long months or three successive short ones?” Guo Shoujing adopted this principle, invariably taking the day containing the precise moment of conjunction as the calculated beginning of the month. Once this beginning is established, the dates and times of conjunction are no longer confused; once conjunctions are accurately determined, advances and delays in celestial motion can be verified. These two depend upon one another, and neither can be neglected.
Our dynasty’s Great Concordance Calendar (Datong li) employs throughout the system of the Season-Granting Calendar (Shoushi li). During the Hongwu reign, Yuan Tong, Erudite of the Clepsydra, selected and adapted its methods, taking the jiazi year, the seventeenth year of Hongwu [1384], as the calendrical epoch. In substance, he followed the existing system without changing it. For more than a hundred and fifty years down to the present, it has been used without defect. In recent years, however, predicted eclipse times have sometimes preceded and sometimes followed the actual celestial events, failing to coincide precisely in every instance. Some commentators therefore maintain that the method, having been in use so long, cannot be free of error, and wish to revise it. In my humble opinion, this may be done if the right person is found; without such a person, I fear revision should not be lightly proposed. I have read Li Qian’s discussion of calendrical methods in the History of the Yuan and carefully considered its methods of observation and verification: from the sun at its nearest to the sun at its farthest [?], and from nearby places to distant ones, extending east to Gaoli, west to the lands of Dian, south beyond Zhuya, and north as far as…

title: 嘉靖四年江西鄉試錄
text:
鐵勒不可謂不精矣而又上考往古自春
秋獻公以來二千一百六十餘年折肯腔
合不可謂不密矣何所據而增損之十或
者又疑元統有年遠數盈漸差天度之說
殊不知所謂歲差云者指冬至日纏赤道
之度耳是故當改者也非謂氣朔也氣朔
不可改也若曰天運難測或有未盡之數
久而方覺則其要又在乎測驗而已今許
衡郭守敬所造簡儀仰儀及諸儀表之制
===
具載於史或可做而行之否乎雖然愚又
有說焉戴記有曰聖人有國則日月不食
星辰不勃朱子曰王者修德行政用賢去
姦能使陽盛足以勝陰則月常避日而不
食是或一道也君天下者於日月之薄蝕
豈可一諉於數哉愚也草茅下士素無師
傳姑舉經史所載者云爾而未敢以爲然
也惟執事進教之
第四問
punctuated:
鐵勒，不可謂不精矣。而又上考往古，自春秋獻公以來二千一百六十餘年，折肯腔合，不可謂不密矣。何所據而增損之？十或者又疑元統有年遠數盈、漸差天度之說，殊不知所謂歲差云者，指冬至日纏赤道之度耳，是故當改者也，非謂氣朔也。氣朔不可改也。若曰天運難測，或有未盡之數，久而方覺，則其要又在乎測驗而已。今許衡、郭守敬所造簡儀、仰儀及諸儀表之制，具載於史，或可做而行之否乎？雖然，愚又有說焉。戴記有曰：「聖人有國，則日月不食，星辰不勃。」朱子曰：「王者修德行政，用賢去姦，能使陽盛足以勝陰，則月常避日而不食。」是或一道也。君天下者，於日月之薄蝕，豈可一諉於數哉？愚也草茅下士，素無師傳，姑舉經史所載者云爾，而未敢以爲然也。惟執事進教之。

第四問
translation_en:
…Tiele: their work cannot be called anything but exact. Moreover, they investigated antiquity, examining more than 2,160 years from the time of Duke Xian in the Spring and Autumn period onward, finding correspondence [?]; their work cannot be called anything but meticulous. On what grounds, then, should it be modified? [?] Some, however, raise doubts because Yuan Tong spoke of numerical excess accumulating over the years and gradually diverging from the celestial degrees. They fail to understand that what is called annual precession refers only to the sun’s position, measured in degrees along the equator, at the winter solstice. This, therefore, is what should be adjusted; it does not refer to the solar terms and new moons. The solar terms and new moons must not be altered. If one says that the movements of Heaven are difficult to fathom and that some numerical factors may remain unaccounted for, becoming apparent only after a long time, then the essential task again lies simply in observation and verification. The designs of the simplified instrument, the upward-facing instrument, and the other instruments and gnomons constructed by Xu Heng and Guo Shoujing are fully recorded in the histories. Might they be reproduced and put into use?

Nevertheless, I have another point to offer. The Record of Rites associated with Dai states: “When a sage possesses a state, the sun and moon are not eclipsed, and the stars do not run contrary to their courses.” Master Zhu said: “If a ruler cultivates virtue and conducts government, employs the worthy and removes the wicked, and can make yang sufficiently strong to overcome yin, then the moon will always avoid the sun, and no eclipse will occur.” This, perhaps, is also a way. How could one who rules all under Heaven attribute eclipses of the sun and moon entirely to numerical cycles? I am a humble scholar in private life and have never received instruction from a master. I have merely adduced what is recorded in the classics and histories, without daring to claim that my account is correct. I ask you, honored examiner, to instruct me further.

Fourth Question

Comment by Associate Examiner Cai, Assistant Instructor: The Rites of Zhou is [?] a great canon for ordering the world. In establishing offices through the study of antiquity, our dynasty has drawn extensively upon it as a model; it is fitting that this should bring about enlightened government. Yet the book has long fallen into obscurity and has not been transmitted in its entirety. Its circulation does not equal that of even a single philosophical or historical work. How deeply regrettable! You have probed its underlying meaning to the very bottom and developed a detailed and lucid answer.
