title: 嘉靖四年江西鄉試錄
text:
所其可俗者棄之矣縱小功之不察而廢
二伞可乎不可況而況將所其可師者棄
之矣一胸之不下而廢朝夕可乎今夫聖
遠不亦不見其盛猶亦得見其書其全篇
盡信者勢也或觭以蔽知或觕以就正皆
是也可因小而盡疑其大哉其大經大法
大義炳炳炳在也而世迹經殘不能一一
又纍纍可行也而時異勢殊不能一一
附者亦勢也或附之而準今或迹之以合
===
俗亦宜也可況迹而不師其意乎夫然則
可以讀天下之書論天下之事而一無難
處者矣況周禮之書之大尤當講求而法
行者乎敢因明問而陳其槩夫周禮者聖
人經世之書也周公以其盡倫之體而爲
盡制之用本乎内聖之學而爲外王之規
上自黄帝以迄二代順風氣之宜因時勢
之變斟酌而損益之蓋集百聖之大成立
一王之定制觀其篇首每曰惟王建國辨
punctuated:
所其可俗者棄之矣。縱小功之不察而廢二伞，可乎？不可。況而況將所其可師者棄之矣。一胸之不下而廢朝夕，可乎？今夫聖遠，不亦不見其盛，猶亦得見其書。其全篇盡信者，勢也；或觭以蔽知，或觕以就正，皆是也。可因小而盡疑其大哉？其大經、大法、大義，炳炳炳在也。而世迹經殘，不能一一；又纍纍可行也，而時異勢殊，不能一一附者，亦勢也。或附之而準今，或迹之以合俗，亦宜也。可況迹而不師其意乎？夫然則可以讀天下之書，論天下之事，而一無難處者矣。況周禮之書之大，尤當講求而法行者乎？敢因明問而陳其槩。
夫周禮者，聖人經世之書也。周公以其盡倫之體，而爲盡制之用，本乎内聖之學，而爲外王之規。上自黄帝以迄二代，順風氣之宜，因時勢之變，斟酌而損益之，蓋集百聖之大成，立一王之定制。觀其篇首，每曰：「惟王建國，辨
translation_en:
…what could be [followed?] would thus be cast aside [?]. Even if some minor achievement went unrecognized, would it be permissible to discard the “two canopies” [?]? No. How much less should one cast aside what could serve as a model [?]. Would one abandon morning and evening because “one breast does not descend” [?]? Now the sages are distant from us: although we cannot witness their flourishing age, we can still see their writings. That their entire texts should be trusted is a consequence of the circumstances [?]. Whether something is partial and obscures understanding, or rough and awaits correction, this applies in either case [?]. Can we doubt everything great in them because of something small? Their great guiding principles, great institutions, and great moral teachings remain brilliantly manifest. Yet the traces of past ages and the surviving classics are fragmentary, so not everything can be [recovered?]. Moreover, although many things could be put into practice, times and circumstances differ, and not everything can be made to fit: this too follows from the circumstances. It is appropriate either to adapt them by taking the present as the standard, or to follow their traces in ways suited to current customs [?]. Can one attend to their traces without taking their underlying intention as one's model [?]? If one proceeds in this way, one may read the books of the world and discuss its affairs without encountering anything impossible to handle. How much more does this apply to a book as great as the Rites of Zhou, which especially deserves investigation and practical implementation as a model! In response to your discerning question, I venture to set forth its broad outlines.
The Rites of Zhou is a book through which a sage ordered the world. The Duke of Zhou took the complete fulfillment of human relationships as the underlying substance and gave it practical expression in a comprehensive institutional order. Grounded in the learning of inner sagehood, he established the standards of outward kingship. Drawing upon the Yellow Emperor and continuing through the two dynasties, he followed what was appropriate to prevailing customs and conditions, responded to changes in the circumstances of the times, and judiciously made reductions and additions. Thus he brought together the accumulated achievements of the many sages and established the settled institutions of a king. Consider how the opening of each section says: “The king, in establishing the capital, distinguishes…”

title: 嘉靖四年江西鄉試錄
text:
方正位體國經野設官分職以為民極則
其非止治岐之政理財之書可見矣故其
旨遠其事密其義該尚而當盡而不迂上
而天地日月如土均土圭之法下而封域
山川若封人虎衛之制著而禮樂刑政若
肆師大司樂土師之掌微而禽獸草木若
內饔甸師醢人食醫之事纖悉備具蓋誠
有以極規模之大盡節目之詳建天地質
鬼神已驗於當時而不利於來世者也漢
===
唐以來雖未能悉遵古制而官聯服御車
旗禮儀之節率有取焉猶為圓之不能踰
規方之不能外矩者亦可以見是書之可
尊與其法之可行也斷然矣夫何秦火之
餘此書晚出巖壁河間獻王得而上之又
取考工記以補冬官之闕故武帝因謂末
世瀆亂之書成帝時劉歆校理秘書識其
可用遂輔新室以泉府理財之說故漢儒
始有六國陰謀之訾歆不足責也至於鄭
punctuated:
方正位，體國經野，設官分職，以為民極」，則其非止治岐之政、理財之書可見矣。故其旨遠，其事密，其義該，尚而當，盡而不迂。上而天地日月，如土均、土圭之法；下而封域山川，若封人、虎衛之制；著而禮樂刑政，若肆師、大司樂、土師之掌；微而禽獸草木，若內饔、甸師、醢人、食醫之事，纖悉備具。蓋誠有以極規模之大，盡節目之詳，建天地，質鬼神，已驗於當時而不利於來世者也。漢唐以來，雖未能悉遵古制，而官聯、服御、車旗、禮儀之節，率有取焉。猶為圓之不能踰規，方之不能外矩者，亦可以見是書之可尊與其法之可行也，斷然矣。
夫何秦火之餘，此書晚出巖壁，河間獻王得而上之，又取《考工記》以補冬官之闕，故武帝因謂末世瀆亂之書。成帝時，劉歆校理秘書，識其可用，遂輔新室以泉府理財之說，故漢儒始有六國陰謀之訾。歆不足責也，至於鄭
translation_en:
…directions and establish the proper positions, lay out the capital and demarcate the countryside, establish offices and allocate duties, thereby providing the people with a supreme standard.” Thus it is clear that this is more than a record of government in Qi or a book on managing wealth. Its purport is far-reaching, its provisions meticulous, and its meaning comprehensive: lofty yet fitting, exhaustive yet not impractical. Above, it embraces heaven and earth, the sun and moon, as in the methods of land equalization and the earth gnomon; below, territorial boundaries, mountains, and rivers, as in the institutions of the Boundary Officers and “Tiger Guards” [?]. In conspicuous matters, it covers rites, music, punishments, and government, as in the responsibilities of the Masters of Sacrifices, the Music Master, and the “Land Officers” [?]; in minute matters, birds and beasts, plants and trees, as in the duties of the Inner Cooks, Directors of the Royal Fields, Makers of Pickled Foods, and Dietitians. Every detail is fully provided for. Indeed, it encompasses the utmost breadth of institutional design and exhausts the particulars of its provisions. Established before heaven and earth and submitted to the spirits for judgment, it had already proved effective in its own time, yet was of no benefit to later ages [?]. Since the Han and Tang, although the ancient institutions could not be followed in their entirety, arrangements for coordinating offices, imperial attire and equipment, carriages and banners, and ceremonial observances have generally drawn upon it. Just as a circle cannot depart from the compass or a square from the carpenter’s square, this demonstrates conclusively that the book deserves reverence and that its methods can be put into practice.
How, then, did matters come to this? After the Qin book-burning, this book emerged only belatedly from a rock wall. Prince Xian of Hejian obtained it and presented it to the throne, also using the Record of Artificers (Kaogong ji) to fill the missing section on the Offices of Winter. Emperor Wu consequently called it a book of a degenerate age, profane and disorderly. During Emperor Cheng’s reign, Liu Xin collated the books in the imperial repository and recognized its practical value. He subsequently assisted the Xin dynasty using its doctrines on managing wealth through the Treasury Office (Quanfu). Hence Han scholars began to disparage it as a work of clandestine schemes from the Six States. Liu Xin is hardly worth reproaching; as for Zheng…

title: 嘉靖四年江西鄉試錄
text:
玄析袁劉杜二鄭爲之註疏然一引緯書
訛於天帝之異名二引司馬法誤以丘乘
爲丘甸三引春秋傳謂王服止於九章四
引左傳國語謂我周之有分野五引漢儒
禮記則以夫人而亂王后副褘之飾此其
失也然此皆其小者也一節可疑不害於
全體之可信冬官雖缺而五官固在也考
工記特任萬民之一職宜不足以厭學者
之心而籍其口吴澄謂冬官未嘗亡雜於五
===
官之中者未爲無據至於三易則大卜筮
人之守四詩則大師籥章之司尚書爲外
史之職春秋亦太史之事總其全書當必
包括五經蓋不特相爲表裏者而其精華
純粹固已見於夫子久矣是其大者之必
可信如此故唐書謂其義可幽贊神明文
可經緯邦國程子謂周禮一書須知道者
觀之可決是非而朱子亦謂其間細碎處
雖可疑其大體直是非聖人不能作故愚
punctuated:
玄析袁劉杜二鄭，爲之註疏。然一引緯書，訛於天帝之異名；二引司馬法，誤以丘乘爲丘甸；三引春秋傳，謂王服止於九章；四引左傳國語，謂我周之有分野；五引漢儒禮記，則以夫人而亂王后副褘之飾。此其失也。然此皆其小者也，一節可疑，不害於全體之可信。冬官雖缺，而五官固在也。考工記特任萬民之一職，宜不足以厭學者之心而籍其口。吴澄謂冬官未嘗亡，雜於五官之中者，未爲無據。
至於三易，則大卜筮人之守；四詩，則大師籥章之司；尚書爲外史之職，春秋亦太史之事。總其全書，當必包括五經，蓋不特相爲表裏者，而其精華純粹，固已見於夫子久矣。是其大者之必可信如此。故唐書謂其義可幽贊神明，文可經緯邦國。程子謂周禮一書，須知道者觀之，可決是非。而朱子亦謂其間細碎處雖可疑，其大體直是非聖人不能作。故愚
translation_en:
…[Zheng] Xuan analyzed the interpretations of Yuan, Liu, Du, and the two Zhengs [?], providing commentary and elucidation for it. Yet, first, he cited the apocryphal writings and erred concerning the different names of Heaven and the Supreme Deity; second, he cited the Methods of the Minister of War and mistakenly equated qiu and sheng with qiu and dian, units of territorial and military organization; third, he cited the Commentary on the Spring and Autumn Annals and asserted that the king’s robes bore only nine emblems; fourth, he cited the Zuo Commentary and the Discourses of the States to assert that our Zhou had terrestrial regions corresponding to celestial divisions; fifth, he cited the Record of Rites transmitted by Han scholars, confusing the ornaments of the queen’s headdress and ceremonial robe with those of the wives of regional lords. These were his errors. Yet all these are minor matters. Doubt about one passage does not impair the trustworthiness of the whole. Although the Offices of Winter are missing, the other five offices certainly remain. The Record of Artificers concerns only one of the occupations assigned to the myriad people; it is understandably insufficient to satisfy scholars’ minds and silence their objections [?]. Wu Cheng’s assertion that the Offices of Winter were never lost, but are scattered among the other five offices, is not without foundation.
As for the three Changes, they were in the keeping of the Grand Diviner and the milfoil diviners; the four divisions of the Odes were under the supervision of the Grand Music Master and the officials responsible for flute music. The Book of Documents belonged to the duties of the Outer Scribe, and the Spring and Autumn Annals likewise concerned the Grand Scribe. Taken as a whole, the book must encompass the Five Classics. Indeed, it does more than complement them: its purest essence had long since been recognized by the Master, Confucius. Such is the necessary trustworthiness of its major principles. Thus the History of the Tang says that its meaning can mysteriously assist the divine powers, and its text can order states and realms. Master Cheng said that only someone who understands the Way can read the Rites of Zhou and determine what is right and wrong. Master Zhu likewise said that although its minute details may admit of doubt, its general structure is certainly something that only a sage could have produced. Thus, in my humble view…

title: 嘉靖四年江西鄉試錄
text:
謂或闕之以俟知或補之以就正但信其
大而不屑屑於其小者亦庶乎可以尊先
聖之經矣至若元魏北齊以來授田分鄉
者蓋十用其一二蘇綽在周約六典以建
官府兵之制微有端緒亦十用其五六隋
文帝之富盛蘇威文景之積益亦既十用
其七八矣而治不古若者蓋竊聖人之似
而不得其真況皆舉一而廢百得此而失
彼夫王道如精金美玉豈容雜也雜則敗
===
矣故曰假而用之者莽也輕而用之者綽
也誤而用之者安石也而蘇子所謂大用
則王小用則亡者也若數人者蓋知王道
而小用之也豈周禮之罪哉至唐太宗則
尤可怪者觀夫貞觀之治世業以授田租
庸調以取民七百三十員以建官十六衛
八百府以置兵雖於周禮多所摸倣至其
言曰周禮真聖作也不井田不封建不肉
刑欲行周公之道不可得也夫太宗居可
punctuated:
謂或闕之以俟知，或補之以就正，但信其大而不屑屑於其小者，亦庶乎可以尊先聖之經矣。至若元魏北齊以來授田分鄉者，蓋十用其一二；蘇綽在周，約六典以建官，府兵之制微有端緒，亦十用其五六；隋文帝之富盛，蘇威文景之積益，亦既十用其七八矣。而治不古若者，蓋竊聖人之似而不得其真，況皆舉一而廢百，得此而失彼。夫王道如精金美玉，豈容雜也？雜則敗矣。故曰：「假而用之者，莽也；輕而用之者，綽也；誤而用之者，安石也。」而蘇子所謂「大用則王，小用則亡」者也。若數人者，蓋知王道而小用之也，豈周禮之罪哉？
至唐太宗，則尤可怪者。觀夫貞觀之治，世業以授田，租庸調以取民，七百三十員以建官，十六衛八百府以置兵，雖於周禮多所摸倣，至其言曰：「周禮真聖作也。不井田，不封建，不肉刑，欲行周公之道，不可得也。」夫太宗居可
translation_en:
…maintain that we may leave gaps pending fuller understanding, or supply what is missing to arrive at a correct text. If we simply trust its main principles without fussing over its minor details, we may come close to honoring the classic of the ancient sage. As for the allocation of land and organization of townships from the Northern Wei and Northern Qi onward, these employed perhaps one or two tenths of its teachings. When Su Chuo served under Zhou, he drew on the Six Statutes to establish offices; the beginnings of the militia system were also faintly discernible. This employed perhaps five or six tenths. The wealth and prosperity under Emperor Wen of Sui, and the accumulated contributions of Su Wei and Wen Jing [?], already represented the use of seven or eight tenths. Yet their government fell short of antiquity because they borrowed the semblance of the sage’s institutions without grasping their reality. Moreover, they adopted one measure while abandoning a hundred, gaining this while losing that. The Way of the True King is like refined gold or fine jade: how could it admit adulteration? Adulterate it, and it is ruined. Thus it is said: “Mang employed it as a pretext; Chuo employed it lightly; Anshi employed it mistakenly.” This is what Master Su meant by “Employ it fully, and one becomes a true king; employ it partially, and one perishes.” These men knew the Way of the True King but employed it only partially. How could that be the fault of the Rites of Zhou?
The case of Emperor Taizong of Tang is still more puzzling. Consider the government of the Zhenguan reign: land was allotted as hereditary holdings; taxes in grain, labor service or its commutation, and textiles were exacted from the people; 730 officials staffed the administration; and sixteen guards and eight hundred garrisons organized the troops. Although much of this imitated the Rites of Zhou, he went so far as to say: “The Rites of Zhou is truly the work of a sage. Without the well-field system, the enfeoffment of hereditary lords, and mutilating punishments, it is impossible to put the Duke of Zhou’s Way into practice.” Now Taizong occupied a position from which he could…

title: 嘉靖四年江西鄉試錄
text:
致之位又當開創之初使其悉意經理以
爲民極何不可者顧乃付之浩歎而不盡
用豈非悅而不繹雜而無本故邪其漸不
克終有自矣然此皆其迹也師迹而無實
不若師意而可行今夫立於百世之上以
俟乎百世之下者聖人之心也奮乎百世
之下而攷諸百世之上者吾人之志也有
時焉不能以皆合勢爲不可以强同令之
不可爲古猶古之不可以爲今也聖人且
===
柰何哉於此不師其意可乎夫冢宰總六
典佐王均邦國者今冢宰固設也唯其能
一天下之政巳矣五官各一職佐王治邦
國者今五官固設也唯其能理庶官之政
巳矣每卿六十屬今六卿之屬固不止三
百六十也可以意汰之乎井牧之法難行
矣授田限田以養民其可乎鄉三物之法
不行矣學校賓興將大比其德行可乎爵
秩固懸也而無封疆朝覲固擧也而無聘
punctuated:
致之位，又當開創之初，使其悉意經理，以爲民極，何不可者？顧乃付之浩歎而不盡用，豈非悅而不繹，雜而無本故邪？其漸不克終有自矣。然此皆其迹也。師迹而無實，不若師意而可行。今夫立於百世之上，以俟乎百世之下者，聖人之心也；奮乎百世之下，而攷諸百世之上者，吾人之志也。有時焉不能以皆合，勢爲不可以强同。令之不可爲古，猶古之不可以爲今也。聖人且柰何哉？於此不師其意可乎？
夫冢宰總六典，佐王均邦國者，今冢宰固設也，唯其能一天下之政巳矣。五官各一職，佐王治邦國者，今五官固設也，唯其能理庶官之政巳矣。每卿六十屬，今六卿之屬固不止三百六十也，可以意汰之乎？井牧之法難行矣，授田限田以養民，其可乎？鄉三物之法不行矣，學校賓興，將大比其德行可乎？爵秩固懸也，而無封疆；朝覲固擧也，而無聘
translation_en:
…a position from which he could accomplish this, and moreover lived at the beginning of a new dynasty. Had he devoted his whole mind to ordering its affairs and establishing a standard for the people, what could he not have achieved? Yet he merely gave way to profound sighs and failed to put these institutions fully into practice. Was this not because he delighted in them without pursuing their implications, and mixed practices together without a firm foundation? There was a reason why his course gradually failed to reach its proper conclusion. Yet all these are only outward traces. To imitate the traces without their substance is inferior to following their intent in a practicable way. To stand a hundred generations in the past and await those a hundred generations later: this is the mind of the sage. To bestir ourselves a hundred generations later and investigate what lay a hundred generations before: this is our aspiration. Circumstances sometimes prevent complete correspondence, and conditions cannot forcibly be made identical. The present [?] cannot be made into antiquity, just as antiquity cannot be made into the present. What could even a sage do about this? In these circumstances, can we fail to follow their intent?
The Minister of State (zhongzai) oversaw the Six Canons of government and assisted the king in bringing the states into balance. Today the office of Minister of State is indeed established; what matters is simply his ability to unify the administration of all under Heaven. The other five ministers each held a distinct responsibility and assisted the king in governing the states. Today these five offices are indeed established; what matters is simply their ability to order the administration of the various officials. Each minister had sixty subordinate officers. Today the subordinates of the six ministers certainly number more than three hundred and sixty. Could their numbers be reduced in accordance with the original intent? The system of well-field divisions and pastoral allotments is difficult to implement. Could land be allotted and limits placed on landholdings to sustain the people? The system of the three categories of township instruction is no longer practiced. Could schools honor and recommend worthy men, conducting a great triennial assessment of their virtue and conduct? Ranks and stipends are indeed established, but there are no territorial fiefs; court audiences are indeed held, but there are no diplomatic visits…

title: 嘉靖四年江西鄉試錄
text:
問所以酌今之宜而不失古之意者可講
也又其大者如比閭族黨州鄉之民卽所
以爲伍兩卒旅師軍之衆此則周家致太
平之基也今以其意而容民畜衆可乎冢
宰制王之左右自飲食衣服侍從之類無
不禀命焉此又所以防君側之惡而謹其
心術之微也今欲使之出入起居罔有不
臧左右前後無非正人豈無可義起之法
乎凡此皆其意之可師者也孔子所謂殷
===
因於夏禮周因於殷禮所損益可知者今
將損益周禮而用之可不可也昔者周公
兼三王以施四事其有不合者仰思繼日
安知周禮所載非其得之待旦者乎設令
周公可復作焉其所以仰思待旦不知又
何如也故愚以爲或酌之以今或通之
而宜俗直師其意而不拘拘於其迹者亦
庶乎可以遵先王之法矣雖然意固師古
之方心實行法之本故不忍人之政由於
punctuated:
問。所以酌今之宜而不失古之意者，可講也。又其大者，如比閭族黨州鄉之民，卽所以爲伍兩卒旅師軍之衆，此則周家致太平之基也。今以其意而容民畜衆，可乎？冢宰制王之左右，自飲食衣服侍從之類，無不禀命焉。此又所以防君側之惡，而謹其心術之微也。今欲使之出入起居罔有不臧，左右前後無非正人，豈無可義起之法乎？凡此皆其意之可師者也。孔子所謂「殷因於夏禮，周因於殷禮，所損益可知」者，今將損益周禮而用之，可不可也？昔者周公兼三王以施四事，其有不合者，仰思繼日，安知周禮所載非其得之待旦者乎？設令周公可復作焉，其所以仰思待旦，不知又何如也。故愚以爲，或酌之以今，或通之而宜俗，直師其意而不拘拘於其迹者，亦庶乎可以遵先王之法矣。
雖然，意固師古之方，心實行法之本。故不忍人之政由於
translation_en:
…diplomatic inquiries. How to weigh what is appropriate today without losing the intent of antiquity is a matter that can be discussed. Among the more important institutions, the people organized into bi, lü, zu, dang, zhou, and xiang were precisely those who formed the military units of wu, liang, zu, lü, shi, and jun. This was the foundation upon which the Zhou house achieved Great Peace. Could we now follow its intent in accommodating the people and nurturing the multitude? The Minister of State controlled those around the king: all those concerned with his food, clothing, and personal attendance took their orders from him. This also served to guard against evil at the ruler’s side and to exercise vigilance over the subtle workings of his mind. If we now wish to ensure that his movements and daily conduct are invariably good, and that those around him are all upright people, surely there are institutions we could devise on the basis of what is right? In all these matters, their underlying intent can serve as our model. Confucius said, “The Yin followed the rites of the Xia; the Zhou followed the rites of the Yin; what they subtracted and added can be known.” Could we now subtract from and add to the Rites of Zhou and put them into practice? Formerly, the Duke of Zhou drew together the precedents of the Three Kings to carry out four undertakings. Wherever something did not accord, he looked upward in thought, continuing through the night. How do we know that what is recorded in the Rites of Zhou was not what he arrived at while awaiting dawn? Suppose the Duke of Zhou could arise again: we cannot know what his reflections as he looked upward and awaited dawn would now be like. Thus, in my humble opinion, if we assess these institutions in light of present circumstances or adapt them to suit prevailing customs, taking their intent directly as our model without clinging narrowly to their outward forms, we may come close to following the laws of the former kings.
Nevertheless, although grasping their intent is the way to take antiquity as our model, the heart is truly the foundation for putting laws into practice. Thus, government that cannot bear to see others suffer arises from…

title: 嘉靖四年江西鄉試錄
text:
不忍人之心非有關雎麟趾之意則不可
以行周官之法度我
國家深仁厚澤重熈累洽百五六十年于茲
正薫蒸融液積德可興之時也昔
太祖稽古建官悉依六典是其大者固已尊信
篤行特未盡而若有待焉耳恭惟
皇上神聖中興孜孜化理而群賢一德協和賛
襄斯所謂人存政舉者倘以是書列之
經筵措諸典禮則成周之治復見今日此千
===
載一時也草茅雖賤豈無王仲淹之志惟
與其進尚當有以
獻焉
第五問
畢□□□
同考試官教諭陳　批〔災異之理不明久矣以諸儒之說不定則省脩之道亦無所主子能折衷諸說之得失而〕
以正心格天爲本斷制精當深切
聖志要非言語文字之學所可及者
punctuated:
不忍人之心，非有《關雎》《麟趾》之意，則不可以行《周官》之法度。我國家深仁厚澤，重熈累洽，百五六十年于茲，正薫蒸融液、積德可興之時也。昔太祖稽古建官，悉依六典，是其大者固已尊信篤行，特未盡而若有待焉耳。恭惟皇上神聖中興，孜孜化理，而群賢一德協和賛襄，斯所謂人存政舉者。倘以是書列之經筵，措諸典禮，則成周之治復見今日，此千載一時也。草茅雖賤，豈無王仲淹之志？惟與其進，尚當有以獻焉。

第五問
畢□□□

同考試官教諭陳　批〔災異之理不明久矣，以諸儒之說不定，則省脩之道亦無所主。子能折衷諸說之得失，而〕以正心格天爲本，斷制精當，深切聖志，要非言語文字之學所可及者。
translation_en:
…a heart that cannot bear the suffering of others. Without the spirit expressed in “Guanju” (Ospreys) and “Linzhi” (The Qilin’s Hoofs), one cannot put into practice the laws and institutions of the Offices of Zhou. Our dynasty’s profound benevolence and abundant bounty have brought successive generations of flourishing peace for a hundred and fifty or sixty years now. This is precisely the time when their pervasive, transforming influence and accumulated virtue can bring about a renewal. Formerly, Taizu consulted antiquity in establishing offices, following the Six Statutes throughout. Their principal provisions were thus already honored, trusted, and earnestly practiced; only their full implementation remained unfinished, as though awaiting a later time. Reverently considering Your Majesty’s sagely and divine restoration of the dynasty, your tireless pursuit of moral transformation and good government, and the worthy ministers united in virtue and harmoniously assisting you, this is what is meant by saying that when the right men are present, government flourishes. If this book were included in the Classics Colloquium and its provisions embodied in institutions and rites, the good government of the Zhou at its height would appear again today. This is an opportunity encountered once in a thousand years. Though I am merely a humble man of the countryside, how could I lack the aspirations of Wang Zhongyan? If only my advancement is encouraged, I shall yet have something to offer.

Fifth Question
Bi □□□ [name partly illegible]

Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor: 〔The principles underlying calamities and anomalies have long been unclear. Because the explanations of the various Confucian scholars remain unsettled, the way of self-examination and cultivation likewise has no fixed guide. You have weighed the merits and shortcomings of these explanations and〕 taken rectifying the heart to move Heaven as your foundation. Your judgments are precise and fitting, and accord deeply with the imperial intent. This is certainly beyond the reach of learning confined to words and literary composition.

title: 嘉靖四年江西鄉試錄
text:
考試官教授吳　批〔論災異所以成就　于此子能言之其必究天人之學而得其門者矣〕
聖明之德善推天心仁愛之意末以聖人無災異而亦懼則聖賢傳心要法正在
考試官教授王　批〔論天人相與之際精切允當　如此可以為矣〕
且忠藎之意溢於言外非深達政體者固未易到也有士
上天垂戒之意徵于變人君弭變之實存
乎德災異之來固所以成人君之德也脩
德以消變則人事備而天道順仁愛之意
===
寓于拂逆之中無言之妙亦惟應之以心
而已是其休祥滋至所以益吾之過而災
異疊興者適所以增吾之不能豈可以常
數自諉而忘其恐懼之念哉執事發策以
災異為問蓋有切於當時之急務仰見我
皇上憂勤之心而欲為
聖德之裨也嘗聞天人一理感應一機中漢之
際相為流通自夫叔興之說行而後天人
之理荒甘石之言出而後感應之機誣矣
punctuated:
考試官教授吳批〔論災異所以成就，于此子能言之，其必究天人之學而得其門者矣。〕聖明之德，善推天心仁愛之意，末以聖人無災異而亦懼，則聖賢傳心要法正在。

考試官教授王批〔論天人相與之際，精切允當，如此可以為矣。〕且忠藎之意溢於言外，非深達政體者固未易到也。有士。

上天垂戒之意徵于變，人君弭變之實存乎德。災異之來，固所以成人君之德也。脩德以消變，則人事備而天道順。仁愛之意寓于拂逆之中，無言之妙亦惟應之以心而已。是其休祥滋至，所以益吾之過，而災異疊興者，適所以增吾之不能，豈可以常數自諉而忘其恐懼之念哉？執事發策以災異為問，蓋有切於當時之急務，仰見我皇上憂勤之心，而欲為聖德之裨也。嘗聞天人一理，感應一機，中漢之際，相為流通。自夫叔興之說行，而後天人之理荒；甘石之言出，而後感應之機誣矣。
translation_en:
Comment by Examiner Wu, Professor: “The discussion explains how disasters and anomalies bring the virtue of an enlightened sovereign to completion, and aptly elucidates the benevolent intentions of Heaven. It concludes that even sages remain fearful when there are no disasters or anomalies: precisely herein lies the essential method by which sages and worthies transmit their understanding of the mind. This candidate can articulate this; he must have investigated the learning concerning Heaven and humanity and found its entrance.” [The transcription dislocates portions of this comment between the annotation and the main text; their sequence is reconstructed here.]

Comment by Examiner Wang, Professor: “The discussion of the interaction between Heaven and humanity is penetrating, precise, and sound. Moreover, an attitude of devoted loyalty overflows beyond the words themselves. Such a level could hardly be attained without a profound understanding of the workings of government. With scholars such as this, much can be accomplished.” [The final wording is dislocated in the transcription; its reconstruction is doubtful [?].]

Heaven above manifests its intention to warn through abnormal phenomena; the substance of a ruler’s efforts to quell such phenomena lies in his virtue. The arrival of disasters and anomalies is indeed a means of bringing the ruler’s virtue to completion. If he cultivates virtue to dispel abnormal phenomena, human affairs will be properly ordered and Heaven’s course harmonious. Benevolent intentions reside within adversity; the subtlety of Heaven’s wordless instruction requires only that one respond with the heart. Thus, the ever more frequent arrival of auspicious signs may increase my faults, whereas disasters and anomalies arising repeatedly serve precisely to augment what I am incapable of [?]. How, then, could one excuse oneself by attributing these things to fixed numerical cycles and forget the need for fear and apprehension?

You, honored examiners, have issued a policy question concerning disasters and anomalies, surely because it bears upon the urgent business of the present time. You reverently perceive our Emperor’s anxious diligence and wish to contribute to his sagely virtue. I have heard that Heaven and humanity share one principle, and that stimulus and response operate through a single mechanism, communicating freely with each other in the intervening realm [?; the transcription reads “中漢”]. Only after Shuxing’s explanation gained currency was the principle linking Heaven and humanity neglected; only after the teachings of Gan and Shi appeared was the mechanism of stimulus and response misrepresented.

title: 嘉靖四年江西鄉試錄
text:
殊不知匹夫匹婦猶能召日星之變致雨
雪之災矧人君爲天地民物之主繫四海
休戚之命哉人事之得失陰陽之順逆此
感彼應捷於影響未可以迹邇異勢遽忘
其參若之道也世世儒論災異者家異其傳
人異其說致天道之不明啓人君之不信
乃自謂其術足以探上玄其功足以開后
世其貽害豈淺哉春秋紀災異以爲人事
之感召特以示畏天戒而已公羊作傳已
===
非聖人之意董仲舒又衍其說以著陰陽
論至火災之對專以刑罰不中爲言其失
愈甚真德秀譏其傳會宜矣所可取者天
人三策其庶幾格君之學乎洪範以五行
之變歸之五事之應槩言其理而已穀梁
有傳已非君子所取劉向又廣其說以著
五行傳至以五行五事各分類應蘇老泉
譏其牽强宜矣所可取者條陳封事其庶
幾天道之驗乎當是時夏侯勝京房之輩
punctuated: 殊不知匹夫匹婦猶能召日星之變，致雨雪之災，矧人君爲天地民物之主，繫四海休戚之命哉！人事之得失，陰陽之順逆，此感彼應，捷於影響，未可以迹邇異勢，遽忘其參若之道也。世世儒論災異者，家異其傳，人異其說，致天道之不明，啓人君之不信，乃自謂其術足以探上玄，其功足以開后世，其貽害豈淺哉！《春秋》紀災異，以爲人事之感召，特以示畏天戒而已。《公羊》作傳，已非聖人之意。董仲舒又衍其說，以著《陰陽論》，至火災之對，專以刑罰不中爲言，其失愈甚。真德秀譏其傳會，宜矣。所可取者，《天人三策》，其庶幾格君之學乎！《洪範》以五行之變歸之五事之應，槩言其理而已。《穀梁》有傳，已非君子所取。劉向又廣其說，以著《五行傳》，至以五行、五事各分類應，蘇老泉譏其牽强，宜矣。所可取者，條陳封事，其庶幾天道之驗乎！當是時，夏侯勝、京房之輩
translation_en:
They fail altogether to understand that even an ordinary man or woman can call forth anomalies of the sun and stars and bring about disasters of rain and snow. How much more so the ruler, who presides over Heaven and Earth, the people and all things, and upon whom the fortunes of all within the Four Seas depend! Successes and failures in human affairs, and the harmonious or contrary workings of yin and yang: a stimulus here elicits a response there, swifter than shadow or echo. One must not, because their manifestations are near yet their circumstances differ [?], abruptly forget the principle of their mutual correspondence [?]. Confucian scholars of successive ages who discuss disasters and anomalies each transmit a different tradition and offer a different explanation. They obscure the Way of Heaven and induce disbelief in rulers, yet claim that their methods suffice to fathom Heaven’s mysteries and their achievements to enlighten later ages. Can the harm they bequeath be slight?

The Spring and Autumn Annals records disasters and anomalies as things elicited by human affairs, solely to demonstrate reverence for Heaven’s warnings. The Gongyang Commentary already departed from the sage’s intent. Dong Zhongshu further elaborated its explanations in his Discourse on Yin and Yang; in his reply concerning a fire disaster, he spoke exclusively of punishments being improperly applied, making his error still greater. Zhen Dexiu was right to criticize his forced associations. What merits acceptance is his Three Policy Responses on Heaven and Man: these perhaps approach the learning that rectifies the ruler!

The Great Plan attributes changes in the Five Phases to their responses to the Five Activities, merely setting out the principle in general terms. The Guliang Commentary already contained explanations that the gentleman would not accept. Liu Xiang further expanded its explanations to compose his Commentary on the Five Phases, going so far as to classify the Five Phases and Five Activities separately and assign corresponding responses to each. Su Laoquan was right to criticize these strained connections. What merits acceptance is his itemized exposition in sealed memorials: these perhaps come close to demonstrating the workings of the Way of Heaven! At that time, men such as Xiahou Sheng and Jing Fang…

title: 嘉靖四年江西鄉試錄
text:
既跡此而騰其說谷永李尋之徒復假此
以濟其姦則又二子之所弗取也至如𣏌
宗元言受命不于其天至上尊號表復條
陳其瑞應盖先人事而后天道亦非盡棄
其瑞應也可盡以是非柳耶歐陽脩以不
畏天變爲欺君至讀蜀書以麟鳳龜龍爲
常事盖王建紀載之謬偶述而誦之耳可
遽以是病歐耶夫諸儒之論說不一則人
君之脩省靡宗至其脩省弗應遂謂天之
===
與人衆不相關而作善之念微矣嘗考論
災祥之埋莫過於商書辯脩省之道莫過
于王嘉書曰天道福善禍淫持此以論而
后春秋洪範之理明矣嘉以應天以實不
以文執此以往而后董仲舒劉向之說破
矣我
皇上即位以來水旱疊奏於郡國火災再見於
宮闈盖天心仁愛俾
聖德之成同符五帝蘇功三王而益之雖然太
punctuated:
既跡此而騰其說，谷永、李尋之徒復假此以濟其姦，則又二子之所弗取也。至如𣏌宗元言受命不于其天，至上尊號表，復條陳其瑞應，盖先人事而后天道，亦非盡棄其瑞應也，可盡以是非柳耶？歐陽脩以不畏天變爲欺君，至讀蜀書，以麟鳳龜龍爲常事，盖王建紀載之謬，偶述而誦之耳，可遽以是病歐耶？夫諸儒之論說不一，則人君之脩省靡宗；至其脩省弗應，遂謂天之與人衆不相關，而作善之念微矣。

嘗考論災祥之埋，莫過於商書；辯脩省之道，莫過于王嘉。書曰：「天道福善禍淫。」持此以論，而后春秋、洪範之理明矣。嘉以應天以實不以文，執此以往，而后董仲舒、劉向之說破矣。我皇上即位以來，水旱疊奏於郡國，火災再見於宮闈，盖天心仁愛，俾聖德之成同符五帝，蘇功三王而益之。雖然，太
translation_en:
…had already followed this course and broadcast their theories; men such as Gu Yong and Li Xun then borrowed these ideas to further their wicked designs. This, too, was something the two masters would have rejected. As for Liu Zongyuan [?], he said that receiving the mandate did not depend upon Heaven; yet in his Memorial Presenting an Honorific Title, he again enumerated auspicious responses. Presumably he placed human affairs before the Way of Heaven without entirely dismissing auspicious responses. Can one condemn Liu outright on these grounds? Ouyang Xiu regarded failure to fear Heaven’s portents as deceiving the ruler; yet in Reading the History of Shu, he treated qilin, phoenixes, tortoises, and dragons as ordinary occurrences. Presumably he merely happened to recount and repeat the erroneous records concerning Wang Jian. Can one hastily fault Ouyang on this account? When the Confucian scholars’ explanations disagree, the ruler has no guiding standard for self-cultivation and self-examination. When these efforts elicit no response, he consequently concludes that Heaven and humankind have no connection, and his resolve to do good grows weak.

I have examined discussions of the principles [?] underlying calamities and auspicious signs: none surpasses the Documents of Shang. For explaining the way of self-cultivation and self-examination, none surpasses Wang Jia. The Book of Documents says, “The Way of Heaven brings blessings upon the good and calamities upon the wicked.” Only by reasoning from this can the principles of the Spring and Autumn Annals and the Great Plan become clear. Wang Jia held that one should respond to Heaven through substance, not outward forms. Only by proceeding on this basis can the theories of Dong Zhongshu and Liu Xiang be refuted. Since Our Sovereign ascended the throne, floods and droughts have repeatedly been reported from the prefectures and territories, and fire has twice appeared within the palace. Presumably Heaven’s benevolent concern intends that his sagely virtue, brought to perfection, should accord with that of the Five Emperors, and that he should revive [?] the achievements of the Three Kings and add to them. Even so, great…

title: 嘉靖四年江西鄉試錄
text:
和之世也恭聞
皇上克謹天戒以享天心納群工之言防未萌
之慾
御經筵以求其故
各便殿以思其失省躬之道不可盡述而上
帝昭臨之矣罷無益之工禁無功之賞廣
儲蓄以固其本去無藝以紓其歛立政之
美不可枚舉而下民永賴之矣憂勤之意
豈特遣賑貸之臣下罪己之
===
詔而已哉考之於古商周之時高宗宣王嘗遇
災異矣一則克正厥事一則側身脩行而
雊雉旱魃之變終不足以爲國之妖雖其
中興之美不待警戒而後諭然勵其志而
成其功者謂非災異可乎西漢之時文景
嘗多災異矣一則恭儉自持一則遵業不
改而水旱雨雪之變終不足以爲民之患
雖其安養之久不待于樽節之崇然禁其
慾而防其侈謂非災異可乎即是以觀則
punctuated: 和之世也。恭聞皇上克謹天戒，以享天心，納群工之言，防未萌之慾，御經筵以求其故，各便殿以思其失。省躬之道，不可盡述，而上帝昭臨之矣。罷無益之工，禁無功之賞，廣儲蓄以固其本，去無藝以紓其歛。立政之美，不可枚舉，而下民永賴之矣。憂勤之意，豈特遣賑貸之臣、下罪己之詔而已哉？考之於古，商周之時，高宗、宣王嘗遇災異矣。一則克正厥事，一則側身脩行，而雊雉旱魃之變，終不足以爲國之妖。雖其中興之美，不待警戒而後諭，然勵其志而成其功者，謂非災異可乎？西漢之時，文、景嘗多災異矣。一則恭儉自持，一則遵業不改，而水旱雨雪之變，終不足以爲民之患。雖其安養之久，不待于樽節之崇，然禁其慾而防其侈，謂非災異可乎？即是以觀，則
translation_en:
…an age of great harmony. We have reverently heard that Your Majesty conscientiously heeds Heaven’s warnings so as to accord with Heaven’s heart, accepts the words of your officials, and guards against desires before they arise. You attend the Classics Colloquium to seek the causes, and in the private audience hall [?] reflect upon your failings. Your methods of examining yourself cannot be fully recounted, and the Lord on High watches over them clearly. You halt unprofitable works, prohibit rewards unsupported by merit, enlarge reserves to secure the foundations, and eliminate unrestrained exactions to ease the burden of taxation. The virtues of your governance are too numerous to enumerate, and the common people will benefit from them enduringly. Could your concern and diligence consist merely in dispatching officials to distribute relief and loans, and issuing an edict taking blame upon yourself?

Looking back to antiquity, in the Shang and Zhou periods, Gaozong and King Xuan encountered calamities and anomalies. The one corrected his affairs; the other humbled himself and cultivated his conduct. Thus the portents of the crowing pheasant and the drought demon ultimately proved insufficient to bring ruin upon their states. Although the excellence of their dynastic restorations did not require warnings before it became apparent, can we deny that calamities and anomalies spurred their resolve and brought their achievements to fruition?

In the Western Han period, Emperors Wen and Jing encountered many calamities and anomalies. The one maintained a reverent and frugal disposition; the other adhered without alteration to the work of his predecessor. Thus extraordinary floods, droughts, rain, and snow ultimately proved insufficient to afflict the people. Although their long period of peace and sustenance did not depend upon the exaltation of frugality, can we deny that calamities and anomalies restrained their desires and guarded against their extravagance? Viewed in this light, then…

title: 嘉靖四年江西鄉試錄
text:
我
皇上省躬以弭變固將比美於商周之中與
端本以立政陋文宗於不足爲矣豈非
聖學之正有以默契乎春秋災異之紀脗合
洪範事應之陳而諸儒之說又何足以惑
之哉然災異之作固人君之所當省而大
平無事尤君子之所深慮蓋功業之成多
得於屯遭困抑之際而怠荒之起易乘於
豐亨豫大之餘詩稱文王曰不聞亦式不
===
諫亦入夫不聞不諫且然況旣聞旣諫者
乎文王且然而況於法文王者乎古之人
君憂勤惕勵無時可寧豈待災異之著
而躬省之道已衛此天理之所以常存而
治化之所以獨盛也以是存心致萬化之
本出咸和之政積而行之則天地以位萬
物以育薰蒸感格災害不生而享國長久
之道要不可以他求者草野之言未知符
朝堂之論否也惟執事進之
punctuated: 我皇上省躬以弭變，固將比美於商周之中與；端本以立政，陋文宗於不足爲矣。豈非聖學之正，有以默契乎《春秋》災異之紀，脗合《洪範》事應之陳，而諸儒之說又何足以惑之哉？然災異之作，固人君之所當省，而大平無事，尤君子之所深慮。蓋功業之成，多得於屯遭困抑之際；而怠荒之起，易乘於豐亨豫大之餘。《詩》稱文王曰：「不聞亦式，不諫亦入。」夫不聞不諫且然，況旣聞旣諫者乎？文王且然，而況於法文王者乎？古之人君憂勤惕勵，無時可寧，豈待災異之著，而躬省之道已衛此？天理之所以常存，而治化之所以獨盛也。以是存心，致萬化之本，出咸和之政，積而行之，則天地以位，萬物以育，薰蒸感格，災害不生，而享國長久之道，要不可以他求者。草野之言，未知符朝堂之論否也，惟執事進之。
translation_en:
…Our August Sovereign examines himself to avert abnormal phenomena and will surely rival the resurgences of Shang and Zhou [?]. By rectifying the root to establish sound government, he regards the achievements of Wen and Zong [?] as too paltry to emulate. Is this not because the correctness of his sagely learning enables him tacitly to accord with the accounts of calamities and anomalies in the Spring and Autumn Annals and to tally with the exposition of actions and their corresponding responses in the Great Plan? How, then, could the various scholars’ explanations suffice to perplex him?

Yet although the occurrence of calamities and anomalies certainly calls for a ruler’s self-examination, peace free from troubles is especially a matter of profound concern to the gentleman. For accomplishments are often attained amid adversity and constraint, whereas negligence and heedlessness readily arise in the wake of prosperity, ease, and abundance. The Book of Odes says in praise of King Wen: “Even without being told, he followed the proper rule; even without remonstrance, he accepted counsel.” If this was so when he had neither been told nor admonished, how much more so when he had! If even King Wen acted thus, how much more should those who take King Wen as their model!

The rulers of antiquity were anxious and diligent, vigilant and assiduous, allowing themselves no moment of repose. How could they wait for calamities and anomalies to become manifest before practicing self-examination? [The concluding wording of this clause is doubtful.] This is why Heaven’s principle remained constantly present and their transforming governance flourished so exceptionally. By maintaining this disposition, bringing to fulfillment the root of all transformation, issuing policies that bring harmony to all, and putting them steadily into practice, Heaven and Earth will take their proper places and the myriad things will be nourished. This influence will permeate all and elicit a response from the spiritual powers; calamities will not arise. The way to enjoy a long-lasting reign must, in essence, be sought here alone.

These are the words of one among the common people; I do not know whether they accord with the deliberations at court. I ask only that you, the officials in charge, submit them.

title: 嘉靖四年江西鄉試錄
text:
江西鄉試錄後序
嘉靖乙酉江西鄉試事竣錄且
成維時人事整暇天氣清朗諸
執事相視欣然如有得也監臨
御史秦〔鉞〕惕然若有之乃言曰
夫固知若得士是賀也不知吾
之有懼於得也恒言科目非所
===
待士而朱子在南康軍時其書
堂講義未嘗戒人科舉特存乎
人耳夫謂科目不足盡士可謂
科目盡不得士不可亦存乎人
耳方士之未得也惟士之有臧
否焉矣既得也厥得失在予漢
興賢良一詔有閩郡不應一人
punctuated:
江西鄉試錄後序

嘉靖乙酉，江西鄉試事竣，錄且成。維時人事整暇，天氣清朗，諸執事相視欣然，如有得也。監臨御史秦〔鉞〕惕然若有之，乃言曰：「夫固知若得士是賀也，不知吾之有懼於得也。恒言科目非所待士，而朱子在南康軍時，其書堂講義未嘗戒人科舉，特存乎人耳。夫謂科目不足盡士，可；謂科目盡不得士，不可。亦存乎人耳。方士之未得也，惟士之有臧否焉矣；既得也，厥得失在予。漢興賢良，一詔有閩郡不應一人。
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Jiangxi Provincial Examination

In the y酉 year of the Jiajing reign [1525], the Jiangxi Provincial Examination had concluded, and its record was nearly complete. Affairs were then in order and those involved at leisure; the weather was clear and bright. The officials attending to the examination looked at one another delightedly, as though they had achieved something. The Supervising Official, Censor Qin〔Yue〕, appeared apprehensive, as though something weighed upon him [?], and said:

“I certainly know that you rejoice in having obtained worthy scholars, but you do not know the apprehension I feel at having obtained them. It is commonly said that the examination system is no way to treat scholars. Yet when Master Zhu was in Nankang Military Prefecture, his Lectures at the Academy never warned people against taking the examinations. It simply depends on the people involved. To say that examinations cannot encompass all worthy scholars is permissible; to say that examinations obtain no worthy scholars at all is not. This, too, depends on the people involved. Before scholars have been selected, it is only their own merits and shortcomings that are at issue. Once they have been selected, the success or failure rests with me. When the Han called for men of worth and goodness, on one occasion an edict brought not a single person forward from Min Commandery…

title: 嘉靖四年江西鄉試錄
text:
若夫地之不產非有司過也產
矣而不知不明知而不舉不忠
不知而舉誣入且自誣非吾輩
今日責哉大江之西故號多賢
率儒先過化之區士之鍾匡廬
而毓彭蠡者景行親切豈不有
超出倫類而特由此進者乎今
===
所知固諸士之文矣而予未敢
遽謂得也適莽蒼者志乎黼黻
之觀管籥之聽去十旬貿貿然
反固也乃若挾千金資之通都
闤闠奇貨百物唯其所取歸而
發笥則燕石也而可乎故人唯
不得之懼吾斯得之懼也于時
punctuated: 若夫地之不產，非有司過也；產矣而不知，不明；知而不舉，不忠；不知而舉，誣入且自誣。非吾輩今日責哉？大江之西，故號多賢，率儒先過化之區。士之鍾匡廬而毓彭蠡者，景行親切，豈不有超出倫類而特由此進者乎？今所知固諸士之文矣，而予未敢遽謂得也。適莽蒼者，志乎黼黻之觀、管籥之聽，去十旬，貿貿然反，固也。乃若挾千金資之通都闤闠，奇貨百物，唯其所取，歸而發笥，則燕石也，而可乎？故人唯不得之懼，吾斯得之懼也。于時
translation_en:
As for a region that produces no worthy men, this is no fault of the responsible officials. But if it produces them and the officials fail to recognize them, that is a lack of discernment; if they recognize them but fail to recommend them, that is disloyalty; if they recommend men without knowing them, they misrepresent others [?] and also misrepresent themselves. Is this not our responsibility today?

The region west of the great river has long been renowned for its many worthy men. Throughout it are places transformed by the influence of earlier Confucian masters. Among scholars who embody the concentrated spirit of Kuanglu and are nurtured by Pengli, the exemplary conduct of those predecessors is close and immediate. Surely there are some who stand above their fellows and advance precisely through this examination? At present, what we know is indeed these scholars’ writing, yet I dare not hastily claim that we have found the right men.

Someone who goes into the wilds hoping to see embroidered ceremonial robes and hear pipes and flutes may spend a hundred days away and return bewildered: that is only to be expected. But suppose someone takes a thousand gold pieces to the markets of a great metropolis, where rare goods and every kind of merchandise await his choice, and then returns home and opens his chest, only to find ordinary stones from Yan. Could that be acceptable? Thus, while others fear only failing to obtain men, I fear the men I have obtained. At this point…

title: 嘉靖四年江西鄉試錄
text:
益夫與諸同事咸作而曰方益
夫等應聘而來也由金陵逾彭
石以泝鄱陽達于章見水焉排
空觸石騰蛟奔龍或風雨恬霽
則波煙相媚咫尺倏忽千態萬
狀蓋天下至文也見山焉五老
九奇摩穹出雲香爐瀑布嶤然
===
相望皆屹立長江之上根盤不
知其幾許又天下一奇觀也若
襟江帶湖之雄西山南浦之秀
又不暇論矣乃今又見文焉有
道政事者有述禮樂者有及性
與天道者其稱堯舜周孔如取
左右又若親見濂溪晦翁象山
punctuated: 益夫與諸同事咸作而曰：「方益夫等應聘而來也，由金陵逾彭石，以泝鄱陽，達于章。見水焉，排空觸石，騰蛟奔龍；或風雨恬霽，則波煙相媚，咫尺倏忽，千態萬狀，蓋天下至文也。見山焉，五老九奇，摩穹出雲，香爐瀑布，嶤然相望，皆屹立長江之上，根盤不知其幾許，又天下一奇觀也。若襟江帶湖之雄，西山南浦之秀，又不暇論矣。乃今又見文焉，有道政事者，有述禮樂者，有及性與天道者。其稱堯舜周孔，如取左右，又若親見濂溪、晦翁、象山
translation_en: …Yifu and his colleagues all rose and said: “When we, Yifu and the others, came in response to the invitation, we traveled from Jinling past Pengshi [?], upstream through Poyang, and reached Zhang. We saw waters surging into the sky and striking the rocks, like leaping flood dragons and racing dragons. At times, when wind and rain subsided and the skies cleared, waves and mist lent each other charm: within a few feet, in an instant, they assumed a thousand forms and ten thousand shapes. These were surely the finest patterns under Heaven. We saw mountains: Wulao and Jiuqi [?], brushing the vault of heaven and rising above the clouds; Xianglu and the waterfall, towering opposite one another. All stood lofty above the Yangzi River, their roots spreading no one knows how far—another extraordinary spectacle under Heaven. As for the grandeur of the river worn as a lapel and the lake as a girdle, and the beauty of Xishan and Nanpu, we had no leisure even to discuss them. Now we have also seen writings: some discuss affairs of government, some expound rites and music, and some address human nature and the Way of Heaven. Their references to Yao, Shun, the Duke of Zhou, and Confucius are as effortless as reaching for something close at hand; it is as though they had personally seen Lianxi, Huiweng, and Xiangshan…”

title: 嘉靖四年江西鄉試錄
text:
諸君子於白鹿鵝湖之上而揖
之者也是故其辭淵然在矣鏘
然鳴矣幽然光矣沛然流矣其
氣如決九仞之淵注之海如乘
凰駕虬直至乎天斯乃下者夫
辭以昭德氣以徵志是謂稱其
山川豪傑之興無待文王矧茲
===
流波之遠也安知不有清風高
節如紫桑翁文章行業如歐陽
子不屈虜廷如洪忠宣精忠大
節如文山疊山忠義敢言如澹
菴盧溪者出而名世乎苟得一
人焉光茲役矣況若而人邪是
益夫與諸執事皆可無懼也已
punctuated: 諸君子於白鹿鵝湖之上而揖之者也。是故其辭淵然在矣，鏘然鳴矣，幽然光矣，沛然流矣。其氣如決九仞之淵注之海，如乘凰駕虬直至乎天斯乃下者。夫辭以昭德，氣以徵志，是謂稱其山川。豪傑之興，無待文王，矧茲流波之遠也！安知不有清風高節如紫桑翁，文章行業如歐陽子，不屈虜廷如洪忠宣，精忠大節如文山、疊山，忠義敢言如澹菴、盧溪者，出而名世乎？苟得一人焉，光茲役矣，況若而人邪！是益夫與諸執事皆可無懼也已
translation_en:
…those gentlemen at Bailu and Ehu, and bowing to them in greeting. Thus their words possess a profound presence, ring out sonorously, shine with a subtle light, and flow abundantly. Their vital force is like breaching a pool nine ren deep and pouring its waters into the sea, or riding a phoenix and driving a horned dragon straight up to heaven before descending. Words manifest virtue; vital force attests to aspiration. This is what it means to be worthy of their mountains and rivers. Outstanding men arise without waiting for a King Wen; how much more so here, where the stream of inherited influence reaches so far!

How can we know that there will not emerge men renowned in their age for pure integrity and lofty principles like the Old Man of Zisang [?]; for literary achievement and conduct like Master Ouyang; for refusing to submit at a foreign court like Hong Zhongxuan; for unswerving loyalty and great integrity like Wenshan and Dieshan; or for loyalty, righteousness, and courageous speech like Dan’an and Luxi? To obtain even one such man would bring distinction to this undertaking; how much more so with so many men as these! Thus I, Yifu, together with all the officials engaged in this undertaking, may be free of apprehension…

title: 嘉靖四年江西鄉試錄
text:
矣時御史以〔益夫〕言然遂書于
末簡
南京京衛武學教授吴〔益夫〕謹
序
punctuated:
矣。時御史以〔益夫〕言然，遂書于末簡。
南京京衛武學教授吴〔益夫〕謹序。
translation_en:
… At that time, the censor considered Yifu’s words sound, and so this was written on the final leaf.
Preface respectfully composed by Wu Yifu, Instructor in the Military School of the Nanjing Capital Guards.

title: 嘉靖四年江西鄉試錄
text:
江西鄉試錄序
嘉靖乙酉秋八月玆維大比先
是江西廵按監察御史秦〔鉞〕颺
言曰玆役也臣子效忠之道莫
急矣庸敢不預迺以謀于鎮守
太監崔〔和〕廵撫右副都御史陳
〔洪謨〕提督南贛軍務右副都御
===

謀于左右布政使蔣〔瑤〕嚴〔紘〕及

江西鄉試錄序

嘉靖乙酉秋八月，玆維大比。先是，江西廵按監察御史秦〔鉞〕颺言曰：「玆役也，臣子效忠之道莫急矣，庸敢不預？」迺以謀于鎮守太監崔〔和〕、廵撫右副都御史陳〔洪謨〕、提督南贛軍務右副都御史聶〔賢〕、清戎監察御史陶〔儼〕，則謀于左右布政使蔣〔瑤〕、嚴〔紘〕及其左右叅政王〔大用〕、馮〔馴〕、左叅議陳〔塀〕、陸〔溥〕，則謀于按察使丁沂及其副使顧〔應祥〕、周〔廣〕、范〔輅〕、林〔大輅〕、查〔約〕、謝〔廸〕，僉事徐〔乾〕、魯綸、汪〔應軫〕、高〔賁亨〕、張〔儉〕，而後𦘕
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Jiangxi Provincial Examination

In the eighth month of autumn in the yǐyǒu year of Jiajing [1525], the triennial examination was held. Before this, Qin Yue, Regional Inspector of Jiangxi and Investigating Censor, declared: “In this undertaking, nothing is more urgent as a means for subjects to demonstrate their loyalty. How could we dare not prepare beforehand?” He therefore consulted Cui He, the Grand Defender and eunuch Director; Chen Hongmo, the Grand Coordinator and Right Vice Censor-in-Chief; Nie Xian, the Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and Supreme Commander of Military Affairs in Nan–Gan; and Tao Yan, the Investigating Censor charged with inspecting military administration. He then consulted Jiang Yao and Yan Hong, the Left and Right Provincial Administration Commissioners, together with their Left and Right Administration Vice Commissioners, Wang Dayong and Feng Xun, and Left Administration Assistant Commissioners, Chen Ping [?] and Lu Pu. Next he consulted Ding Yi, the Provincial Surveillance Commissioner, together with his Surveillance Vice Commissioners, Gu Yingxiang, Zhou Guang, Fan Lu, Lin Dalu, Zha Yue, and Xie Di, and Surveillance Assistant Commissioners, Xu Qian, Lu Lun, Wang Yingzhen, Gao Benheng, and Zhang Jian. Only then did he draw up …

title: 嘉靖四年江西鄉試錄
text:
事於是禮聘〔度〕及教授吳〔益夫〕
爲考試官教諭朱〔佩龍〕潘〔相〕許
黃〔源〕王〔昺〕陳〔希登〕馬〔驎〕訓導張
〔廉〕吳〔桂〕蔡〔珀〕爲同考試官一時
有事茲土者南京戶部署郎中
蔣〔孔煬〕兵部署郎中彭〔本用〕戶
部主事江〔元輔〕狙〔瑶〕亦罔不與
===
聞之〔度〕等既至則聞都臺藩臬
亦各遷拜不常矣〔賢〕遷而潘〔希〕
〔曾〕代〔瑶〕遷而〔紘〕代〔紘〕轉而袁〔擯〕

兼有勞焉提調則屬布政使〔紘〕
參議溥監試則屬副使〔應祥〕僉
punctuated:
事。於是禮聘〔度〕及教授吳〔益夫〕爲考試官，教諭朱〔佩龍〕、潘〔相〕、許、黃〔源〕、王〔昺〕、陳〔希登〕、馬〔驎〕，訓導張〔廉〕、吳〔桂〕、蔡〔珀〕爲同考試官。一時有事茲土者，南京戶部署郎中蔣〔孔煬〕、兵部署郎中彭〔本用〕、戶部主事江〔元輔〕、狙〔瑶〕，亦罔不與聞之。
〔度〕等既至，則聞都臺、藩臬亦各遷拜不常矣。〔賢〕遷而潘〔希〕〔曾〕代，〔瑶〕遷而〔紘〕代，〔紘〕轉而袁〔擯〕代，〔沂〕遷而張〔羽〕代，〔廣〕遷而徐〔一〕〔鳴〕代，〔乾〕去而鍾〔雲瑞〕代。執事者兼有勞焉。提調則屬布政使〔紘〕、參議溥，監試則屬副使〔應祥〕、僉
translation_en:
…the arrangements. Thereupon, Du 〔度〕 and Wu Yifu, a Prefectural School Instructor, were ceremoniously invited to serve as Examiners. The County School Instructors Zhu Peilong, Pan Xiang, Xu [?], Huang Yuan, Wang Bing, Chen Xideng, and Ma Lin, together with the Assistant Instructors Zhang Lian, Wu Gui, and Cai Po, were appointed Associate Examiners. Those then conducting official business in this region—Jiang Kongyang, Acting Bureau Director in the Nanjing Ministry of Revenue; Peng Benyong, Acting Bureau Director in the Ministry of War; and Jiang Yuanfu and Ju Yao [?], Secretaries in the Ministry of Revenue—were also all consulted about the matter.
After Du and the others arrived, they learned that appointments in the censorial, provincial administration, and surveillance offices had likewise undergone repeated changes. Nie Xian was transferred and replaced by Pan Xizeng; Jiang Yao was transferred and replaced by Yan Hong; Yan Hong was reassigned and replaced by Yuan Bin [?]; Ding Yi was transferred and replaced by Zhang Yu; Zhou Guang was transferred and replaced by Xu Yiming; and Xu Qian departed and was replaced by Zhong Yunrui. The officials handling the examination consequently bore additional labors. The duties of Proctor were entrusted to Provincial Administration Commissioner Yan Hong and Administration Assistant Commissioner Lu Pu; supervision of the examination was entrusted to Surveillance Vice Commissioner Gu Yingxiang and the Assistant…

title: 嘉靖四年江西鄉試錄
text:
事〔僉〕防檢于外則屬署都指揮
僉事劉〔璽〕馮〔勳〕王〔寧〕其掌卷彌
封對讀諸執事自知府而下則
又各以其檄來遂以乙之日入
簾合前董學副使〔廣〕所選十三
郡之士如故事而試之三積二
十餘日凡閱三千卷而拔茲九
===
十五人者蓋
制額也於是鄉試錄成〔度〕以職事當
序諸首惟
今制揭曉有燕歌鹿鳴以賓與之其
來遠矣請以鹿鳴之說為旅酬
告焉鹿鳴之詩曰我有嘉賓鼓
瑟吹笙吹笙鼓簧承筐是將人
punctuated:
事〔僉〕。防檢于外，則屬署都指揮僉事劉〔璽〕、馮〔勳〕、王〔寧〕。其掌卷、彌封、對讀諸執事，自知府而下，則又各以其檄來。遂以乙之日入簾，合前董學副使〔廣〕所選十三郡之士，如故事而試之，三積二十餘日，凡閱三千卷，而拔茲九十五人者，蓋制額也。
於是鄉試錄成，〔度〕以職事當序諸首。惟今制，揭曉有燕，歌《鹿鳴》以賓與之，其來遠矣。請以《鹿鳴》之說為旅酬告焉。《鹿鳴》之詩曰：「我有嘉賓，鼓瑟吹笙。吹笙鼓簧，承筐是將。人
translation_en:
…Assistant Surveillance Commissioner [Qian?]. External security and inspection were entrusted to the acting Assistant Regional Military Commissioners Liu Xi, Feng Xun, and Wang Ning. The other functionaries responsible for handling examination papers, sealing identifying information, and checking copies by reading them against the originals, from prefects downward, each arrived in accordance with his official summons. On the yi day [?], we entered the examiners’ enclosure and assembled the candidates from the thirteen prefectures previously selected by Guang, the Vice Commissioner responsible for supervising education. We examined them according to established practice, over three [sessions?] totaling more than twenty days. In all, we read three thousand papers and selected these ninety-five men, the quota prescribed by imperial regulation.
The Record of the Provincial Examination was then completed. By virtue of my duties, I, Du, was obliged to place a preface at its beginning. Under the present regulations, a banquet follows the announcement of the results, at which “The Deer Call” is sung to honor the successful candidates as guests. This practice has ancient origins. Allow me to offer an interpretation of “The Deer Call” as an address accompanying the successive toasts. The poem “The Deer Call” says: “I have fine guests; we play the zithers and blow the mouth organs. We blow the mouth organs, sounding their reeds; we present baskets of gifts. Those …

title: 嘉靖四年江西鄉試錄
text:
之好我示我周行以乞言也今
之錄其文以
獻加多矣曰我有嘉賓德音孔昭
示民不恌君子是則是傚以名
教也今之錄其名氏傳播無窮
加顯矣古鹿鳴之嘉賓類皆司
徒之養士司馬樂正之所論而
===
官之者也何其盛也後世鄉舉
里選之瀍廢而一切科目之途
闢獨賓興之禮往往有古之意
又何未也我
朝設科取士剗滌漢唐以來詞賦
之習而一於經義論策乎求之
所以採文之弊也比其後也歟
punctuated: 之好我，示我周行」，以乞言也。今之錄其文以獻，加多矣。曰：「我有嘉賓，德音孔昭。示民不恌，君子是則是傚。」以名教也。今之錄其名氏，傳播無窮，加顯矣。古《鹿鳴》之嘉賓，類皆司徒之養士、司馬樂正之所論而官之者也。何其盛也！後世鄉舉里選之瀍廢，而一切科目之途闢，獨賓興之禮，往往有古之意，又何未也！我朝設科取士，剗滌漢唐以來詞賦之習，而一於經義論策乎求之，所以採文之弊也。比其後也，歟
translation_en:
…“Those who cherish me show me the great Way”: this was to solicit counsel. Today, recording their compositions for presentation to the throne provides still more of it. The poem says: “I have fine guests, whose virtuous reputation shines brightly. They show the people how to shun frivolity; gentlemen take them as their rule and example.” This was to teach through recognition of merit. Today, recording their names and disseminating them without end makes that recognition still more conspicuous. The fine guests of the ancient “Deer Call” were generally scholars nurtured by the Minister of Education, assessed by the Minister of War and the Director of Music, and then appointed to office. How flourishing it was! In later ages, local recommendation and selection fell into disuse [?], and the various examination routes opened. Only the ceremony of honoring recommended men as guests often retained the spirit of antiquity. What, then, was still lacking [?]?

Our dynasty established examinations to recruit scholars, sweeping away the habits of verse and rhapsody cultivated since the Han and Tang, and seeking men solely through interpretations of the Classics, discourses, and policy essays. This was intended to remedy the defects of selection by literary accomplishment [?]. By the time of its later development [?] …

title: 嘉靖四年江西鄉試錄
text:
學相禪主司士相遭而亦不免
焉蓋其勢也方今
皇上嗣極惇本復質于茲再舉百執
事祗承
德意視昔彌周江西固多賢之地也
必有所謂道德之士出而名世
凡茲與鹿鳴之席而不以古之
===
嘉賓自待者有其善者也令夫
琴瑟笙簧同管籠幣帛同言論
風旨同而古今人不同則可乎
古之人歌鹿鳴而興也受之而
不慚令之人歌鹿鳴而與也閒
之而足以懼凡茲冒古人之樂
而不以令人自懼者無是心者
punctuated: 學相禪，主司士相遭，而亦不免焉，蓋其勢也。方今皇上嗣極，惇本復質，于茲再舉。百執事祗承德意，視昔彌周。江西固多賢之地也，必有所謂道德之士出而名世。凡茲與鹿鳴之席，而不以古之嘉賓自待者，有其善者也。令夫琴瑟笙簧同，管籠幣帛同，言論風旨同，而古今人不同，則可乎？古之人歌鹿鳴而興也，受之而不慚；令之人歌鹿鳴而與也，閒之而足以懼。凡茲冒古人之樂，而不以令人自懼者，無是心者
translation_en:
…Learning passes from one generation to the next, and examiners and candidates encounter one another [?]; yet they too cannot escape these failings. Such, indeed, is the tendency of circumstances. Now that His Majesty has succeeded to the throne, he strengthens the foundations and restores simplicity; this examination is the second held under his reign. The officials reverently carry out his virtuous intentions, with arrangements still more thorough than before. Jiangxi has always been a land rich in worthy men. Surely men of moral virtue will emerge to win renown in their age. Among all those attending this Deer’s Cry banquet, those who do not hold themselves to the standard of the honored guests of antiquity nevertheless possess goodness [?].

Now [?], if the zithers, mouth organs, and reeds are the same, the pipes, baskets [?], and gifts of silk are the same, and the discourse and guiding spirit are the same, can it be acceptable for the people of antiquity and today to differ? When the people of antiquity sang “Deer’s Cry” and promoted worthy men, those receiving the honor felt no shame. When people today [?] sing “Deer’s Cry” and participate, hearing it [?] should suffice to inspire apprehension. All those who presume to enjoy the music of the ancients, yet do not feel apprehension about themselves as people of today [?], are people without this sense of concern…

title: 嘉靖四年江西鄉試錄
text:
也天之所以與我者古今一而
已周行德音胥此焉出而非學
亦何以反其本也故曰仕而優
則學學而優則仕也善學者合
仕與學而一之者也合道德名
實而一之者也今之學者二矣
或失則固或失則浮是故與其
===
浮也寧固其言也浮于實也其
名也浮于行也而今之所錄者
固言也名也於虖懼哉茲役也
簾以內考試同考試官得行之
也簾以外提調監試官各專之
也而御史鉞寔合內外而臨之
者也作興之者兩都御史及清
punctuated:
也。天之所以與我者，古今一而已。周行、德音，胥此焉出，而非學，亦何以反其本也？故曰：「仕而優則學，學而優則仕。」也善學者，合仕與學而一之者也，合道德、名實而一之者也。今之學者二矣，或失則固，或失則浮。是故與其浮也，寧固。其言也浮于實也，其名也浮于行也，而今之所錄者，固言也、名也。於虖，懼哉！
茲役也，簾以內，考試、同考試官得行之也；簾以外，提調、監試官各專之也。而御史鉞，寔合內外而臨之者也。作興之者，兩都御史及清
translation_en:
…such a disposition. What Heaven has bestowed upon us is the same in ancient and modern times. The exemplary way and virtuous utterances both issue from this; without learning, how could one return to their source? Thus it is said: “When service leaves you capacity to spare, study; when study leaves you capacity to spare, enter service.” Those who learn well unite service and learning as one, and unite the Way and virtue, reputation and substance as one. Today’s learners separate them into two. Some err through rigidity, others through superficiality. Thus rigidity is preferable to superficiality. Their words exceed their substance, and their reputations exceed their conduct; yet what we have assessed in this examination is, after all, words and reputations. Alas, how sobering!
In this examination, within the curtain, the Examiners and Associate Examiners were able to carry out their duties; outside the curtain, the Proctors and Examination Monitors each had their particular responsibilities. Censor Yue brought the inner and outer operations together and supervised them. Those who promoted this undertaking were the two Censors-in-chief and the censor charged with inspecting…

title: 嘉靖四年江西鄉試錄
text:
戎御史之意也相成之者後先
諸藩臬之功也而御史寔集衆
思而用之者也始而選士董學
之明也終而拔尤諸考校之勤
也而度竊自附於公無私者也
直隷松江府儒學教授王度謹
序
===
□
□
□
□
□
□
□
punctuated:
戎御史之意也。相成之者，後先諸藩臬之功也；而御史寔集衆思而用之者也。始而選士，董學之明也；終而拔尤，諸考校之勤也；而度竊自附於公無私者也。
直隷松江府儒學教授王度謹序。
□□□□□□□
translation_en:
…the intent of the censor responsible for military inspection. The complementary efforts that brought this about were the achievement of successive officials of the provincial administration and surveillance commissions; and it was the censor who gathered their collective wisdom and put it to use. The initial selection of candidates reflected the discernment of those supervising education; the final selection of the outstanding reflected the diligence of the examiners. I, Du, venture to count myself among those who acted impartially, without private bias.
Preface respectfully written by Wang Du, Professor of the Confucian School of Songjiang Prefecture in the directly administered territory.
[Seven illegible characters.]

title: 嘉靖四年江西鄉試錄
text:
第壹塲
四書
無欲速無見小利欲速則不達見小利則
大事不成
肫肫其仁淵淵其淵浩浩其天
滄浪之水清兮可以濯我纓滄浪之水濁
兮可以濯我足孔子曰小子聽之清斯
濯纓濁斯濯足矣自取之也
易
===
貞固足以幹事
天地感而萬物化生聖人感人心而天下
和平觀其所感而天地萬物之情可見
矣
是故法象莫大乎天地變通莫大乎四時
縣象著明莫大乎日月崇高莫大乎富
貴備物致用立成器以爲天下利莫大
乎聖人探賾索隱鉤深致遠以定天下
之吉凶成天下之亹亹者莫大乎蓍龜
punctuated:
第壹塲

四書

無欲速，無見小利。欲速則不達，見小利則大事不成。

肫肫其仁，淵淵其淵，浩浩其天。

滄浪之水清兮，可以濯我纓；滄浪之水濁兮，可以濯我足。孔子曰：「小子聽之！清斯濯纓，濁斯濯足矣，自取之也。」

易

貞固足以幹事。

天地感而萬物化生，聖人感人心而天下和平。觀其所感，而天地萬物之情可見矣。

是故法象莫大乎天地，變通莫大乎四時，縣象著明莫大乎日月，崇高莫大乎富貴，備物致用、立成器以爲天下利莫大乎聖人，探賾索隱、鉤深致遠、以定天下之吉凶、成天下之亹亹者莫大乎蓍龜。
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

Do not seek haste, and do not look to small gains. Seeking haste prevents attainment; looking to small gains prevents great undertakings from being accomplished.

How earnest his benevolence, how unfathomable his depth, how vast his heaven-like greatness!

When the waters of the Canglang are clear, I can wash my cap strings in them; when the waters of the Canglang are muddy, I can wash my feet in them. Confucius said: “My young disciples, listen to this! When clear, they are used to wash cap strings; when muddy, they are used to wash feet. They bring this treatment upon themselves.”

Book of Changes (Yijing)

Being correct and firm is sufficient to take charge of affairs.

Heaven and earth act upon one another, and the myriad things are transformed and brought into being. The sage moves people's hearts, and all under heaven is peaceful and harmonious. By observing what they move and respond to, the true nature of heaven, earth, and the myriad things can be discerned.

Thus, among models and images, none are greater than heaven and earth; in change and adaptation, none are greater than the four seasons; among suspended images shining brightly, none are greater than the sun and moon; in eminence, nothing is greater than wealth and high rank. In preparing things for use and creating finished implements to benefit all under heaven, none are greater than the sages. In probing the intricate, seeking the hidden, plumbing the depths, and reaching the distant, thereby determining good and ill fortune for all under heaven and bringing the world's endeavors to completion, none are greater than the milfoil stalks and tortoise shells used in divination.

title: 嘉靖四年江西鄉試錄
text:
有大者不可以盈故受之以謙有大而能
謙必豫故受之以豫
書
帝曰咨汝羲暨和朞三百有六旬有六日
以閏月定四時成歲允釐百工庶績咸
熙
與治同道罔不興
人之有能有為使羞其行而邦其昌凡厥
正人既富方穀
寛而有制從容以和
===
詩
關關雎鳩在河之洲窈窕淑女君子好逑
鴥彼飛隼其飛戾天亦集爰止方叔涖止
其車三千師干之試方叔率止鉦人伐
鼓陳師鞠旅顯允方叔伐鼓淵淵振旅
闐闐
受天之祜四方來賀
穆穆魯侯敬明其德敬慎威儀維民之則
punctuated:
有大者不可以盈，故受之以謙；有大而能謙，必豫，故受之以豫。

書
帝曰：「咨！汝羲暨和，朞三百有六旬有六日，以閏月定四時成歲，允釐百工，庶績咸熙。」
與治同道，罔不興。
人之有能有為，使羞其行，而邦其昌。凡厥正人，既富方穀。
寛而有制，從容以和。

詩
關關雎鳩，在河之洲。窈窕淑女，君子好逑。
鴥彼飛隼，其飛戾天，亦集爰止。方叔涖止，其車三千。師干之試，方叔率止。鉦人伐鼓，陳師鞠旅。顯允方叔，伐鼓淵淵，振旅闐闐。
受天之祜，四方來賀。
穆穆魯侯，敬明其德。敬慎威儀，維民之則。
translation_en:
Those who possess much must not become full of themselves; hence Great Possession is followed by Modesty. Possessing much yet remaining modest necessarily brings joy; hence Modesty is followed by Joy.

Book of Documents
The emperor said: “Ah! You, Xi and He! The full year comprises three hundred and sixty-six days. Use intercalary months to determine the four seasons and complete the year. Truly put the hundred offices in order, and all undertakings will flourish.”
Those who follow the same way as good government invariably prosper.
When people possess ability and capacity for action, let them display their accomplishments, and your state will flourish. As for its upright officers, once provided for abundantly, they will become good.
Be generous yet governed by rules, composed and harmonious.

Book of Odes
“Guan, guan,” call the ospreys on the islet in the river. The modest, graceful, virtuous maiden is a fitting mate for the gentleman.
Swift is that flying falcon; its flight reaches heaven, yet it also alights and rests. Fang Shu has arrived, with three thousand chariots. The host displays its martial strength; Fang Shu leads it. The gong officers beat the drums; they array the army and muster the troops. Illustrious and trustworthy is Fang Shu! The drums sound deep and resonant; the troops are marshalled amid their thunder.
Receiving Heaven’s blessing, he is congratulated by those who come from the four quarters.
Majestic is the Lord of Lu, reverently making his virtue shine. Reverent and careful in his dignified bearing, he is a model for the people.

title: 嘉靖四年江西鄉試錄
text:
春秋
春王正月〔隱公元年〕夏齊侯衛侯胥命于蒲
〔桓公三年〕
楚人伐黄〔僖公十有一年〕楚人滅黄〔僖公十有二年〕
冬十月甲午叔孫得臣敗狄于鹹〔文公十有
一年〕
楚子使椒來聘〔文公九年〕十有一月公如楚
〔襄公二十八年〕夏五月公至自楚〔襄公二十九年〕
禮記
===
夫爲人子者三賜不及車馬
郊特牲而社稷大牢天子適諸侯諸侯膳
用犢諸侯適天子天子賜之禮大牢貴
誠之義也
宮爲君商爲臣角爲民徵爲事羽爲物
事君欲諫不欲陳詩云心乎愛矣瑕不謂
矣中心藏之何日忘之
第貳塲
論
punctuated:
春秋
春，王正月。〔隱公元年〕夏，齊侯、衛侯胥命于蒲。〔桓公三年〕
楚人伐黄。〔僖公十有一年〕楚人滅黄。〔僖公十有二年〕
冬，十月甲午，叔孫得臣敗狄于鹹。〔文公十有一年〕
楚子使椒來聘。〔文公九年〕十有一月，公如楚。〔襄公二十八年〕夏，五月，公至自楚。〔襄公二十九年〕
禮記
夫爲人子者，三賜不及車馬。
郊特牲，而社稷大牢。天子適諸侯，諸侯膳用犢；諸侯適天子，天子賜之禮大牢，貴誠之義也。
宮爲君，商爲臣，角爲民，徵爲事，羽爲物。
事君欲諫，不欲陳。《詩》云：「心乎愛矣，瑕不謂矣？中心藏之，何日忘之？」
第貳塲
論
translation_en:
Spring and Autumn Annals

In spring, the first month of the royal calendar. 〔First year of Duke Yin〕 In summer, the Marquis of Qi and the Marquis of Wei exchanged pledges at Pu. 〔Third year of Duke Huan〕
The men of Chu attacked Huang. 〔Eleventh year of Duke Xi〕 The men of Chu extinguished the state of Huang. 〔Twelfth year of Duke Xi〕
In winter, on the jiawu day of the tenth month, Shusun Dechen defeated the Di at Xian. 〔Eleventh year of Duke Wen〕
The Viscount of Chu sent Jiao on a diplomatic visit to our court. 〔Ninth year of Duke Wen〕 In the eleventh month, the duke went to Chu. 〔Twenty-eighth year of Duke Xiang〕 In summer, in the fifth month, the duke returned from Chu. 〔Twenty-ninth year of Duke Xiang〕
Book of Rites

For one who occupies the position of a son, even three grants of gifts do not extend to carriages and horses.

At the suburban sacrifice, a single sacrificial animal is offered; at the altars of Soil and Grain, a full set of sacrificial animals—an ox, a sheep, and a pig—is offered. When the Son of Heaven visits a feudal lord, the lord uses a calf for his meal; when a feudal lord visits the Son of Heaven, the Son of Heaven presents him with a full set of sacrificial animals as a ceremonial gift. This expresses the principle of valuing sincerity.

The gong note represents the ruler; shang, the ministers; jue, the people; zhi, affairs; and yu, material things.

In serving a ruler, one should seek to remonstrate with him, not to display his faults. The Book of Odes says: “In my heart I love him; why should I not tell him? I hold him within my heart; on what day could I forget him?”

Second Session

Discourse

title: 嘉靖四年江西鄉試錄
text:
聖學無所為而然
詔誥表〔內科一道〕
擬漢文帝弛利省費以振民詔〔後六年〕
擬唐以韓愈為吏部侍郎誥〔長慶三年〕
擬宋以九經須賜州縣學校及聚徒講誦
之所謝表〔咸平四年〕
判語〔五條〕
選用軍職
守掌在官財物
===
收藏禁書及私習天文
窩弓殺傷人
家人求索
第叁場
策五道
問粤漢以來代凡幾君靡有不尊孔氏矣
若遍魯之祀先聖之褒親自為贊特其
尤隆者耳然皆隨其一時秉彝之好而
非終身致治之實皆未有若我
punctuated:
聖學無所為而然。

詔誥表〔內科一道〕
擬漢文帝弛利省費以振民詔〔後六年〕。
擬唐以韓愈為吏部侍郎誥〔長慶三年〕。
擬宋以九經須賜州縣學校及聚徒講誦之所謝表〔咸平四年〕。

判語〔五條〕
選用軍職。
守掌在官財物。
收藏禁書及私習天文。
窩弓殺傷人。
家人求索。

第叁場
策五道
問：粤漢以來，代凡幾君，靡有不尊孔氏矣。若遍魯之祀、先聖之褒、親自為贊，特其尤隆者耳。然皆隨其一時秉彝之好，而非終身致治之實，皆未有若我
translation_en:
The learning of the sages is so of itself, without any ulterior purpose.

Edicts, proclamations of appointment, and memorials 〔One topic from this section [?]〕
Compose an edict in the voice of Emperor Wen of Han relaxing revenue exactions and reducing expenditure to relieve the people. 〔Sixth year of the Later Era〕
Compose a Tang proclamation appointing Han Yu Vice Minister of Personnel. 〔Third year of Changqing〕
Compose a memorial of thanks for the Song court’s bestowal of the Nine Classics upon prefectural and county schools and places where students assemble for lectures and recitation [?]. 〔Fourth year of Xianping〕

Legal judgments 〔Five topics〕
Selection and appointment of military officers.
Custody and management of government property.
Keeping prohibited books and privately studying astronomy.
Killing or injuring people with concealed crossbow traps.
Demands and solicitations by household members.

Third Session
Five Policy Questions
Question: Since the Han, however many rulers there have been through successive dynasties, none has failed to honor Confucius. Such acts as sacrifices throughout Lu [?], commendations of the Former Sage, and personally composing encomiums are merely the most conspicuous instances of this reverence. Yet all these followed a momentary fondness arising from their innate moral dispositions, rather than constituting the substance of a lifelong pursuit of good government. None has equaled our …

title: 嘉靖四年江西鄉試錄
text:
朝之極其崇重而形行之者也蓋嘗伏讀我
太宗文皇帝御製孔廟之碑而仰窺
祖宗右文之治矣
聖德之厚及其子孫
宸翰之光被諸林闕自肇祀以來所未覯也
文皇之言曰尚推孔子之道一
皇考之所以表章者於乎盛矣然則
文皇之所學者固
聖祖之所謂學乎
===
聖祖之所學者又吾孔子之所謂學乎得其學
則所表章者非虛文得其表章則其致
治者不徒矣或謂南都之未主其華之
而未盡乎京師之塑像其因之而未革
乎此則
聖人之用意有非恒情之所易窺否則漢唐宋
諸君亦嘗修其祀矣即儀文之詳畧不
同而治化必不如是之相懸也其亦有
可得而論乎諸生述
punctuated:
朝之極其崇重而形行之者也。蓋嘗伏讀我太宗文皇帝御製孔廟之碑，而仰窺祖宗右文之治矣。聖德之厚及其子孫，宸翰之光被諸林闕，自肇祀以來所未覯也。文皇之言曰：「尚推孔子之道，一皇考之所以表章者。」於乎盛矣！然則文皇之所學者，固聖祖之所謂學乎？

聖祖之所學者，又吾孔子之所謂學乎？得其學，則所表章者非虛文；得其表章，則其致治者不徒矣。或謂南都之未主，其華之而未盡乎？京師之塑像，其因之而未革乎？此則聖人之用意，有非恒情之所易窺。否則漢唐宋諸君亦嘗修其祀矣，即儀文之詳畧不同，而治化必不如是之相懸也。其亦有可得而論乎？諸生述。
translation_en:
…our dynasty, which has carried its reverence to the utmost and put it into practice. I have reverently read the stele inscription for the Temple of Confucius composed by our Emperor Taizong Wen, and thereby glimpsed the culture-honoring governance of our imperial ancestors. The generosity of imperial virtue extends to Confucius’s descendants, and the radiance of the imperial brush shines upon his grove and temple precincts—something never witnessed since sacrifices to him began. Emperor Wen said: “May we promote the Way of Confucius, in full accord with what Our deceased imperial father honored and made manifest.” How magnificent! Was what Emperor Wen studied, then, indeed what the Sagely Progenitor called learning?

And was what the Sagely Progenitor studied what our Confucius called learning? If that learning is grasped, what is honored and made manifest is no empty ceremony; if the meaning of that honoring is grasped, its contribution to good government is not fruitless. Some might ask: “As for the absence of a spirit tablet in the Southern Capital, was this an embellishment not fully carried through [?]? As for the sculpted image in the capital, was this a continuation of earlier practice that had not been reformed?” Here the sage’s intentions may not be readily fathomed by ordinary understanding. Otherwise, the rulers of the Han, Tang, and Song also maintained sacrifices to Confucius; even allowing for differences in the elaborateness of their ceremonial forms, their achievements in government and moral transformation surely could not have differed so greatly. Is there something here that can be discussed? You candidates are to set it forth.

title: 嘉靖四年江西鄉試錄
text:
食或在晦何歟近年以來步交食者率
多先後不同而不能一一密合或謂授
時曆法久而不能無差建議欲增損之
者不知果真有所見歟古今論曆者或
曰有一定之法或曰無一定之法不過
隨時考驗以合於天而已若果有一定
之法則皆可以常數求而脩德格天之
說爲不足信若果無一定之法則不可
以常數求而考測推步之術爲不足憑
===
矣是皆載諸史冊班班可攷諸士子寧
無究心於此者乎願著于篇毋隱
問周禮聖人經世之書周公所以致太平
之跡上而天地日月下而封域山川著
而禮樂刑政微而禽獸草木纖悉具備
其精神心術盡於此矣孔子曰周監于
二代郁郁乎文哉其以是歟後世雖未
能悉遵古制要之官聯服御車旗禮儀
之節率有取焉秦人滅學斯禮厄矣漢
punctuated:
食或在晦，何歟？近年以來，步交食者率多先後不同，而不能一一密合。或謂授時曆法久而不能無差，建議欲增損之者，不知果真有所見歟？古今論曆者，或曰有一定之法，或曰無一定之法，不過隨時考驗以合於天而已。若果有一定之法，則皆可以常數求，而脩德格天之說爲不足信；若果無一定之法，則不可以常數求，而考測推步之術爲不足憑矣。是皆載諸史冊，班班可攷。諸士子寧無究心於此者乎？願著于篇，毋隱。
問：周禮，聖人經世之書，周公所以致太平之跡。上而天地日月，下而封域山川，著而禮樂刑政，微而禽獸草木，纖悉具備，其精神心術盡於此矣。孔子曰：「周監于二代，郁郁乎文哉！」其以是歟？後世雖未能悉遵古制，要之官聯、服御、車旗、禮儀之節，率有取焉。秦人滅學，斯禮厄矣。漢
translation_en:
…eclipses sometimes occur on the last day of the lunar month: why is this? In recent years, those calculating eclipses have generally differed in placing them earlier or later, and have been unable to achieve exact agreement in every instance. Some say that the methods of the Season-Granting Calendar (Shoushi li), having been in use so long, cannot be free of discrepancies. Do those proposing adjustments to them truly have sound insights? Among those who have discussed calendrical calculation, past and present, some say that it has fixed methods; others say that it has no fixed methods, and that one merely tests and verifies it as circumstances change, so that it accords with Heaven. If there truly are fixed methods, everything can be determined through constant numerical values, and the claim that cultivating virtue can move Heaven becomes unworthy of belief. If there truly are no fixed methods, constant numerical values cannot determine these things, and the techniques of observation, measurement, and astronomical calculation become unreliable. These matters are all recorded in the histories and can be clearly examined. Can it be that none of you candidates has devoted serious thought to them? Please set out your views in writing, withholding nothing.
Question: The Rites of Zhou (Zhou li) is a sage’s book on governing the world, a record of the means by which the Duke of Zhou brought about Great Peace. Above, it encompasses Heaven and Earth, the sun and moon; below, territorial boundaries, mountains, and rivers. In manifest matters, it encompasses rites, music, punishments, and government; in minute matters, birds, beasts, grasses, and trees. Every detail is fully provided for: his spirit and the workings of his mind are entirely embodied here. Confucius said: “Zhou looked to the two preceding dynasties as its models. How rich was its culture!” Was this what he meant? Although later ages could not follow the ancient institutions in every respect, their arrangements for coordination among offices, clothing and articles of use, carriages and banners, and ritual observances generally drew upon this book. When the men of Qin destroyed learning, these rites suffered calamity. The Han…

title: 嘉靖四年江西鄉試錄
text:
詔何以有是哉即其憂勤惕勵不違寧處其視
古人之弭變也何如變異疊興民不爲
患其視古人之立政也何如世儒論災
異者紛然不一以致人君之脩省漫無
所從有行公羊之派以著陰陽論者或
有譏其傅會然則春秋紀山川之變異
以爲人爲之感召非歟有廣穀梁之說
以著五行傳者或有譏其牽强然則洪
範以五行之災祥爲五事之休咎非歟
===
文章名世後學所宗一則以受命不于
其天至於請復尊號表則條陳其瑞應
之美何自背其說歟一則以不畏天變
爲非至讀蜀書則以麟鳳龜龍爲常事
何自蹈其轍歟要之災異之作非無由
而至天心仁愛必有道可回然而五經
所載有一定之理諸儒所論有一定之
見可得指而言歟諸士子積學待用將
以堯舜其君其於災異之說辯之明矣
punctuated:
詔，何以有是哉？即其憂勤惕勵，不違寧處，其視古人之弭變也何如？變異疊興，民不爲患，其視古人之立政也何如？世儒論災異者紛然不一，以致人君之脩省漫無所從。有行公羊之派以著陰陽論者，或有譏其傅會，然則春秋紀山川之變異，以爲人爲之感召，非歟？有廣穀梁之說以著五行傳者，或有譏其牽强，然則洪範以五行之災祥爲五事之休咎，非歟？

文章名世，後學所宗，一則以受命不于其天，至於請復尊號表，則條陳其瑞應之美，何自背其說歟？一則以不畏天變爲非，至讀蜀書，則以麟鳳龜龍爲常事，何自蹈其轍歟？要之，災異之作，非無由而至；天心仁愛，必有道可回。然而五經所載，有一定之理；諸儒所論，有一定之見，可得指而言歟？諸士子積學待用，將以堯舜其君，其於災異之說辯之明矣。
translation_en:
…an imperial edict. Why was this so? As for his anxious diligence, vigilance, and self-exhortation, and his not departing from repose [?], how did these compare with the ancients’ efforts to avert abnormal phenomena? When anomalies arose repeatedly yet the people suffered no harm, how did this compare with the ancients’ establishment of good government? Scholars through the ages have offered numerous conflicting accounts of calamities and anomalies, leaving rulers with no clear guidance for self-cultivation and self-examination. Some followed the Gongyang school and composed a Discourse on Yin and Yang, which others criticized as contrived. Yet does not the Spring and Autumn Annals record anomalies affecting mountains and rivers as having been elicited by human actions? Some expanded upon the teachings of Guliang and composed a Commentary on the Five Phases, which others criticized as strained. Yet does not the Great Plan treat the calamitous and auspicious manifestations of the Five Phases as corresponding to favorable and unfavorable outcomes of the Five Activities?

There were writers renowned in their own times whom later scholars took as models. One held that receiving the mandate did not derive from Heaven [?], yet in his Memorial Requesting the Restoration of the Honorific Title he enumerated the beauties of auspicious responses. Why did he contradict his own argument? Another condemned the failure to fear heavenly anomalies, yet in Reading the Book of Shu he treated qilin, phoenixes, tortoises, and dragons as commonplace. Why did he himself fall into the same error? In essence, calamities and anomalies do not arise without cause; Heaven’s disposition is benevolent and loving, and there must be a way to turn it back. Yet are there settled principles in what the Five Classics record, and settled judgments in what the various scholars argue, that can be identified and explained? You examination candidates have accumulated learning while awaiting employment and intend to make your ruler the equal of Yao and Shun. Surely you have clearly distinguished among the explanations of calamities and anomalies.
