translation_en:
Associate Examiner Cai, Assistant Instructor, comments: “Correcting the seasons and emphasizing trustworthiness both involve changing Zhou institutions. Writers often force connections in discussing these matters. This essay is precise, incisive, clear, and fluent; it has therefore been selected for inclusion.”
Associate Examiner Wang, Instructor, comments: “The reasoning in the discussion of taking Heaven’s Way as a model and rectifying people’s hearts is very profound.”
Examiner Wu, Professor, comments: “It elucidates clearly and fully the meaning of the Spring and Autumn Annals ‘exhausting the Changes’ [?].”
Examiner Wang, Professor, comments: “It grasps the sage’s intention in changing Zhou institutions.”
The Spring and Autumn Annals changes Zhou institutions to accord with the Book of Changes: it provides means to correct the seasons and to emphasize trustworthiness. Here we see approval of following the Xia calendar; the passage concerning commanding the sage [?] likewise concerns exercising discretionary judgment to change Zhou institutions. How profound is its purpose in transmitting instruction! Chou, midwinter, was the beginning of the Zhou year [?]. The Classic writes ‘spring’ with the first month. Does this mean that beginning the year in midwinter—in winter—was wrong? The seasons guide the undertaking of activities; neither Yin’s beginning the year in the month of chou nor Zhou’s beginning it in the month of zi properly served to impart the seasons to the people. What could equal Xia’s beginning the year in the month of yin in the correctness of its seasonal reckoning and the excellence of its ordinances? Established before Heaven and Earth and tested before ghosts and spirits, it could indeed endure through a hundred kings without defect.
The Spring and Autumn Annals weighs the rites of the former kings and establishes standards for ten thousand generations. Taking the regulation of the calendar and clarification of the seasons as its task, it achieves something significant here. It is as though it says: ‘The numbering of months may follow Zhou, and the events recorded may be those of Lu, but the seasons must follow Xia.’ Even if this changes Zhou institutions, what grounds are there for doubt? Thus, before the first month of Duke Yin’s reign, it expressly places the words ‘spring, the king’s.’ Its intention is surely the same as that behind riding in the Yin carriage and employing the Shao dance: to transmit models to later generations. If this principle is put into practice, the four seasons will be fixed, and [?] the year …

title: 嘉靖四年江西鄉試錄
text:
以齊欽若之治可繼無復事不師古而建亥者
矣若司盟周之秋官也經善胥命之不盟然則
官有司盟者非耶蓋信以發志而殺之作誓周
之作會皆非所以示民信也孰有言相結信相
諭如齊衛之胥命者乎意氣有乎盤珽無設誠
牘百年而一見也夫子嘅末世之僞志大道之
行以講信修睦爲事於此有取焉若曰食可去
也生可無也信不可以不同乎古也雖變周之
制無異焉故於齊衛之不盟特書胥命以善之
===
殆與茆屋之謹蕭魚之美同一見諸行事之驗
也此義行則不動而敬不言而信淳古之風可
回無復人愛其情而質乎者矣吁時方建子變
之以建寅時方相盟變之以相命信非知權而
盡易者莫能與也然則春秋其空言哉大抵法
天者莫大乎時教民者莫先於信天道無形所
可見者時而已人心不同所可仗者信而已法
天以時則天德備乾之義也教民以信則人心
從中孚之義也然則夫子春與胥命之文豈直
punctuated: 以齊，欽若之治可繼，無復事不師古而建亥者矣。若司盟，周之秋官也，經善胥命之不盟，然則官有司盟者非耶？蓋信以發志，而殺之作誓、周之作會，皆非所以示民信也。孰有言相結、信相諭，如齊衛之胥命者乎？意氣有乎，盤珽無設，誠牘百年而一見也。夫子嘅末世之僞，志大道之行，以講信修睦爲事，於此有取焉。若曰：「食可去也，生可無也，信不可以不同乎古也。」雖變周之制，無異焉。故於齊衛之不盟，特書胥命以善之，殆與茆屋之謹、蕭魚之美，同一見諸行事之驗也。此義行，則不動而敬，不言而信，淳古之風可回，無復人愛其情而質乎者矣。吁！時方建子，變之以建寅；時方相盟，變之以相命。信非知權而盡易者，莫能與也。然則《春秋》其空言哉？大抵法天者莫大乎時，教民者莫先於信。天道無形，所可見者時而已；人心不同，所可仗者信而已。法天以時，則天德備，《乾》之義也；教民以信，則人心從，《中孚》之義也。然則夫子春與胥命之文，豈直
translation_en:
…thereby bringing them into order. Government that reverently accords with Heaven could be continued, and there would no longer be those who, failing to model their actions on antiquity, began the year with the month designated hai.

As for the Director of Covenants, this was an office under Zhou’s Ministry of Justice. The classic praises the exchange of pledges without a sworn covenant. Does this mean that establishing an office of Director of Covenants was wrong? Trust serves to express intentions; yet the making of oaths through killing [?] and Zhou’s holding of assemblies were neither means of showing the people trustworthiness. What could compare with Qi and Wei’s exchange of pledges, in which words bound them together and trust conveyed their intentions to one another? Their goodwill was present, without setting out basins and jade tablets [?]: truly something seen only once in a hundred years [?]. The Master lamented the falsity of a declining age and aspired to the practice of the Great Way. Making the cultivation of trust and harmony his concern, he found something here worthy of approval. It was as though he said: “Food may be dispensed with, and life may be relinquished, but trust must accord with antiquity.” Though this altered Zhou’s institutions, there was nothing amiss in it. Thus, where Qi and Wei did not swear a covenant, he specifically wrote “exchanged pledges” to commend them. This presumably offers the same evidence through actual events as the circumspection at Maowu [?] and the excellence of Xiaoyu. If this principle were practiced, people would command respect without acting and inspire trust without speaking. The simple ways of antiquity could return, and people would no longer conceal their true feelings and resort to guarantees [?].

Ah! When the year began with the month designated zi, he changed it to begin with yin; when people made sworn covenants with one another, he changed this to an exchange of pledges. Truly, only someone who understood discretionary judgment and fully comprehended the Changes could accomplish this. Can the Spring and Autumn Annals, then, be mere empty words? In general, nothing is more important in modeling oneself on Heaven than the seasons, and nothing takes precedence over trust in teaching the people. Heaven’s Way has no visible form; what can be seen of it is simply the seasons. Human hearts differ; what can be relied upon is simply trust. Modeling oneself on Heaven through the seasons brings Heaven’s virtue to completion: this is the meaning of the hexagram Qian, “The Creative.” Teaching the people through trust wins their allegiance: this is the meaning of the hexagram Zhongfu, “Inner Sincerity.” Thus, could the Master’s wording, “spring” and “exchanged pledges,” be merely …

title: 嘉靖四年江西鄉試錄
text:
魯史而已哉故曰聖人隨時變易以從道
冬十月甲午叔孫得臣敗狄于鹹〔文公十一年〕
阮范
同考試官訓導蔡　批〔題本平易作者不害則泛是〕〔篇寫出聖人正名之意筆力峻健可以式矣〕
同考試官教諭王　批〔分别族類有制禦夷狄之意〕〔子能發之盖深於經者〕
考試官教授吳　批〔發得正名意明淨〕
考試官教授王　批〔正名處須如此說方盡〕
===
即春秋紀狄之文見聖人正名之法夫春秋正
名之書也觀得臣敗狄之文槩可見矣恩昔太
王有獯鬻之侵魯頌有膺懲之訓狄之爲中國
患久矣春秋中葉暴横益張既潛師以侵齊遂
長驅而伐魯於是我公命將出師以禦門庭之
寇得臣分閫仗鉞以紓攘郤之謀一鼓而踣其
徒再鼓而奪其帥狄於是乎有鹹之敗焉春秋
直書其事何以見正名之法耶誠以統天下而
觀之一夷一夏不無内外美惡之分就夷狄而
punctuated:
魯史而已哉？故曰：「聖人隨時變易以從道。」

冬十月甲午，叔孫得臣敗狄于鹹。〔文公十一年〕
阮范

同考試官訓導蔡　批〔題本平易，作者不害則泛，是〕〔篇寫出聖人正名之意，筆力峻健，可以式矣。〕
同考試官教諭王　批〔分别族類，有制禦夷狄之意。〕〔子能發之，盖深於經者。〕
考試官教授吳　批〔發得正名意，明淨。〕
考試官教授王　批〔正名處須如此說方盡。〕

即春秋紀狄之文，見聖人正名之法。夫春秋，正名之書也。觀得臣敗狄之文，槩可見矣。恩昔太王有獯鬻之侵，魯頌有膺懲之訓，狄之爲中國患久矣。春秋中葉，暴横益張，既潛師以侵齊，遂長驅而伐魯。於是我公命將出師，以禦門庭之寇。得臣分閫仗鉞，以紓攘郤之謀，一鼓而踣其徒，再鼓而奪其帥。狄於是乎有鹹之敗焉。春秋直書其事，何以見正名之法耶？誠以統天下而觀之，一夷一夏，不無内外美惡之分；就夷狄而
translation_en:
…merely the annals of Lu? Thus it is said: “The sage changes with the times in order to follow the Way.”

“In winter, in the tenth month, on the jiawu day, Shusun Dechen defeated the Di at Xian.” 〔Eleventh year of Duke Wen.〕
By Ruan Fan.

Associate Examiner Cai, Assistant Instructor, comments: 〔The topic itself is straightforward; writers tend toward either distortion or vagueness [?]. This〕〔essay brings out the sage’s intention to rectify names. Its writing is forceful and vigorous, and may serve as a model.〕
Associate Examiner Wang, Instructor, comments: 〔Distinguishing peoples and their kinds conveys the intention to control and resist the Yi and Di.〕〔You have been able to bring this out: surely you are deeply versed in the Classic.〕
Examiner Wu, Professor, comments: 〔It brings out the meaning of rectifying names clearly and cleanly.〕
Examiner Wang, Professor, comments: 〔The rectification of names must be explained in this way for its meaning to be fully expressed.〕

In the Spring and Autumn Annals’ account of the Di, we see the sage’s method of rectifying names. The Spring and Autumn Annals is a book that rectifies names. By examining its account of Dechen’s defeat of the Di, we can see the general principle. In ancient times [?], King Tai suffered an invasion by the Xunyu, and the Hymns of Lu contained an injunction to strike and punish them. The Di had long been a source of trouble for the central states. By the middle of the Spring and Autumn period, their violence and insolence had grown still greater. Having secretly sent troops to invade Qi, they then drove deep into Lu to attack it. Our duke thereupon ordered a general to lead out the army and resist the invaders at our very gates. Dechen, entrusted with independent military command and wielding the battle-axe of authority, carried out his plans to repel them. At the first beating of the drums he laid low their followers; at the second, he captured their commander. Thus the Di suffered their defeat at Xian.

The Spring and Autumn Annals records the event directly. How does this reveal the method of rectifying names? It is because, viewing all under Heaven as a whole, the Yi and the Xia are distinguished as outer and inner, good and bad; considering the Yi and Di themselves…

title: 嘉靖四年江西鄉試錄
text:
論之其地其人不無大小强弱之異故在我之
界限既不可以不嚴而在彼之種類亦不容以
不别今狄也不守北方之巢穴敢與大國以抗
衡其狼貪虎噬之心非若獫狁之效順猶有所
慕而朝也其跋扈跳梁之勢非若赤狄之寡弱
猶可得撲而滅也雖見挫於今不容無防於其
後雖幸勝於魯不能恒保於其他聖人於此本
其實正其名直以狄書而别於白狄赤狄云者
蓋以無心之文寓有心之法使後之人知此狄
蓋嘗侵齊者也蓋嘗伐魯者也蓋屢爲中國患
===
者也因名以考其地因地以察其人隨其大小
强弱之勢以立吾禦之之法則聖人之意得矣
雖然狄固不足責也使文公能倚於法家拂士
以德脩國政得臣能急於責難陳善以禮格君
心則國勢乂安外憂不作何狄人之敢伐哉君
以苟安爲志臣以幸勝爲功上下嬉嬉而魯日
不競矣聖人本其詐戰而以敗書意者深著魯
國君臣之罪以爲好武功而不脩文德者戒歟
punctuated:
論之，其地其人不無大小强弱之異。故在我之界限，既不可以不嚴，而在彼之種類，亦不容以不别。今狄也，不守北方之巢穴，敢與大國以抗衡。其狼貪虎噬之心，非若獫狁之效順，猶有所慕而朝也；其跋扈跳梁之勢，非若赤狄之寡弱，猶可得撲而滅也。雖見挫於今，不容無防於其後；雖幸勝於魯，不能恒保於其他。聖人於此，本其實，正其名，直以狄書，而别於白狄、赤狄云者，蓋以無心之文寓有心之法，使後之人知此狄蓋嘗侵齊者也，蓋嘗伐魯者也，蓋屢爲中國患者也。因名以考其地，因地以察其人，隨其大小强弱之勢，以立吾禦之之法，則聖人之意得矣。
雖然，狄固不足責也。使文公能倚於法家拂士，以德脩國政，得臣能急於責難陳善，以禮格君心，則國勢乂安，外憂不作，何狄人之敢伐哉？君以苟安爲志，臣以幸勝爲功，上下嬉嬉，而魯日不競矣。聖人本其詐戰而以敗書，意者深著魯國君臣之罪，以爲好武功而不脩文德者戒歟？
translation_en:
…considered in their own terms, their territories and peoples differ in size and strength. Thus, while the boundary separating us from them must be strictly maintained, distinctions among their groups must also be observed. These Di, instead of remaining in their northern lairs, dared to contend with a great state. Their wolfish greed and tigerlike appetite were unlike the submission of the Xianyun, who still had something they admired and therefore came to court. Their overbearing and unruly power was unlike the numerical weakness of the Red Di, who could still be struck down and destroyed. Though checked now, they must still be guarded against in the future; though Lu was fortunate enough to defeat them, victory could not always be assured elsewhere. Here the Sage grounded his account in the facts and rectified the names, writing simply “Di” to distinguish them from those called White Di and Red Di. In seemingly disinterested wording he thus embedded a deliberate rule, enabling later generations to recognize that these were the Di who had invaded Qi, attacked Lu, and repeatedly afflicted the Central States. By examining their territory through their name, and investigating their people through their territory, we can establish methods of resisting them suited to their size and strength. In this way, the Sage’s intent is grasped.
Even so, the Di hardly merit reproach. Had Duke Wen relied on hereditary ministers who upheld the laws and on counselors who would correct him, cultivating the government of his state through virtue, and had Dechen made it his urgent concern to demand difficult achievements of his ruler and set goodness before him, rectifying his ruler’s heart through ritual propriety, then the state would have been orderly and secure, and external troubles would not have arisen. How would the Di have dared to attack? Yet the ruler sought only ease for the moment, and his minister counted a fortunate victory as an accomplishment. High and low alike were heedlessly at ease, while Lu grew weaker by the day. The Sage, taking account of their deceitful warfare, recorded the event with the word “defeated.” Might his intention have been to expose fully the guilt of Lu’s ruler and minister, as a warning to those who prize martial achievements but fail to cultivate civil virtue?

title: 嘉靖四年江西鄉試錄
text:
禮記
郊特牲而社稷大牢天子適諸侯諸侯膳
用犢諸侯適天子天子賜之禮大牢貴
誠之義也
黄濬
同考試官教諭陳　批〔善發揮以少爲貴之意〕
考試官教授吳　批〔辭理明整〕
考試官教授王　批〔有文藻〕
記者詳禮之以少爲貴者而必有其義也甚矣
===
禮之所貴者誠也則夫郊祀之所用與天子之
所膳者得非以此義歟想其意謂夫禮必有義
而其大者唯誠已矣是故饗帝曰郊郊禮之重
者也禮重則心肅故天子之郊也大報天之事
而就陽位以求其格者薦惟一牛而已至若社
稷三獻之祀輕則祭以大牢而駿奔于祼亦彰
功德之報矣奉君曰膳膳禮之至者也禮至則
敬深故天子之出也入諸侯之境而列盆盎以
致其養者牲亦用犢而已若夫人臣來朝之禮
punctuated:
禮記

郊特牲，而社稷大牢。天子適諸侯，諸侯膳用犢；諸侯適天子，天子賜之禮大牢。貴誠之義也。

黄濬

同考試官教諭陳　批〔善發揮以少爲貴之意〕
考試官教授吳　批〔辭理明整〕
考試官教授王　批〔有文藻〕

記者詳禮之以少爲貴者，而必有其義也。甚矣，禮之所貴者誠也！則夫郊祀之所用與天子之所膳者，得非以此義歟？想其意謂夫禮必有義，而其大者唯誠已矣。是故饗帝曰郊，郊，禮之重者也。禮重則心肅，故天子之郊也，大報天之事，而就陽位以求其格者，薦惟一牛而已。至若社稷三獻之祀，輕則祭以大牢，而駿奔于祼，亦彰功德之報矣。奉君曰膳，膳，禮之至者也。禮至則敬深，故天子之出也，入諸侯之境，而列盆盎以致其養者，牲亦用犢而已。若夫人臣來朝之禮
translation_en:
Record of Rites (Liji)

“At the suburban sacrifice, a single animal is offered, whereas at sacrifices to the altars of Soil and Grain, a full complement of animals is offered. When the Son of Heaven visits a feudal lord, the lord provides a calf for his meal; when a feudal lord visits the Son of Heaven, the Son of Heaven bestows on him the ceremonial gift of a full complement of animals. This expresses the principle of valuing sincerity.”

Huang Jun 黄濬

Associate Examiner Chen, a School Instructor, comments: “Skillfully develops the meaning of valuing spareness.”
Examiner Wu, a Confucian School Instructor, comments: “Expression and reasoning are clear and orderly.”
Examiner Wang, a Confucian School Instructor, comments: “Possesses literary elegance.”

The compiler of the Record explains in detail those instances in ritual where spareness is valued; these necessarily have an underlying meaning. How profoundly ritual values sincerity! Could this principle not explain both what is used in the suburban sacrifice and what is served to the Son of Heaven? I take the passage to mean that ritual necessarily embodies principles, and that the greatest of these is simply sincerity.

Thus, the offering to the Supreme Lord is called the suburban sacrifice, which is a rite of the greatest weight. The weightiness of the rite makes the heart solemn. Accordingly, when the Son of Heaven performs the suburban sacrifice, this is the great act of requiting Heaven. Taking his place in the yang quarter to seek Heaven’s arrival, he offers only a single ox. As for the sacrifices to Soil and Grain, with their three presentations of offerings, these are of lesser weight, and so a full complement of animals—an ox, a sheep, and a pig—is sacrificed. Those who hasten to perform the libation [?] likewise manifest the requital of merit and beneficence.

Providing food for the ruler is called presenting a meal, and this is a rite of the utmost degree. The fullness of the rite makes reverence profound. Accordingly, when the Son of Heaven travels and enters a feudal lord’s territory, the lord sets out bowls and jars to provide for his nourishment, yet the sacrificial animal used is likewise only a calf. As for the rite by which a subject comes to court …

title: 嘉靖四年江西鄉試錄
text:
之外者君子其知之乎
宮爲君商爲臣角爲民徵爲事羽爲物
畢竟晐
同考試官教諭陳　批〔五聲於君臣民事物非指爲象而寔有通貫之妙此作獨精到明暢是宜錄出〕
考試官教授吳　批〔說出道即器器即道意義〕
得者
考試官教授王　批〔文思精緻〕
論樂聲之妙而寓人道之大焉夫樂也者象倫
===
者也惟聲音之見於樂者有寓於人之道則可
以知政矣樂記君子謂夫樂以妙天道於無形
聲以闡人道於有象蓋五聲之始有所謂宮者
厥音屬土而統乎律呂之元其聲至濁而起於
黃鍾之度是則五聲之獨尊者也其有君道乎
蓋君也者刑于百辟而建有極之中憲于萬邦
而端作孚之體然則宮之主於衆音也其猶君
之宰於萬化者耶商之爲聲也生於徵之三分
而益一得數七十而有二屬乎金而聲之次濁
punctuated:
之外者，君子其知之乎？

宮爲君，商爲臣，角爲民，徵爲事，羽爲物。

畢竟晐

同考試官教諭陳，批〔五聲於君臣民事物，非指爲象，而寔有通貫之妙。此作獨精到明暢，是宜錄出。〕

考試官教授吳，批〔說出道即器、器即道意義。〕

得者

考試官教授王，批〔文思精緻。〕

論樂聲之妙，而寓人道之大焉。夫樂也者，象倫者也。惟聲音之見於樂者，有寓於人之道，則可以知政矣。樂記君子謂夫樂以妙天道於無形，聲以闡人道於有象。蓋五聲之始，有所謂宮者，厥音屬土，而統乎律呂之元；其聲至濁，而起於黃鍾之度。是則五聲之獨尊者也，其有君道乎？蓋君也者，刑于百辟，而建有極之中；憲于萬邦，而端作孚之體。然則宮之主於衆音也，其猶君之宰於萬化者耶？商之爲聲也，生於徵之三分而益一，得數七十而有二，屬乎金，而聲之次濁
translation_en:
…those beyond it—would the gentleman know them?

Gong represents the ruler; shang, the minister; jue, the people; zhi, affairs; and yu, things.

Bi Jinggai 畢竟晐 [?]

Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor, comments: 〔The relation of the five tones to ruler, minister, people, affairs, and things is not merely an assignment of symbols: there truly is a subtle interconnectedness running through them. This composition is exceptionally penetrating, lucid, and fluent; it deserves to be included in the record.〕

Examiner Wu, Professor, comments: 〔It brings out the meaning of “the Way is concrete things, and concrete things are the Way.”〕

“Those who attain it” [?]

Examiner Wang, Professor, comments: 〔The composition’s thought is refined and meticulous.〕

In discussing the subtleties of musical sounds, it embodies the grandeur of the human Way. Music is that which represents ordered relationships. Precisely because the sounds manifested in music embody the Way of human relations, one can discern government through them. The gentleman of the Record of Music holds that music gives subtle expression to the Way of Heaven in what has no form, while sound elucidates the human Way through perceptible representations.

At the beginning of the five tones is what is called gong. Its tone belongs to Earth and presides over the source of the pitch standards. Its sound is the lowest, and it originates in the measure of the Huangzhong pitch. Thus it alone occupies the position of highest honor among the five tones. Does it not possess the Way of the ruler? The ruler serves as a model for the many lords and establishes the central standard; he serves as an exemplar for the myriad states and rectifies his own person as the embodiment of trustworthiness. Is gong’s presiding over the other tones, then, not like the ruler’s governing the myriad transformations?

As a tone, shang is generated by dividing zhi into three parts and adding one part, yielding the number seventy-two. It belongs to Metal, and its sound is the next lowest…

title: 嘉靖四年江西鄉試錄
text:
者也臣曷爲其象之夫臣之義所以祗承厥辟
而宣力于四方則商之次宮無邇臣之棐翊於
君者耳角之爲聲也生於羽之三分而益一得
數六十而有四屬乎木而聲則清濁半之者也
民曷爲其象之夫民之道所以夙夜勞止而服
役於一人則角之次商無邇民之用命於上者
耳有民而後有事也其徵音屬火而聲之清者
象之則數之五十有四蓋得於下生之宮者然
也故事之有深茂連動之宜其所以妙變化於
===
萬端者殆與徵聲之主於動盪者而一機乎有
事而後有物也其羽音屬水而聲之至清者象
之則數之四十有八蓋得於下生之商者然也
故物之有形榦材質之體其所以致利用於天
下者殆與羽聲之主於凝寂者而一揆乎夫聲
有五所以極音樂之全象有五所以貫人道之
大使樂之倫定而不可易則治道備於是矣豈
直爲導和之具哉抑考周官大師之職掌六律
六同以合陰陽之聲皆文之以五聲播之以八
punctuated: 者也。臣曷爲其象之？夫臣之義，所以祗承厥辟而宣力于四方，則商之次宮，無邇臣之棐翊於君者耳。角之爲聲也，生於羽之三分而益一，得數六十而有四，屬乎木，而聲則清濁半之者也。民曷爲其象之？夫民之道，所以夙夜勞止而服役於一人，則角之次商，無邇民之用命於上者耳。有民而後有事也，其徵音屬火而聲之清者象之，則數之五十有四，蓋得於下生之宮者然也。故事之有深茂連動之宜，其所以妙變化於萬端者，殆與徵聲之主於動盪者而一機乎？有事而後有物也，其羽音屬水而聲之至清者象之，則數之四十有八，蓋得於下生之商者然也。故物之有形榦材質之體，其所以致利用於天下者，殆與羽聲之主於凝寂者而一揆乎？夫聲有五，所以極音樂之全；象有五，所以貫人道之大。使樂之倫定而不可易，則治道備於是矣，豈直爲導和之具哉？抑考《周官》大師之職，掌六律六同，以合陰陽之聲，皆文之以五聲，播之以八
translation_en:
…such is its character. Why does the minister serve as its counterpart? The duty of a minister is reverently to serve his sovereign and exert himself throughout the four quarters. Thus, shang’s position next after gong is like [?] the minister’s assistance to his ruler. The tone jue is generated by dividing yu into three parts and adding one part, yielding the number sixty-four. It corresponds to Wood, and its sound lies halfway between clear and turbid. Why do the people serve as its counterpart? The way of the people is to labor morning and night and render service to the One Man, the ruler. Thus, jue’s position next after shang is like [?] the people’s obedience to those above them.

Only once there are people are there affairs. These are represented by the tone zhi, which corresponds to Fire and has a clear sound. Its number is fifty-four, obtained by downward generation from gong. Thus, affairs require depth, flourishing development, and interconnected movement [?]; the principle by which they achieve wondrous transformations in myriad circumstances is perhaps the same as that underlying the stirring movement characteristic of zhi. Only once there are affairs are there things. These are represented by the tone yu, which corresponds to Water and has the clearest sound. Its number is forty-eight, obtained by downward generation from shang. Thus, things possess embodied form, structure, material, and substance; the principle by which they provide practical benefit throughout the world is perhaps the same as that underlying the concentrated stillness characteristic of yu.

The five tones encompass the fullness of music; their five counterparts embrace the vast scope of the human way. When the ordered relationships of music are fixed and unalterable, the way of governance is fully present therein. Could music be merely an instrument for fostering harmony? Furthermore, examining the duties of the Music Master in the Offices of Zhou, we find that he administers the six pitch standards and the six corresponding pitches to harmonize the sounds of yin and yang, patterns them all with the five tones, and gives them expression through the eight…

title: 嘉靖四年江西鄉試錄
text:
音其典同之爲樂器以十有二律爲之度數以
十有二聲爲之齊量是知樂也者天地之命中
和之紀者也聲音以文之倫理以象之律呂以
宣之夫然後樂道形焉人道立焉治道洽焉然
則先王之作樂於天下其感通化導之本誠有
在於上者故曰六律五聲八音在治忽有國者
圖之
第貳塲
論
===
聖學無所爲而然　　魏良政
同考試官教諭許　批〔作聖之功自義利之辨始此作辨析幾微可以占所養矣〕
同考試官教諭宋　批〔說義之爲利處精切蓋績於義者〕
考試官教授吳　批〔性理之學以浮古之文發之可取〕
考試官教授王　批〔得張子未言之旨〕
punctuated:
音。其典同之爲樂器，以十有二律爲之度數，以十有二聲爲之齊量。是知樂也者，天地之命，中和之紀者也。聲音以文之，倫理以象之，律呂以宣之。夫然後樂道形焉，人道立焉，治道洽焉。然則先王之作樂於天下，其感通化導之本，誠有在於上者。故曰：「六律五聲八音，在治忽。」有國者圖之！
第貳塲
論
聖學無所爲而然。魏良政。
同考試官教諭許，批〔作聖之功自義利之辨始，此作辨析幾微，可以占所養矣。〕
同考試官教諭宋，批〔說義之爲利處精切，蓋績於義者。〕
考試官教授吳，批〔性理之學，以浮古之文發之，可取。〕
考試官教授王，批〔得張子未言之旨。〕
translation_en:
…tones. When the Director of Music makes musical instruments, he uses the twelve pitch standards to determine their dimensions and the twelve sounds to regulate their measures. Thus we know that music is the ordinance of Heaven and Earth and the guiding principle of equilibrium and harmony. Sounds embellish it; ordered relationships give it symbolic expression; the yin and yang pitch standards give it voice. Only then does the Way of music take form, the human Way become established, and the Way of government prevail everywhere. Thus, when the former kings instituted music throughout the realm, the foundation of its power to evoke responses and to transform and guide people truly lay with those above. Hence the saying: “The six pitch standards, five notes, and eight timbres depend upon whether government is orderly or negligent.” Let those who rule a state consider this!
Second Session
Discourse
“Sagely Learning Is So of Itself, without an Ulterior Purpose” — Wei Liangzheng.
Associate Examiner Xu, Instructor, comments: “The work of becoming a sage begins with distinguishing righteousness from profit. This composition discriminates between the subtlest impulses, allowing us to judge the author's moral cultivation.”
Associate Examiner Song, Instructor, comments: “The discussion of how righteousness becomes profit is precise and incisive. The author has evidently accumulated achievement in righteousness [?].”
Examiner Wu, Professor, comments: “The learning of human nature and principle is expounded through prose of ‘floating antiquity’ [?]; this merits approval.”
Examiner Wang, Professor, comments: “It grasps what Master Zhang intended but left unstated.”

title: 嘉靖四年江西鄉試錄
text:
君子求至於聖人之道亦唯謹其微而已夫聖
人非有異於人也唯於幾微之間不辨則義利
之分不明斯學非聖人之道矣聖人之道非自
外至也天地生人之初與其形而併賦之無所
謂聖愚之別者矣其誠而無爲者聖之所以同
天世學以復其初者君子之所以求至於聖也
是豈可以有爲而爲之哉有爲則人欲之私非
天之所以與我之本心矣以是而學聖人之道
亦利而已矣請申張子之說夫學亦不同也其
===
幾甚微其別甚大世之人有同學而其行不同
者矣有同行而其心不同者矣又有其心雖同
而一念之公私不同者矣堯舜之所以異於途
人者豈必於其行與事求之哉亦在於公私之
間耳於乎天無爲而爲命聖人無爲而爲道君
子無爲而爲學學也者所以求至於聖人也聖
人也者其道誠而無僞純而不雜天下之理皆
其心之所具其視天下之事皆其分所當爲固
無所事於學也而亦何所爲而學也未至於聖
punctuated:
君子求至於聖人之道，亦唯謹其微而已。夫聖人非有異於人也，唯於幾微之間不辨，則義利之分不明，斯學非聖人之道矣。聖人之道非自外至也，天地生人之初，與其形而併賦之，無所謂聖愚之別者矣。其誠而無爲者，聖之所以同天；世學以復其初者，君子之所以求至於聖也。是豈可以有爲而爲之哉？有爲則人欲之私，非天之所以與我之本心矣。以是而學聖人之道，亦利而已矣。請申張子之說。

夫學亦不同也，其幾甚微，其別甚大。世之人有同學而其行不同者矣，有同行而其心不同者矣，又有其心雖同而一念之公私不同者矣。堯舜之所以異於途人者，豈必於其行與事求之哉？亦在於公私之間耳。於乎！天無爲而爲命，聖人無爲而爲道，君子無爲而爲學。學也者，所以求至於聖人也。聖人也者，其道誠而無僞，純而不雜，天下之理皆其心之所具，其視天下之事，皆其分所當爲，固無所事於學也，而亦何所爲而學也？未至於聖
translation_en:
The gentleman who seeks to attain the Way of the sage need only exercise care over the subtlest stirrings of his mind. The sage is not inherently different from other people. Yet if one fails to discriminate among these subtle stirrings, the distinction between righteousness and profit remains unclear, and such learning is not the Way of the sage. The Way of the sage does not come from outside. When Heaven and Earth first bring human beings into existence, they bestow it together with bodily form, making no distinction between sage and fool. Being sincere and acting without an ulterior purpose is how the sage accords with Heaven; learning in the world [?] to recover one's original condition is how the gentleman seeks to attain sagehood. How could this be pursued with an ulterior purpose? Such a purpose belongs to the selfishness of human desires, not to the original mind that Heaven bestowed upon me. To study the Way of the sage on this basis is merely to seek profit. Allow me to elaborate on Master Zhang's explanation.

Learning, too, takes different forms: its incipient stirrings are exceedingly subtle, but the resulting differences are exceedingly great. Some people in the world pursue the same learning yet differ in their conduct. Others share the same conduct yet differ in their minds. Still others, though their minds are alike, differ in whether a single thought is impartial or selfish. Must we necessarily seek what distinguishes Yao and Shun from an ordinary passerby in their conduct and deeds? It lies simply in the distinction between impartiality and selfishness. Ah! Heaven establishes its mandate without ulterior purpose; the sage practices the Way without ulterior purpose; the gentleman pursues learning without ulterior purpose. Learning is the means by which one seeks to attain sagehood. As for the sage, his Way is sincere and without falsity, pure and without admixture. All the principles under Heaven are present within his mind. He regards all the affairs of the world as things he ought to undertake as his proper duty. He therefore has no need to apply himself to learning; and for what ulterior purpose would he learn? Those who have not yet attained sagehood…

title: 嘉靖四年江西鄉試錄
text:
者以其所得於天之初心而反觀之則作聖之
功思過半矣不然雖聖人日與之俱面命耳提
以求其肖終亦有爲而爲利矣吾未見其能聖
人也聖學之所以無爲者何如哉蓋必省察於
隱微之間而存養於不覩不聞之地晝審之應
酧夜驗之夢寐視聽言動而有非禮之干事物
人倫而有虛妄之雜近而男女飲食之微遠而
經綸輔相之業其念慮之發蓋有鬼神之所未
窺而義利之辨巳著此豈待見之於行事而師
===
友亦何所見而箴規之耶亦唯其心之自知焉
耳有是心則去之無是心則𢙣之聖賢所以遏
人欲存天理而别義利者莫先於此奈何今之
學者知利之爲利者多矣而義之爲利蓋未之
知也利之爲利固有爲也義之爲利亦有爲也
一念幾微之間而善惡係焉君子小人判焉盍
以其本然之初心而驗之是故見孺子入井而
有惻隱之心焉見嘑蹴之食而有羞惡之心焉
臨取予而有辭讓之心焉處善惡而有是非之
punctuated: 者，以其所得於天之初心而反觀之，則作聖之功，思過半矣。不然，雖聖人日與之俱，面命耳提，以求其肖，終亦有爲而爲利矣，吾未見其能聖人也。聖學之所以無爲者何如哉？蓋必省察於隱微之間，而存養於不覩不聞之地，晝審之應酧，夜驗之夢寐。視聽言動而有非禮之干，事物人倫而有虛妄之雜，近而男女飲食之微，遠而經綸輔相之業，其念慮之發，蓋有鬼神之所未窺，而義利之辨巳著。此豈待見之於行事，而師友亦何所見而箴規之耶？亦唯其心之自知焉耳。有是心則去之，無是心則𢙣之。聖賢所以遏人欲、存天理而别義利者，莫先於此。奈何今之學者，知利之爲利者多矣，而義之爲利，蓋未之知也。利之爲利，固有爲也；義之爲利，亦有爲也。一念幾微之間，而善惡係焉，君子小人判焉，盍以其本然之初心而驗之？是故見孺子入井而有惻隱之心焉，見嘑蹴之食而有羞惡之心焉，臨取予而有辭讓之心焉，處善惡而有是非之
translation_en: …those who have not yet attained sagehood, if they reflect upon themselves through the original mind they received from Heaven, will have accomplished more than half the work of becoming sages. Otherwise, even if a sage were with them daily, instructing them face to face and taking them by the ear to make them resemble him, they would ultimately still act with an ulterior purpose, seeking profit. I have never seen such people become sages. What, then, does it mean that the learning of sages is free of ulterior purpose? One must examine oneself in what is hidden and subtle, and preserve and nurture the mind where nothing is seen or heard, scrutinizing it by day in dealings with others and testing it by night in dreams. In seeing, hearing, speaking, and acting, there may be intrusions of what violates ritual propriety; in affairs and human relationships, there may be admixtures of falsity. From the intimate details of relations between men and women and of eating and drinking, to the far-reaching work of ordering affairs and assisting in government, thoughts may arise that even ghosts and spirits have not yet glimpsed, while the distinction between righteousness and profit is already manifest. How could this await expression in conduct? And what could teachers and friends see that would enable them to admonish and correct it? Only one's own mind knows it. If such a thought is present, remove it; if absent, abhor it. Nothing takes precedence over this in the sages’ and worthies’ efforts to restrain human desires, preserve Heaven’s principle, and distinguish righteousness from profit. How is it that so many scholars today recognize the pursuit of profit as profit-seeking, yet apparently do not recognize that righteousness can also be used to seek profit? Seeking profit through profit is certainly acting with an ulterior purpose; seeking profit through righteousness is also acting with an ulterior purpose. Good and evil hinge upon the subtlest stirrings of a single thought; there the gentleman and the petty man are distinguished. Why not test these stirrings against the original mind in its inherent condition? Thus, on seeing a young child fall into a well, one has a heart of compassion; on seeing food offered with a contemptuous shout or a kick, one has a heart of shame and aversion; when faced with taking or giving, one has a heart of deference; when confronting good and evil, one has a sense of right and wrong…

title: 嘉靖四年江西鄉試錄
text:
心焉卒然遇之於計較未及之際而此心即應
之者是義也無爲而然者也自夫人欲間之而
失其初則有内交要譽惡其聲而然者矣有白
日驕人而昏夜乞哀者矣有矯情以賈廉爲利
祿而爲善者矣是皆人欲之私非天之所以與
我者矣義利之辨其微矣哉甞因是而歷觀古
今之變矣古之人聞求利於市矣及其後則求
利於朝也又其後則求利於儒也求利於義也
人而求利於義則禮樂衣冠道德性命之地而
===
穿窬小人有厠跡於其間者矣世變至此良可
惜也是故術數權謀奔命世味投富貴之機赴
功名之會者人知其爲利矣至於習堯舜之讀
誦孔孟之言聚首接膝終日以談詩書者人不
知其爲利也躄躠以爲仁踶跂以爲義遵先王
之道而稱儒行于天下者人亦不知其爲利也
能知僞言僞行之爲利則知無爲而爲聖學矣
由是而推之則尊主庇民救亡興滅固義也以
桓文之心行之爲利矣又安知不有爲利而羞
punctuated:
心焉。卒然遇之於計較未及之際，而此心即應之者，是義也，無爲而然者也。自夫人欲間之而失其初，則有内交、要譽、惡其聲而然者矣，有白日驕人而昏夜乞哀者矣，有矯情以賈廉、爲利祿而爲善者矣。是皆人欲之私，非天之所以與我者矣。義利之辨，其微矣哉！
甞因是而歷觀古今之變矣。古之人，聞求利於市矣；及其後，則求利於朝也；又其後，則求利於儒也，求利於義也。人而求利於義，則禮樂衣冠、道德性命之地，而穿窬小人有厠跡於其間者矣。世變至此，良可惜也！是故術數權謀、奔命世味、投富貴之機、赴功名之會者，人知其爲利矣。至於習堯舜之讀、誦孔孟之言、聚首接膝、終日以談詩書者，人不知其爲利也。躄躠以爲仁，踶跂以爲義，遵先王之道而稱儒行于天下者，人亦不知其爲利也。能知僞言僞行之爲利，則知無爲而爲聖學矣。由是而推之，則尊主庇民、救亡興滅，固義也；以桓文之心行之，爲利矣。又安知不有爲利而羞
translation_en:
…such a heart. When one suddenly encounters something before there is time to calculate, and this heart responds immediately, that is righteousness: it arises without an ulterior purpose. Once human desires intrude and the heart loses its original condition, however, people act to cultivate connections, seek praise, or avoid a bad reputation. Some treat others arrogantly in broad daylight but beg for pity after dark. Some disguise their true feelings to purchase a reputation for integrity, or do good for profit and official emoluments. These are all the selfish workings of human desire, not what Heaven has bestowed upon us. How subtle is the distinction between righteousness and profit!
Reflecting on this, I have surveyed the changes from antiquity to the present. Among the ancients, one heard of seeking profit in the marketplace. Later, people sought profit at court; still later, they sought profit in Confucian learning and in righteousness itself. When people seek profit in righteousness, petty men who bore through walls and climb over them to steal come to mingle within the very realm of ritual, music, proper dress, the Way and virtue, human nature and Heaven’s mandate. That the world should have changed to this extent is truly lamentable! Thus, when people employ stratagems and manipulation, exhaust themselves pursuing worldly pleasures, seize opportunities for wealth and rank, and rush toward occasions for achievement and fame, others recognize that they are pursuing profit. But when people study the readings of Yao and Shun [?], recite the words of Kongzi and Mengzi, and sit close together discussing the Classic of Poetry and the Book of Documents all day, others do not recognize that they are pursuing profit. When people strain awkwardly to enact benevolence and stretch on tiptoe to enact righteousness, follow the way of the former kings, and profess Confucian conduct throughout the world, others likewise fail to recognize that they are pursuing profit. If one can recognize that false words and false conduct serve profit, one will understand the learning of the sages: acting without an ulterior purpose. Extending this reasoning, honoring one’s ruler, protecting the people, rescuing states from ruin, and restoring extinguished states are certainly righteous acts. Yet to perform them with the intentions of Duke Huan of Qi and Duke Wen of Jin is to pursue profit. And how do we know that there are not people who pursue profit yet are ashamed …

title: 嘉靖四年江西鄉試錄
text:
稱桓文者乎稱義熙寧崇正棄詭固義也以宋
襄之心行之爲利矣又安知不有爲利而薄宋
襄者乎又由是而推之則攘善者利也讓勞者
亦利也偷生者利也爭死者亦利也夫勞而不
施死而不惜雖孔門之學亦不過是而今謂之
利者豈非以其有爲而爲之邪毫釐之差千里
之謬隱微不察則固有君子之行而不免於小
人之心者矣聖人之學則不然以命者天之所
以命我也我自立之何所爲而立也性者吾之
===
所得於天也吾自盡之何所爲而盡也教者所
以輔相造化之偏因其所固有而去其所本無
又何所爲而爲教也不然不唯不可以爲學且
不可以爲人矣何暇有所規取於利而爲之哉
以其最切於人身者言之則如饑之於食渴之
於飲寒之於衣也如盲者之不忘視痿者之不
忘起疾痛疴癢者之不忘于撫摩也發於中心
之誠而求必得之不唯不可有所爲而亦不暇
有所爲矣聖賢愼獨之學誠不可以不講也不
punctuated:
稱桓文者乎？稱義熙寧，崇正棄詭，固義也；以宋襄之心行之，爲利矣，又安知不有爲利而薄宋襄者乎？又由是而推之，則攘善者利也，讓勞者亦利也；偷生者利也，爭死者亦利也。夫勞而不施，死而不惜，雖孔門之學亦不過是，而今謂之利者，豈非以其有爲而爲之邪？毫釐之差，千里之謬。隱微不察，則固有君子之行而不免於小人之心者矣。
聖人之學則不然。以命者，天之所以命我也，我自立之，何所爲而立也？性者，吾之所得於天也，吾自盡之，何所爲而盡也？教者，所以輔相造化之偏，因其所固有而去其所本無，又何所爲而爲教也？不然，不唯不可以爲學，且不可以爲人矣，何暇有所規取於利而爲之哉？以其最切於人身者言之，則如饑之於食，渴之於飲，寒之於衣也；如盲者之不忘視，痿者之不忘起，疾痛疴癢者之不忘于撫摩也。發於中心之誠而求必得之，不唯不可有所爲，而亦不暇有所爲矣。聖賢愼獨之學，誠不可以不講也。不
translation_en:
…to invoke Dukes Huan and Wen? To profess righteousness and bring peace [?], to honor uprightness and reject deceit, are certainly righteous acts. Yet to perform them with the heart of Duke Xiang of Song is to pursue advantage. And how can we know that there are not those who pursue advantage while disdaining Duke Xiang of Song? Extending this reasoning further, appropriating credit for good deeds is a pursuit of advantage, but so too is declining credit for one's labors; clinging ignobly to life is a pursuit of advantage, but so too is vying to die. To labor without boasting of it and to die without begrudging one's life—even the learning of Confucius's school goes no further than this. If we now call these pursuits of advantage, is it not because they are done with an ulterior aim? A discrepancy of a hair's breadth becomes an error of a thousand li. If one fails to scrutinize what is hidden and subtle, one may indeed display the conduct of a gentleman yet remain unable to escape the heart of a petty man.
The learning of the sages is otherwise. As for the mandate [?], it is what Heaven has decreed for me. I establish it myself: for what ulterior purpose would I establish it? My nature is what I have received from Heaven. I fully realize it myself: for what ulterior purpose would I fully realize it? Teaching serves to assist and redress the unevenness of creation, drawing upon what is inherently present and removing what was originally absent. Again, for what ulterior purpose would one undertake teaching? Otherwise, one could neither pursue learning nor even be a proper human being. What room, then, is there to act with some calculated advantage in view? To speak of what bears most immediately upon the person, it is like hunger seeking food, thirst seeking drink, or cold seeking clothing. It is like the blind person's unceasing desire to see, the paralyzed person's unceasing desire to rise, or the sick, aching, and itching person's unceasing desire to rub and soothe the afflicted part. It issues from sincerity within the heart and seeks fulfillment without fail. Not only must there be no ulterior aim; there is no room for one. The sages' and worthies' learning of vigilance when alone must indeed be studied. If not …

title: 嘉靖四年江西鄉試錄
text:
然王伯之辨君子小人之分彰彰在人耳目矣
待張子擴其所未發哉約而精之則知天下之
所謂學者自聖人以往未嘗無所爲也故遊方
之外無干於時甚至離形去智剗其心而弗之
有佛老之學人皆知其無所爲而不爲利也而
不知其近名近刑之戒與夫出入死生之說則
固深乎利者矣噫利之爲利夫人能言之義之
爲利非喻於義者不能辨也學者求至於聖人
之道當立志以爲先持敬以爲本反身而誠以
===
至於天下之事皆吾分內而一毫不係乎人則
事皆無所爲而爲天之所以與我者盡矣故夫
子有爲已爲人之說孟子以舜跖之分在於利
善之間數百年來未有盡發其旨者張子以有
爲無爲言之深有以中俗學之病𢃄其所以有
功於聖門也善乎象山陸子有言曰古之君子
喻人於義小人喻於利今之君子其喻於義者皆
爲利而喻也爲利而喻非義矣聖賢之言其互
相發明者以此
punctuated: 然，王伯之辨、君子小人之分，彰彰在人耳目矣，待張子擴其所未發哉？約而精之，則知天下之所謂學者，自聖人以往，未嘗無所爲也。故遊方之外，無干於時，甚至離形去智，剗其心而弗之有，佛老之學，人皆知其無所爲而不爲利也，而不知其近名近刑之戒，與夫出入死生之說，則固深乎利者矣。噫！利之爲利，夫人能言之；義之爲利，非喻於義者不能辨也。學者求至於聖人之道，當立志以爲先，持敬以爲本，反身而誠，以至於天下之事皆吾分內，而一毫不係乎人，則事皆無所爲而爲，天之所以與我者盡矣。故夫子有爲已爲人之說，孟子以舜跖之分在於利善之間。數百年來，未有盡發其旨者。張子以有爲無爲言之，深有以中俗學之病，𢃄其所以有功於聖門也。善乎，象山陸子有言曰：「古之君子喻人於義，小人喻於利；今之君子，其喻於義者，皆爲利而喻也。爲利而喻，非義矣。」聖賢之言，其互相發明者以此。
translation_en:
…Otherwise, the distinction between kingly and hegemonic rule, and the division between the gentleman and the petty man, are already plain for all to see and hear. Could they have awaited Master Zhang to elaborate what had not yet been expressed? To state the matter concisely and precisely, we see that what the world calls learning, from the sages onward, has never been without a purpose. Thus, as for roaming beyond the ordinary world, having no involvement in contemporary affairs, and even casting off bodily form, abandoning knowledge, and effacing the mind until one no longer possesses it—the learning of Buddhists and Daoists—everyone recognizes it as having no ulterior purpose and seeking no profit. Yet they fail to recognize that its warnings against approaching fame or punishment, together with its teachings about passing beyond life and death, are themselves deeply concerned with personal advantage.

Alas! Anyone can explain how profit constitutes personal advantage; only someone who understands righteousness can distinguish how righteousness may be turned to personal advantage. Those who study in pursuit of the Way of the sages should give first priority to establishing their resolve and take maintaining reverent attentiveness as their foundation. They should turn inward and become sincere, until they regard all affairs under Heaven as falling within their own responsibilities, without depending in the slightest on other people. Then everything they do will be done without ulterior purpose, and they will fully realize what Heaven has bestowed upon them.

Thus Confucius spoke of learning for oneself [?] and learning for others, while Mengzi located the distinction between Shun and the robber Zhi in the difference between pursuing advantage and pursuing goodness. For several hundred years, no one fully elucidated their meaning. Master Zhang explained it in terms of acting with and without ulterior purpose, striking deeply at the malady of conventional learning. This is presumably [?] how he rendered service to the school of the sages.

How well Master Lu of Xiangshan put it: “The gentlemen of antiquity enlightened others concerning righteousness, while petty men understood personal advantage. Among today’s gentlemen, those who understand righteousness all do so for the sake of advantage. Understanding it for the sake of advantage is not righteousness.” This is how the words of the sages and worthies illuminate one another.

title: 嘉靖四年江西鄉試錄
text:
同前　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　胡文宗
同考試官　教諭許　批　孔孟教人爲學無非辨義利
而已張子揭出無所爲一語尤見警切此作議論者貫徹
讀愈有滋味殆知潜心於聖學者故不厭其複而重録之
同考試官教諭朱　批　義利之論前賢屢發明之而
無所爲有所爲之詞至南軒而始撮其要是篇體認親切
而造語渾融讀之惟恐其竟也噫南軒發前賢之所未發
于殆發南軒之所未發者歟
===
考試官教授吳　批　論於無所爲處多欠親切此
篇明白痛快當是理學
考試官教授王　批　無所爲一言南軒平生精神
盡在於此且非平時見其意緒臨文豈容強合偶出此題
關係甚大宜其知言者寡矣連日閱卷明白剴切典則昌
徤無踰此篇參以前後二塲雄博之中亦隱隱足以自見
主司所以拭目者豈直以其文已耶
論曰君子之學始於辨幾終於爲聖人幾其起
于義利之間乎而所繇適於聖凡之路也學以
punctuated:
同前。胡文宗。

同考試官教諭許批：孔孟教人爲學，無非辨義利而已。張子揭出「無所爲」一語，尤見警切。此作議論者貫徹，讀愈有滋味，殆知潜心於聖學者，故不厭其複而重録之。

同考試官教諭朱批：義利之論，前賢屢發明之，而「無所爲」「有所爲」之詞，至南軒而始撮其要。是篇體認親切，而造語渾融，讀之惟恐其竟也。噫！南軒發前賢之所未發，于殆發南軒之所未發者歟？

考試官教授吳批：論於無所爲處，多欠親切。此篇明白痛快，當是理學。

考試官教授王批：「無所爲」一言，南軒平生精神盡在於此。且非平時見其意緒，臨文豈容強合？偶出此題，關係甚大，宜其知言者寡矣。連日閱卷，明白剴切，典則昌徤，無踰此篇。參以前後二塲，雄博之中，亦隱隱足以自見。主司所以拭目者，豈直以其文已耶？

論曰：君子之學，始於辨幾，終於爲聖人。幾，其起于義利之間乎？而所繇適於聖凡之路也。學以
translation_en:
Same topic as the preceding essay. By Hu Wenzong.

Comment by Associate Examiner Xu, Instructor: Confucius and Mencius, in teaching people to learn, did nothing other than distinguish righteousness from profit. Master Zhang’s formulation, “acting without an ulterior purpose,” is especially admonitory and incisive. This composition sustains its argument throughout [?]; the more one reads it, the richer its meaning becomes. Its author evidently knows how to devote himself to the learning of the sages. Thus, without objecting to the repetition, we have included another essay on this topic.

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhu, Instructor: Earlier worthies repeatedly elucidated the distinction between righteousness and profit, but only with Nanxuan was its essence first distilled into the expressions “acting without an ulterior purpose” and “acting with an ulterior purpose.” This essay displays an intimate grasp of the subject, and its language is thoroughly integrated and harmonious. Reading it, one fears only that it will end. Ah! Nanxuan brought out what earlier worthies had not brought out. Has this author [?] perhaps brought out what Nanxuan himself had not?

Comment by Examiner Wu, Professor: Discussions of acting without an ulterior purpose generally lack an intimate grasp of the matter. This essay is clear, incisive, and satisfying: surely this is the learning of principle.

Comment by Examiner Wang, Professor: Nanxuan’s lifelong intellectual spirit is fully contained in the single expression “acting without an ulterior purpose.” Unless one has already grasped its underlying meaning through regular study, how could one force an agreement with it when composing an essay? Though this topic happened to be set, its implications are very great; it is fitting that few understand its import. Among the scripts read over these past days, none surpasses this essay in clarity and incisiveness, classical propriety, and flourishing vigor. Considered alongside his work in the second and third sessions, the author’s qualities also subtly reveal themselves amid their grandeur and breadth. Is it merely his literary skill that makes the examiners look upon him with heightened attention?

The discourse reads: The gentleman’s learning begins with distinguishing the incipient stirrings of action and culminates in becoming a sage. Do these stirrings not arise at the dividing line between righteousness and profit? They are the route by which one proceeds toward sagehood or toward remaining an ordinary person. Learning, by …

title: 嘉靖四年江西鄉試錄
text:
義矣爲人而爲之斯爲利矣無所爲而爲之斯
爲己矣有所爲而爲之斯爲人矣至此則所謂
無所爲者不徒强仁慕義之事雖以一毫正助
之心而不敢有不徒富貴利達之謀雖以一毫
便適之意而不忍欺以此日存諸心亦不過即
其本心之明而不善未嘗不知知之未嘗復萌
理日以明則欲日以消義常在内則利常在外
以操其心則心可正以檢其身則身可脩推而
天下國家將無處而不當是之謂聖學是之謂
===
天德是之謂王道出乎此則五伯焉耳矣爲伯
之學者彼固知君子之爲美而非其所安也又
知小人之不爲美而不能不便其身圖也於此
亦足以見天理之未嘗亡而天幾之不容已也
由是遂辨而充之而義不可勝用矣特以其志
不至於義而至於利則非其末流之罪也昔者
子夏嘗學於夫子矣其言曰吾出見紛華富貴
而悅入聞夫子之道而樂二者心戰戰勝故肥
危矣哉子夏氏之幾乎王之所以王伯之所以
punctuated:
義矣。爲人而爲之，斯爲利矣；無所爲而爲之，斯爲己矣；有所爲而爲之，斯爲人矣。至此，則所謂無所爲者，不徒强仁慕義之事，雖以一毫正助之心而不敢有；不徒富貴利達之謀，雖以一毫便適之意而不忍欺。以此日存諸心，亦不過即其本心之明，而不善未嘗不知，知之未嘗復萌。理日以明，則欲日以消；義常在内，則利常在外。以操其心，則心可正；以檢其身，則身可脩。推而天下國家，將無處而不當。是之謂聖學，是之謂天德，是之謂王道。出乎此，則五伯焉耳矣。爲伯之學者，彼固知君子之爲美，而非其所安也；又知小人之不爲美，而不能不便其身圖也。於此亦足以見天理之未嘗亡，而天幾之不容已也。由是遂辨而充之，而義不可勝用矣。特以其志不至於義而至於利，則非其末流之罪也。
昔者，子夏嘗學於夫子矣。其言曰：「吾出見紛華富貴而悅，入聞夫子之道而樂。二者心戰，戰勝故肥。」危矣哉，子夏氏之幾乎！王之所以王，伯之所以
translation_en:
…is righteousness. To act for the sake of others’ regard is to pursue profit; to act without an ulterior purpose is to act for oneself; to act with an ulterior purpose is to act for others’ regard. At this point, what is called acting without an ulterior purpose means not merely refraining from efforts to force benevolence or aspire to righteousness: one dares not harbor even the slightest impulse to anticipate results or force their growth. It means not merely refraining from schemes for wealth, rank, profit, and advancement: one cannot bear to deceive oneself with even the slightest thought of personal ease. To preserve this daily in one’s heart is simply to follow the illumination of one’s original heart. One never fails to recognize what is bad, and once recognized, it never sprouts again. As principle grows clearer each day, desire diminishes each day. When righteousness is always within, profit remains without. By this one holds fast to the heart, and the heart can be rectified; by this one disciplines oneself, and the person can be cultivated. Extended to all under Heaven, the state, and the family, it will be fitting everywhere. This is called the learning of the sages, the virtue of Heaven, and the Way of the true king. Outside this, there is only the way of the Five Hegemons. Those who pursue the learning of hegemony certainly know that the gentleman’s conduct is admirable, yet they are not at ease with it. They also know that the petty man’s conduct is not admirable, yet cannot help pursuing schemes for their own advantage [?]. This suffices to show that Heaven’s principle has never perished and that its incipient stirrings cannot be suppressed. If they proceeded from this to distinguish and fully develop these stirrings, their righteousness would be inexhaustible in its application. But their resolve is directed toward profit rather than righteousness: the fault therefore does not lie merely in the later consequences.
In former times, Zixia studied under the Master. He said: “When I went out and saw splendor, wealth, and rank, I was delighted; when I entered and heard the Master’s Way, I rejoiced. The two fought within my heart. Once the battle was won, I grew stout.” How perilous was the critical juncture at which Zixia stood! What makes a king a true king, and what makes a hegemon…

title: 嘉靖四年江西鄉試錄
text:
伯決於此矣特以其志有足以勝之此所以爲
仲尼之徒也夫子嘗使門人言志矣他日又曰
吾十有五而志于學矣曰志於道矣夫惟志學
而後可以立可以不惑可以知天命可以耳順
可以不踰矩夫惟志道而後德可據仁可依藝
可游不有聖人之志而徒有聖人之學吾恐其
未有不爲爲人者而況於學非其所學者乎
表
擬宋以九經頒賜州縣學校及聚徒講誦
之所謝表〔咸平四年〕
===
江治
同考試官訓導吳　批〔駢儷之文至宋爲精此作深得宋體時出晉魏語以潤色之可謂寓奇於正者錄之〕
同考試官訓導張　批〔臣子感激之情溢於言外得謝表體〕
考試官教授吳　批〔豐贍嚴整〕
考試官教授王　批〔典雅〕
臣某等言咸平四年六月某日伏蒙
punctuated:
伯，決於此矣。特以其志有足以勝之，此所以爲仲尼之徒也。夫子嘗使門人言志矣，他日又曰：「吾十有五而志于學矣。」曰：「志於道矣。」夫惟志學，而後可以立，可以不惑，可以知天命，可以耳順，可以不踰矩。夫惟志道，而後德可據，仁可依，藝可游。不有聖人之志，而徒有聖人之學，吾恐其未有不爲爲人者，而況於學非其所學者乎？

表

擬宋以九經頒賜州縣學校及聚徒講誦之所謝表〔咸平四年〕

江治

同考試官訓導吳　批〔駢儷之文至宋爲精，此作深得宋體，時出晉魏語以潤色之，可謂寓奇於正者，錄之。〕

同考試官訓導張　批〔臣子感激之情溢於言外，得謝表體。〕

考試官教授吳　批〔豐贍嚴整。〕

考試官教授王　批〔典雅。〕

臣某等言：咸平四年六月某日，伏蒙
translation_en:
…to become a hegemon is decided at this point. It was only because his resolve sufficed to overcome this that he was a disciple of Zhongni [Confucius]. The Master once asked his disciples to state their aspirations. On another occasion he said, “At fifteen I set my heart on learning,” and also, “Set your heart on the Way.” Only after setting one’s heart on learning can one stand firm, be free from perplexity, understand Heaven’s mandate, have an ear attuned to truth, and act without overstepping the bounds. Only after setting one’s heart on the Way can one take virtue as one’s foundation, rely on benevolence, and find enjoyment in the arts. If one lacks the sage’s resolve and merely possesses the sage’s learning, I fear that one will invariably study for the approval of others. How much more so if what one studies is not even what the sage studied?

Memorial

A model memorial of thanks on the Song court’s bestowal of the Nine Classics upon prefectural and county schools and places where pupils gathered for lectures and recitation. 〔Fourth year of Xianping [1001].〕

By Jiang Zhi.

Comment by Associate Examiner Wu, Assistant Instructor: 〔Parallel prose attained refinement under the Song. This composition captures the Song style profoundly, occasionally introducing expressions from the Jin and Wei to embellish it. It may be said to lodge the unusual within the orthodox. Selected for inclusion.〕

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhang, Assistant Instructor: 〔The grateful emotion of a subject overflows beyond the words. It captures the proper form of a memorial of thanks.〕

Comment by Examiner Wu, Instructor: 〔Rich and ample, rigorous and orderly.〕

Comment by Examiner Wang, Instructor: 〔Classical and elegant.〕

Your servants, so-and-so and others, report: On a certain day of the sixth month of the fourth year of Xianping, we humbly received…

title: 嘉靖四年江西鄉試錄
text:
聖恩頒賜九經于州縣學校及聚徒講誦之所
者
伏以
大道顯天本九經以垂訓
聖王御極合四海以同文蓋致治莫大於崇儒
而敦本必先於正學顧玆
新渥廣若舊聞
離明發天下之蒙元始泄人心之賁含章義
著垂象文昭易闡幽微書紀政事養情性
===
無過三百篇之抑揚定是非不出十二公
之褒貶禮以正行樂以和心孝弟通於神
明語孟垂其典則人君無他途以成化學
者有正路以專門義既契於
聖
淵衷
恩遂施於海宇道明不夜政煥如春喜降福之
自天愧承
恩之無地玆蓋伏遇
punctuated:
聖恩頒賜九經于州縣學校及聚徒講誦之所者。

伏以，大道顯天，本九經以垂訓；聖王御極，合四海以同文。蓋致治莫大於崇儒，而敦本必先於正學。顧玆新渥，廣若舊聞。

離明發天下之蒙，元始泄人心之賁；含章義著，垂象文昭。《易》闡幽微，《書》紀政事；養情性，無過三百篇之抑揚；定是非，不出十二公之褒貶。禮以正行，樂以和心；孝弟通於神明，《語》《孟》垂其典則。人君無他途以成化，學者有正路以專門。義既契於聖淵衷，恩遂施於海宇。道明不夜，政煥如春。喜降福之自天，愧承恩之無地。玆蓋伏遇……
translation_en:
…Your Majesty’s sagely grace has bestowed the Nine Classics upon the prefectural and county schools and upon places where pupils gather for lectures and recitation.

We humbly reflect: the Great Way manifests Heaven, relying upon the Nine Classics to transmit its teachings; the sage king occupies the supreme throne, uniting all within the Four Seas in a common written culture. Nothing is greater for achieving good government than honoring Confucian learning, and strengthening the foundations must begin with rectifying learning. This new bounty is as far-reaching as the precedents known from antiquity.

The radiance of Li dispels the ignorance of all under Heaven; the primal beginning reveals the adornment of the human heart [?]. In containing patterned excellence, its meaning becomes manifest; in displaying images, its pattern shines forth. The Book of Changes elucidates the hidden and subtle; the Book of Documents records affairs of government. For nurturing feelings and character, nothing surpasses the modulations of the Three Hundred Odes; for determining right and wrong, nothing goes beyond the praise and blame apportioned under the twelve dukes in the Spring and Autumn Annals. Ritual corrects conduct; music harmonizes the heart. Filial piety and fraternal deference reach the spirits; the Analects and the Mencius transmit exemplary standards. Rulers have no other path by which to accomplish moral transformation, while students have a proper road toward mastery of a particular field. Since these principles accord with Your Majesty’s profound, sagely heart, grace has consequently been extended throughout the realm. The Way shines with a brightness that knows no night; government glows like spring. We rejoice that blessings descend from Heaven, yet feel ashamed that we have no means of requiting this grace. This is surely because we have humbly encountered…

title: 嘉靖四年江西鄉試錄
text:
堯仁廣運
舜德重華
則大居尊景緯耀三辰之珠璧
希聲應物文章宣六代之雲英畏天變而求
言志已勤於初政悲人窮而貸負心實發
於至誠縉紳仰
朝野之清明冠劍喜老成之登用以先王立
教固本之躬行而後學相師每陋於聞見
珍藏三萬軸恐非經濟之言積聚四十年
===
多涉詞章之見以茲傳習何補身心惟九
經具道德之真第諸儒無講解之素憐遐
方之東偏授借免宿學之禿筆手抄白鹿
茅山
寵既均於州縣嵩陽石鼓惠亦徹于生徒錦
軸牙籤光照黌宮之壁芸香蘗紙春輝雲
霧之窓山增高而水增深家可傳而人可
誦聖賢在目何須游市肆於洛陽德義入
心不必瞻星辰於東觀在昔覃粟帛之賜
punctuated: 堯仁廣運，舜德重華，則大居尊，景緯耀三辰之珠璧；希聲應物，文章宣六代之雲英。畏天變而求言，志已勤於初政；悲人窮而貸負，心實發於至誠。縉紳仰朝野之清明，冠劍喜老成之登用。以先王立教固本之躬行，而後學相師，每陋於聞見。珍藏三萬軸，恐非經濟之言；積聚四十年，多涉詞章之見。以茲傳習，何補身心？惟九經具道德之真，第諸儒無講解之素。憐遐方之東偏授借，免宿學之禿筆手抄。白鹿、茅山，寵既均於州縣；嵩陽、石鼓，惠亦徹于生徒。錦軸牙籤，光照黌宮之壁；芸香蘗紙，春輝雲霧之窓。山增高而水增深，家可傳而人可誦。聖賢在目，何須游市肆於洛陽？德義入心，不必瞻星辰於東觀。在昔覃粟帛之賜，
translation_en:
…Your benevolence, like Yao’s, extends everywhere; your virtue, like Shun’s, renews his resplendence. Taking Heaven’s greatness as your model, you occupy the exalted position: the celestial lights shine like the pearls and jade discs of sun, moon, and stars. With the rarefied sound of supreme harmony, you respond to all things; your cultural brilliance proclaims the music of the Six Dynasties, the Cloud Gate and the Six Flowers. In awe of Heaven’s portents, you solicit counsel, your resolve already diligent at the beginning of your reign. Pitying the people’s destitution, you remit their debts, moved by utter sincerity. Officials look up to the clarity and good order of court and country; those wearing official caps and swords rejoice that seasoned men have been appointed to office.

The former kings established instruction and strengthened its foundations through personal practice; yet later scholars, teaching one another, are often confined by their limited learning. Even a treasured collection of thirty thousand scrolls may contain little counsel for ordering the realm and aiding the people; learning accumulated over forty years may largely concern literary composition. What benefit to one’s person and mind comes from transmitting and studying such things? Only the Nine Classics contain the truth of the Way and virtue, yet scholars lack an established grounding in their exposition. Taking pity on the remote eastern region, you have provided books for its use [?], sparing veteran scholars the labor of copying them by hand with worn-out brushes. At Bailu and Maoshan, your favor has already been bestowed equally upon prefectures and counties; at Songyang and Shigu, your bounty likewise reaches the students. Brocade-wrapped scrolls and ivory labels cast their radiance upon the school walls; rue-scented books and paper treated with cork-tree bark bring springtime brilliance to windows amid clouds and mist. Mountains gain in height and waters in depth; every household can transmit these texts, and everyone can recite them. With sages and worthies before our eyes, why need we wander the bookstalls of Luoyang? With virtue and righteousness entering our hearts, we need not gaze upon the stars at the Eastern Library. In former times, when gifts of grain and silk were widely bestowed…

title: 嘉靖四年江西鄉試錄
text:
不過溫飽其身惟玆泳道德之波實乃漸
摩其性措之而治家治國共傳萬世之良
方蘊之而爲聖爲賢永拜
九重之天爵臣等業同學究志戀書巢
寵無干於甘露石渠心自省於蒲輪符節辣
粃羞稱乎野外聲音不取於河間上法天
經遠陋漢儒之姤下敦地義近刋唐集之
訛勉焉以半部致太平誤矣衷七篇爲權
變求無慚於一字幸自奮於三餘伏願
===
濬德乃文
嘉言必史帝王之治純於道旣廣其說以爲
公君子之道本諸身必體其實以爲政
事疏通而志精潔
履中正而樂和平絃歌無鄭衛之音左右屛
讒邪之迹至德微言之允著仁義王道之
皆聞郡邑聚徒之區必有淹九經而出者
廟堂論道之地行將擬三代而用之道旣尊
於
punctuated:
不過溫飽其身，惟玆泳道德之波，實乃漸摩其性。措之而治家治國，共傳萬世之良方；蘊之而爲聖爲賢，永拜九重之天爵。臣等業同學究，志戀書巢，寵無干於甘露石渠，心自省於蒲輪符節。辣粃羞稱乎野外，聲音不取於河間。上法天經，遠陋漢儒之姤；下敦地義，近刋唐集之訛。勉焉以半部致太平，誤矣衷七篇爲權變。求無慚於一字，幸自奮於三餘。
伏願濬德乃文，嘉言必史。帝王之治純於道，旣廣其說以爲公；君子之道本諸身，必體其實以爲政。事疏通而志精潔，履中正而樂和平。絃歌無鄭衛之音，左右屛讒邪之迹。至德微言之允著，仁義王道之皆聞。郡邑聚徒之區，必有淹九經而出者；廟堂論道之地，行將擬三代而用之。道旣尊於
translation_en:
…merely warmed and fed their bodies. But now, bathing in the waves of the Way and virtue truly nurtures their nature. Put into practice in governing families and the state, these teachings will be transmitted by all as excellent prescriptions for ten thousand generations; treasured within, they enable one to become a sage or worthy, forever gratefully receiving Heaven’s nobility bestowed from the imperial heights. We, your servants, pursue the same occupation as scholars and set our hearts upon our nests of books. We do not seek the favor accorded at the Ganlu and Shiqu scholarly assemblies; we examine our own hearts when faced with summons conveyed by rush-cushioned carriages and credentials of office. Ashamed to be called ‘pungent chaff’ [?] in the countryside, we do not seek recognition for our voices in Hejian [?]. Above, we take Heaven’s constant order as our model, rejecting as unworthy the errors [?] of Han scholars of long ago; below, we uphold Earth’s proper order, correcting the more recent errors in Tang collections. We strive to bring about Great Peace with half a book; it is mistaken to regard the seven books as a source of expedient stratagems [?]. We seek to feel no shame over even a single character and hope to exert ourselves during the ‘three spare times’ for study.
We humbly wish that Your Majesty’s profound virtue may shine forth in cultured brilliance, and that your excellent words may invariably be recorded by the historians. The government of emperors and kings is grounded purely in the Way: having disseminated its teachings widely for the common good, one must recognize that the gentleman’s Way is rooted in his own person and embody its substance in governing. May your conduct be discerning and your intentions pure; may you tread the path of centrality and rectitude and delight in peace and harmony. May music and song be free of the sounds of Zheng and Wei, and may every trace of slander and wickedness be banished from your attendants. May the subtle words concerning consummate virtue be truly made manifest, and may benevolence, righteousness, and the kingly Way be heard by all. From the places where students gather in prefectures and counties, there will surely emerge men deeply versed in the Nine Classics; in the court where the Way is discussed, they will soon be employed in emulation of the Three Dynasties. Comment by Associate Examiner Ma, Instructor: Our dynasty’s rites honoring and sacrificing to the First Teacher [Confucius] embody the transmitted teachings of the ancient sage emperors and kings concerning the mind. title: 嘉靖四年江西鄉試錄
text:
聖化而有得者歟〻〻
同考試官教諭潘　批
聖製策目塲屋累科有之士子援引傳文往往答非所問未有真切如此作者録之
考試官教授吳　批
朝崇儒之意明備子之學可謂識其大者　鋪叙我
考試官教授王　批
朝文明之治首見於此以此策士固宜塲中往往有不知誰之爲之者雖足以見　我
王道之大而非所望於士也此策義理精詳竊窺
===
聖學文辭深厚取法
聖謨化成之久宜有斯士哉
對知
聖人之政先於崇天下之大禮當知
聖人之心在於繼千載之絶學求其學可以知
其心矣得其心可以知其禮矣見其禮可
以知其政矣由是言之則知表章聖道者
天下之大政王祀夫子者天下之大禮禮
以心行心以學正而吾夫子固學之的也
punctuated:
聖化而有得者歟〻〻。

同考試官教諭潘批：聖製策目，塲屋累科有之。士子援引傳文，往往答非所問，未有真切如此作者，録之。

考試官教授吳批：朝崇儒之意明備，子之學可謂識其大者。鋪叙我。

考試官教授王批：朝文明之治首見於此，以此策士固宜。塲中往往有不知誰之爲之者，雖足以見我王道之大，而非所望於士也。此策義理精詳，竊窺聖學；文辭深厚，取法聖謨。化成之久，宜有斯士哉！

對：知聖人之政先於崇天下之大禮，當知聖人之心在於繼千載之絶學。求其學，可以知其心矣；得其心，可以知其禮矣；見其禮，可以知其政矣。由是言之，則知表章聖道者，天下之大政；王祀夫子者，天下之大禮。禮以心行，心以學正，而吾夫子固學之的也。
translation_en:
…has gained something from the sage’s transforming influence?

Comment by Associate Examiner Pan, Instructor: Policy questions composed by the Emperor have appeared in successive examinations. Candidates cite passages from the commentaries, yet their answers often fail to address the question. There has never been an essay as pertinent and earnest as this one. Include it in the record.

Comment by Examiner Wu, Professor: [The wording appears displaced here.] The essay fully and clearly expounds our dynasty’s intention to honor Confucian learning [?]. Your learning may be said to grasp what is fundamental.

Comment by Examiner Wang, Professor: Our dynasty’s enlightened governance is manifested foremost in this matter; it is certainly fitting to examine candidates through it. In the examination hall there are often those who do not know who has brought this about. Although this suffices to show the greatness of our kingly Way, it is not what we expect of scholars. This policy essay treats moral principles with precision and thoroughness, venturing a glimpse into imperial sagely learning; its language is profound and substantial, taking the Emperor’s sagely counsels as its model. After so long a period of transforming instruction, surely such a scholar should emerge!

Reply: To know that the sage’s governance gives priority to honoring the great rites of the realm, one should understand that the sage’s purpose lies in carrying forward the learning whose transmission has been interrupted for a thousand years. By investigating his learning, one may understand his heart; by grasping his heart, one may understand his rites; by observing his rites, one may understand his governance. From this perspective, we know that making manifest the Way of the sages is a great undertaking of government throughout the realm, and that the sovereign’s sacrifices to the Master are a great rite of the realm. Rites are carried out through the heart, and the heart is rectified through learning; our Master is indeed the standard of learning.

title: 嘉靖四年江西鄉試錄
text:
學官成其後也須賜經籍至其文也作養
士類敎其敎也
聖祖之武功告成即興文教者此也
文皇之纘承大統至法成憲者亦此也是之謂
大政而名實舉矣是之謂大禮而情文備
矣非心聖人之心不能有是禮非學聖人
之學不能有是心且
祖宗之論學者多矣而其大本不外乎一心論
心者多矣而其大要不外乎大學惟我
===
聖祖書而揭之廡壁謂宋濂曰朕之為君上畏
天地下畏兆民兢兢業業不敢自逸即吾
孔子誠意正心之功也惟我
文皇舉而證諸堯典謂楊士奇曰帝王之學貴
切已實用講說之際一切浮汎無益之語
勿用即
聖祖表章大學之心也是學也
文皇得之
聖祖
punctuated:
學官，成其後也；須賜經籍，至其文也；作養士類，敎其敎也。聖祖之武功告成，即興文教者，此也；文皇之纘承大統，至法成憲者，亦此也。是之謂大政而名實舉矣，是之謂大禮而情文備矣。非心聖人之心，不能有是禮；非學聖人之學，不能有是心。且祖宗之論學者多矣，而其大本不外乎一心；論心者多矣，而其大要不外乎大學。
惟我聖祖書而揭之廡壁，謂宋濂曰：「朕之為君，上畏天地，下畏兆民，兢兢業業，不敢自逸，即吾孔子誠意正心之功也。」惟我文皇舉而證諸堯典，謂楊士奇曰：「帝王之學，貴切已實用。講說之際，一切浮汎無益之語勿用。」即聖祖表章大學之心也。是學也，文皇得之聖祖；
translation_en:
…educational officials, bringing its subsequent development to completion [?]; bestowing canonical texts, bringing its literary refinement to the utmost [?]; nurturing scholars, teaching them what should be taught. This is why the Sagely Progenitor, once his military achievements were accomplished, immediately promoted civil learning and moral instruction. This is also why Emperor Wen, upon succeeding to the imperial throne, took established statutes as his model [?]. This is what is called great governance, in which both name and substance are fully realized; this is what is called great ritual, in which both feeling and outward form are complete. Unless one takes the sage’s mind as one’s own, one cannot possess such ritual; unless one studies what the sage studied, one cannot possess such a mind. Moreover, our ancestral emperors spoke much about learning, yet its great foundation lay entirely in the mind. They spoke much about the mind, yet its essentials lay entirely in the Great Learning.
Our Sagely Progenitor wrote this out and displayed it on the wall of a covered gallery. He told Song Lian: “As ruler, above I stand in awe of Heaven and Earth; below I stand in awe of the multitude of the people. Vigilant and diligent, I dare not indulge myself in ease. This is precisely the work of making the intentions sincere and rectifying the mind taught by our Confucius.” Our Emperor Wen invoked it and corroborated it through the Canon of Yao. He told Yang Shiqi: “In the learning of emperors and kings, what matters is its direct bearing on oneself and its practical application. In lectures and discussions, employ none of those superficial, diffuse, and useless words.” This was precisely the intention with which the Sagely Progenitor had given prominence to the Great Learning. This learning Emperor Wen received from the Sagely Progenitor; …

title: 嘉靖四年江西鄉試錄
text:
聖祖得之孔子孔子得之文武周公文武周公
得之堯舜禹湯堯舜禹湯得之羲農黃帝
羲農黃帝得之天愚又何足以知之亦嘗
竊取我
文皇之意而知之矣於此有以見我
祖宗之學其體則格物致知誠意正心脩身其
用則齊家治國平天下是以
聖神相繼而禮樂大行
君師兼隆而聲教四訖雖唐虞三代之治何以
加諸彼漢高祖過魯之祀未幾而溲溺之
風無改唐太宗先聖之褒雖美而躬行之
德尚虧宋太祖孔顏之贊雖隆而作興之
典多缺惟其心僞而不誠故其禮得其文
而不得其本政有其名而無其實而所謂
學者固不足言矣執事所謂即儀文之詳
畧不同而治化必不如是之相懸者豈非
有見于其大哉雖然言及之不可以不復
也
punctuated: 聖祖得之孔子，孔子得之文武周公，文武周公得之堯舜禹湯，堯舜禹湯得之羲農黃帝，羲農黃帝得之天。愚又何足以知之？亦嘗竊取我文皇之意而知之矣。於此有以見我祖宗之學，其體則格物、致知、誠意、正心、脩身，其用則齊家、治國、平天下。是以聖神相繼而禮樂大行，君師兼隆而聲教四訖，雖唐虞三代之治，何以加諸？彼漢高祖過魯之祀，未幾而溲溺之風無改；唐太宗先聖之褒雖美，而躬行之德尚虧；宋太祖孔顏之贊雖隆，而作興之典多缺。惟其心僞而不誠，故其禮得其文而不得其本，政有其名而無其實，而所謂學者固不足言矣。執事所謂即儀文之詳畧不同，而治化必不如是之相懸者，豈非有見于其大哉？雖然，言及之，不可以不復也。
translation_en:
…The Sagely Founder received it from Kongzi; Kongzi received it from Kings Wen and Wu and the Duke of Zhou; Kings Wen and Wu and the Duke of Zhou received it from Yao, Shun, Yu, and Tang; Yao, Shun, Yu, and Tang received it from Fuxi, Shennong, and the Yellow Emperor; and Fuxi, Shennong, and the Yellow Emperor received it from Heaven. How could someone as unworthy as I be capable of understanding it? Yet I have ventured to draw upon the intent of our Emperor Wen and thereby come to understand it. Here we can discern the learning of our imperial ancestors: its substance consists in investigating things, extending knowledge, making the intentions sincere, rectifying the mind, and cultivating oneself; its application consists in regulating the family, governing the state, and bringing peace to all under Heaven. Thus sage and divinely enlightened sovereigns succeeded one another, and rites and music flourished widely. The roles of ruler and teacher were both exalted, and their civilizing influence reached the four corners of the realm. How could even the government of Yao and Shun and the Three Dynasties surpass this?

As for Han Gaozu’s sacrifice when passing through Lu, scarcely any time had elapsed, yet his habit of urinating in scholars’ caps remained unchanged. Tang Taizong’s praise of the Former Sage was admirable, yet his virtue in personal conduct remained deficient. Song Taizu’s praise of Kongzi and Yan Hui was exalted, yet the institutions for promoting learning were largely wanting. Precisely because their hearts were false and insincere, their rites attained the outward forms but not the foundation, and their government possessed the name but not the substance. Their supposed learning was certainly not worth discussing.

You, sir, have said that, even if ceremonial forms differed in elaborateness or simplicity, the effects of government and moral transformation should surely not have been so far apart. Does this not show that you have perceived what is fundamental? Nevertheless, since the matter has been raised, I cannot leave it without a further reply.

title: 嘉靖四年江西鄉試錄
text:
國初南都之塑像乃元人之俗而我
聖祖毅然去之其功偉矣彼大成之稱獨非元
之所加者與此愚之未解一也今京師之
太學亦元人之舊而我
文皇因之不改其義深矣彼
聖祖之華獨非義之至當者歟此愚之未解二
也嘗觀吾孔子之作春秋也内夏外夷不
遺餘力而鞀鞬亂華又古今所無之變其
一時君臣誣罔矯偽之禮愚恐聖人在天
===
之靈必所不屑也執事所謂
聖人之用意有非恒情之所易窺愚則以為
祖宗一時慎重之意當如此爾乃今百有五十
餘年于茲矣
聖天子在上賢公卿在下苟有以
聞豈無主張斯議以為吾道之一快乎此非愚
之狂也固薦紳之議也惟進而折衷之謹
對
第二問
punctuated:
國初，南都之塑像乃元人之俗，而我聖祖毅然去之，其功偉矣。彼大成之稱，獨非元之所加者與？此愚之未解一也。今京師之太學亦元人之舊，而我文皇因之不改，其義深矣。彼聖祖之華，獨非義之至當者歟？此愚之未解二也。嘗觀吾孔子之作《春秋》也，内夏外夷，不遺餘力，而鞀鞬亂華，又古今所無之變。其一時君臣誣罔矯偽之禮，愚恐聖人在天之靈必所不屑也。執事所謂「聖人之用意，有非恒情之所易窺」，愚則以為祖宗一時慎重之意當如此爾。乃今百有五十餘年于茲矣。聖天子在上，賢公卿在下，苟有以聞，豈無主張斯議，以為吾道之一快乎？此非愚之狂也，固薦紳之議也。惟進而折衷之。謹對。

第二問
translation_en:
At the beginning of our dynasty, the sculpted images in the Southern Capital, Nanjing, were a custom inherited from the Yuan. Our Sagely Progenitor resolutely removed them: great indeed was his achievement. Yet was not the designation “Great Perfection” likewise conferred under the Yuan? This is the first point that I, in my ignorance, cannot understand. The Imperial University in the present capital likewise survives from the Yuan, yet our Emperor Wen retained it unchanged: his reasons were profound indeed. Yet were not the Chinese forms of the Sagely Progenitor [?] supremely appropriate in principle? This is the second point that I cannot understand.

I have observed that when our Confucius composed the Spring and Autumn Annals, he spared no effort to treat the Chinese states as insiders and the foreign peoples as outsiders. Yet drums and bow-cases bringing disorder to Chinese civilization [?] constituted a calamity unprecedented in any age. I fear that the sage’s spirit in Heaven must have disdained the deceptive and counterfeit rites of the ruler and ministers of that time. You say that “the sage’s intentions are not always readily fathomed by ordinary understanding.” I would take this simply to mean that the founding emperors had reasons for proceeding cautiously under the circumstances of their time.

But more than one hundred and fifty years have now passed. With a sagely Son of Heaven above and worthy high ministers below, if someone brought the matter to his attention, would there not be someone to champion this proposal and thereby give satisfaction to those who uphold our Way? This is no wild assertion of mine; it is indeed a proposal discussed among officials. I ask only that you advance it and arrive at a considered judgment. Respectfully submitted in reply.

Second Question

title: 嘉靖四年江西鄉試錄
text:
江治
同考試官訓導吳批以體用偏全發明政學且能
詳擧古人而評隲之必知學而可達於政者也
同考試官訓導張批策士以政學欲觀所養故不
以隱僻之說相困子能探本窮源據經斷史灼有定見學已
至此何有於政耶
考試官教授吳批問目所及士子類能言之至
於援引該博文勢舂容無踰子者
考試官教授王批議論精當故實不遺可以驗
===
===
博古之學矣
對天下未嘗有無體之用也唯其偏全之
分已矣亦未嘗有無用之體也惟其難易
之時已矣是故觀天下之用者存乎體體
有偏全而用之小大隨之世豈有無體之
用哉論天下之體者存乎時時有難易而
體之通塞繫之世豈有無用之體哉觀此
則知吾儒內外合一之學體用相須之妙
而執事政學不同之問亦可得而復矣夫
